# eai types

## Synopsis

```
eai types <subcommand> [options]
```

## Description

`eai types` manages Object Type definitions for your vertical application. Object Types are the schema definitions that describe your data model -- they define properties, relationship links, actions, side effects, and access roles.

Type definitions live in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` and are organized by tenant key. Each tenant key maps to an array of Object Type definitions.

This command must be run from within an EAI project directory.

## Subcommands

### eai types validate

Check Object Type definitions against platform schema rules. Validates naming conventions, property types, link cardinality, action roles, and side effect references.

```
eai types validate
```

Validation rules include:

- Type names must be PascalCase
- A `displayName` is required
- Status must be `draft`, `published`, or `deprecated`
- Property names must be unique within a type
- Property types must be one of: `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `select`, `json`, `file`, `relationship`
- Select properties must have an `options` array
- Link cardinality must be: `one-to-one`, `one-to-many`, `many-to-one`, or `many-to-many`
- Action roles must be: `tenant-user`, `tenant-staff`, or `tenant-admin`
- Side effect types must be: `set_field`, `set_timestamp`, or `set_user`

### eai types seed

Push local Object Type definitions to the platform. Creates new types or updates existing ones based on name matching within each tenant scope.

```
eai types seed [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--env <environment>` | Target environment | `dev` |
| `--tenant-key <key>` | Seed a specific tenant key only (from object-types.ts) | All tenant keys |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be seeded without making changes | `false` |

### eai types diff

Compare local Object Type definitions with what is currently published on the platform. Shows which types and properties are local-only, remote-only, or changed.

```
eai types diff
```

### eai types pull

Download remote Object Types from the platform and generate a local TypeScript file. Useful for syncing changes made through other tools back to your local definitions.

```
eai types pull [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--tenant-id <id>` | Platform tenant ID to pull from | Resolved from environment |
| `--output <path>` | Output file path | `src/eai.config/object-types.generated.ts` |

### eai types define

Interactive Object Type builder (planned for a future release).

```
eai types define
```

## Examples

### Validate Object Types

```bash
eai types validate
```

```
⠋ Loading Object Types...
✔ Loaded Object Types

Tenant: patient-intake
✔ Patient — 8 props, 1 links, 2 actions
✔ Document — 4 props, 0 links, 0 actions

✔ All Object Types are valid
```

### Validate with errors

```bash
eai types validate
```

```
⠋ Loading Object Types...
✔ Loaded Object Types

Tenant: patient-intake
✖ patient
    error: name "patient" must be PascalCase
    error: select property "status" must have options
⚠ Document
    warn: property "tags" has options but type is "text" (not select)

✖ 2 error(s), 1 warning(s)
```

### Seed types to platform

```bash
eai types seed
```

```
⠋ Loading Object Types...
✔ Found 3 types across 1 tenant scope(s): patient-intake

Tenant: patient-intake → 8f3a1b2c-...
  ✔ Patient (created)
  ✔ Document (created)
  ✔ Appointment (updated)

```

### Dry-run seed

```bash

```

```

✔ Found 3 types across 1 tenant scope(s): patient-intake

Tenant: patient-intake → 8f3a1b2c-...
  Patient — 8 props, 1 links, 2 actions

```

### Seed a specific tenant key

```bash

```

### Diff local vs remote

```bash

```

```

✔ Loaded local types

  ⠋ Fetching remote types...

  = Document — no differences
  ~ Appointment
    + property: notes (local only)

    = 4 properties unchanged
```

### Pull remote types to local

```bash
eai types pull
```

```
⠋ Fetching remote Object Types...
✔ Found 3 remote types

✔ Written to src/eai.config/object-types.generated.ts
ℹ Review the generated file and merge into object-types.ts
```

### Pull to a custom output path

```bash
eai types pull --output src/eai.config/remote-types.ts
```

## Related Commands

- [`eai verify`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/verify/) -- check that local Object Types are loadable

# eai resources

## Synopsis

```
eai resources <subcommand> [options]
```

## Description

`eai resources` provides full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations on platform resources. Resources are instances of Object Types -- the data records that your vertical application manages.

All subcommands require `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and at least one `TENANT_*_ID` to be set in `.env.local` or the environment. The tenant ID is resolved from environment variables automatically.

This command must be run from within an EAI project directory.

## Subcommands

### eai resources list

List resources of a given Object Type with pagination and sorting.

```
eai resources list <type> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<type>` | Object Type name (e.g., `Patient`, `Document`) | Required |
| `--page <n>` | Page number | `1` |
| `--limit <n>` | Items per page | `20` |
| `--sort <field>` | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending. | `-created_at` |
| `--json` | Output raw JSON | `false` |

### eai resources get

Retrieve a single resource by type and ID.

```
eai resources get <type> <id> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<type>` | Object Type name | Required |
| `<id>` | Resource ID | Required |
| `--json` | Output raw JSON | `false` |

### eai resources create

Create a new resource. Provide data as an inline JSON string or from a file.

```
eai resources create <type> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<type>` | Object Type name | Required |
| `--data <json>` | Resource data as a JSON string | -- |
| `--file <path>` | Read resource data from a JSON file | -- |

One of `--data` or `--file` is required.

### eai resources update

Update an existing resource. The CLI automatically fetches the current version for optimistic locking if `--version` is not provided.

```
eai resources update <type> <id> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<type>` | Object Type name | Required |
| `<id>` | Resource ID | Required |
| `--data <json>` | Updated fields as a JSON string | Required |
| `--version <n>` | Resource version for optimistic locking. Auto-fetched if omitted. | Auto |

### eai resources delete

Delete a resource. Prompts for confirmation unless `--force` is set.

```
eai resources delete <type> <id> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<type>` | Object Type name | Required |
| `<id>` | Resource ID | Required |
| `--force` | Skip confirmation prompt | `false` |

### eai resources query

Run a cross-type query across multiple Object Types with filter conditions.

```
eai resources query [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--types <types>` | Comma-separated Object Type names | Required |
| `--where <json>` | Filter conditions as a JSON string | -- |
| `--limit <n>` | Maximum number of results | `20` |
| `--json` | Output raw JSON | `false` |

### eai resources schema

Show the published Object Types for the current tenant. Displays property, link, and action counts for each type.

```
eai resources schema
```

## Examples

### List resources

```bash
eai resources list Patient
```

```
⠋ Listing Patient...
✔ 42 total — page 1/3
  8f3a1b2c title=Jane Doe, status=in-progress, priority=2
  a7c9e4d1 title=John Smith, status=draft, priority=0
  b2d8f6e3 title=Maria Garcia, status=complete, priority=1
  ...
```

### List with pagination and sorting

```bash
eai resources list Patient --page 2 --limit 10 --sort -priority
```

```bash
eai resources list Patient --json
```

```json
    {
      "id": "8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",

        "priority": 2
      },
```

```bash

```

```json

  "id": "8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",

    "title": "Jane Doe",

    "isActive": true,

  "created_at": "2026-03-01T10:30:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-05T14:15:00Z"

```

### Create a resource with inline data

```bash
eai resources create Patient --data '{"title": "New Patient", "status": "draft", "isActive": true}'
```

```

```

### Create a resource from a file

```bash
eai resources create Patient --file ./data/patient.json
```

### Update a resource

```bash
eai resources update Patient 8f3a1b2c --data '{"priority": 3, "status": "in-progress"}'
```

```

✔ Updated Patient 8f3a1b2c-...
```

### Update with explicit version

```bash

```

### Delete a resource

```bash

```

```
  "results": [
```

### View published schema


```
⠋ Fetching schema...
✔ 3 published types
  Patient — 8 props, 1 links, 2 actions
  Document — 4 props, 0 links, 0 actions
  Appointment — 5 props, 2 links, 1 actions
```

## Related Commands

- [`eai types`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/types/) -- manage Object Type definitions (schema)
- [`eai chat`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/chat/) -- interact with AI workflows
- [`eai docs`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/docs/) -- upload and manage documents

# eai tenant

## Synopsis

```
eai tenant <subcommand> [options]
```

## Description

`eai tenant` manages tenants on the EAI platform. Tenants are organizational boundaries that isolate data and configuration. A vertical application is scoped to one or more tenants, and all resources, Object Types, and workflows operate within a tenant context.

Tenants can be organized hierarchically with parent-child relationships. The `list` subcommand is scoped to a parent tenant when specified.

This command must be run from within an EAI project directory and requires `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` to be set.

## Subcommands

### eai tenant list

List tenants, optionally scoped to a parent tenant.

```
eai tenant list [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--parent <id>` | Parent tenant ID to scope the listing | -- (lists all accessible) |
| `--json` | Output raw JSON | `false` |

### eai tenant info

Show detailed information about a specific tenant.

```
eai tenant info <id>
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<id>` | Tenant ID to inspect | Required |

### eai tenant create

Create a new tenant on the platform.

```
eai tenant create [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--name <name>` | Tenant name (required) | Required |
| `--slug <slug>` | Tenant slug in kebab-case (required) | Required |
| `--parent <id>` | Parent tenant ID for hierarchical tenants | -- |
| `--domain <domains>` | Comma-separated list of associated domains | -- |

## Examples

### List all tenants

```bash
eai tenant list
```

```
⠋ Fetching tenants...
✔ 3 tenants
  patient-intake 8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
    domains: intake.myenterprise.ai
  claims-portal a7c9e4d1-b2c3-4567-89ab-cdef01234567
    domains: claims.myenterprise.ai
  admin-hub b2d8f6e3-c4d5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
```

### List tenants under a parent

```bash
eai tenant list --parent 8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
```

### List as JSON

```bash
eai tenant list --json
```

```json
{
  "docs": [
    {
      "id": "8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
      "name": "Patient Intake",
      "slug": "patient-intake",
      "domain": ["intake.myenterprise.ai"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Inspect a tenant

```bash
eai tenant info 8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
```

```
⠋ Fetching tenant...
✔ Tenant: Patient Intake
{
  "id": "8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
  "name": "Patient Intake",
  "slug": "patient-intake",
  "domain": ["intake.myenterprise.ai"],
  "parent": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-01-15T08:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-02-20T12:30:00Z"
}
```

### Create a tenant

```bash
eai tenant create --name "Claims Portal" --slug claims-portal --domain claims.myenterprise.ai
```

```
⠋ Creating tenant "Claims Portal"...
✔ Created tenant claims-portal (a7c9e4d1-...)
```

### Create a child tenant

```bash
eai tenant create \
  --name "Claims Staff" \
  --slug claims-staff \
  --parent a7c9e4d1-b2c3-4567-89ab-cdef01234567
```

### Create a tenant with multiple domains

```bash
eai tenant create \
  --name "Multi-Region Portal" \
  --slug multi-region \
  --domain portal-us.example.com,portal-eu.example.com
```

## Related Commands

- [`eai whoami`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/whoami/) -- show current tenant context
- [`eai types seed`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/types/) -- seed Object Types to a specific tenant
- [`eai resources`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/resources/) -- manage resources within a tenant

# eai chat

## Synopsis

```
eai chat <subcommand> <message> [options]
```

## Description

`eai chat` interacts with AI workflows on the EAI platform. You can send single messages and receive a complete response, or stream a conversation using Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time output.

Each chat message is associated with a workflow, a stage within that workflow, and a conversation ID. The conversation ID allows you to continue a multi-turn conversation across multiple commands.

This command requires `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and a tenant ID to be set in `.env.local` or the environment.

## Subcommands

### eai chat send

Send a single message and receive the full response at once.

```
eai chat send <message> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<message>` | The message to send | Required |
| `--workflow <id>` | Workflow ID (required) | Required |
| `--stage <stage>` | Chat stage within the workflow | `chat` |
| `--conversation <id>` | Conversation ID for multi-turn conversations. Auto-generated if omitted. | Auto-generated UUID |

### eai chat stream

Stream a conversation in real-time using SSE. Tokens are printed to stdout as they arrive.

```
eai chat stream <message> [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<message>` | The initial message to send | Required |
| `--workflow <id>` | Workflow ID (required) | Required |
| `--stage <stage>` | Chat stage within the workflow | `chat` |
| `--conversation <id>` | Conversation ID for multi-turn conversations. Auto-generated if omitted. | Auto-generated UUID |

## Examples

### Send a single message

```bash
eai chat send "What documents are required for a new patient intake?" \
  --workflow wf-abc-123
```

```
ℹ Conversation: 7e2a4f6b-c8d9-4321-abcd-ef0123456789

{
  "response": "For a new patient intake, the following documents are typically required:\n\n1. Photo ID (driver's license or passport)\n2. Insurance card (front and back)\n3. Completed patient registration form\n4. Medical history questionnaire\n5. Signed consent forms",
  "conversationId": "7e2a4f6b-c8d9-4321-abcd-ef0123456789",
  "stage": "chat"
}
```

### Stream a conversation

```bash
eai chat stream "Summarize the latest claims for region West" \
  --workflow wf-claims-456
```

```
ℹ Streaming conversation: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890

Based on the latest data, here are the claims for the West region:

1. **Claim #W-2024-001** — $12,500 — Status: Under Review
   Filed by: Acme Corp on March 1, 2026

2. **Claim #W-2024-002** — $8,200 — Status: Approved
   Filed by: Widget Inc on February 28, 2026

3. **Claim #W-2024-003** — $45,000 — Status: Pending Documentation
   Filed by: GlobalTech on February 25, 2026

Total claims value: $65,700 across 3 active claims.

✔ Stream complete
```

### Continue an existing conversation

```bash
eai chat send "Tell me more about claim W-2024-003" \
  --workflow wf-claims-456 \
  --conversation a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
```

### Use a specific stage

```bash
eai chat stream "Generate a summary report" \
  --workflow wf-reports-789 \
  --stage report-generation
```

### Pipe the response for downstream processing

```bash
eai chat send "List all overdue tasks as JSON" \
  --workflow wf-tasks-101 | jq '.response'
```

## Workflow and Stage

- **Workflow**: Identifies the AI configuration to use (model, system prompt, tools, RAG settings). Workflow IDs are provisioned on the platform and stored in your `.env.local` as `WORKFLOW_*_ID`.
- **Stage**: A named phase within a workflow. The default stage is `chat`. Other stages might include `triage`, `classification`, `report-generation`, etc.
- **Conversation ID**: Groups messages into a single conversation context. The AI retains memory of previous messages within the same conversation ID.

## Related Commands

- [`eai docs`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/docs/) -- upload and index documents for RAG-powered chat
- [`eai resources`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/resources/) -- manage the data that AI workflows operate on
- [`eai whoami`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/whoami/) -- verify auth and workflow configuration

---

# eai docs

## Synopsis

```
eai docs <subcommand> <argument> [options]
```

## Description

`eai docs` manages documents on the EAI platform. You can upload files, run AI-powered classification to automatically categorize documents, and index them for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) so they become searchable by AI chat workflows.

This command requires `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and a tenant ID to be set in `.env.local` or the environment. The `upload` subcommand also requires valid authentication tokens (run `eai login` first).

## Subcommands

### eai docs upload

Upload a file to the platform. The file is sent as a multipart form upload with an authorization header.

```
eai docs upload <file>
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<file>` | Path to the file to upload | Required |

### eai docs classify

Run AI-powered classification on a document. The platform analyzes the document content and returns a classification result including category, confidence score, and extracted metadata.

```
eai docs classify <file>
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<file>` | Path to the file to classify | Required |

### eai docs index

Index an uploaded document for RAG (retrieval-augmented generation). Once indexed, the document's content becomes available to AI chat workflows for context-aware responses.

```
eai docs index <documentId>
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `<documentId>` | The ID of the previously uploaded document | Required |

## Examples

### Upload a document

```bash
eai docs upload ./reports/q1-financial-summary.pdf
```

```
⠋ Uploading q1-financial-summary.pdf...
✔ Uploaded q1-financial-summary.pdf
{
  "id": "doc-8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789",
  "fileName": "q1-financial-summary.pdf",
  "fileUrl": "https://storage.myenterprise.ai/docs/doc-8f3a1b2c.pdf",
  "uploadedAt": "2026-03-09T10:30:00Z"
}
```

### Classify a document

```bash
eai docs classify ./reports/q1-financial-summary.pdf
```

```
⠋ Classifying q1-financial-summary.pdf...
✔ Classified q1-financial-summary.pdf
{
  "category": "report",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "subcategory": "financial-report",
  "extractedMetadata": {
    "period": "Q1 2026",
    "department": "Finance",
    "documentType": "Quarterly Summary"
  }
}
```

### Index a document for RAG

```bash
eai docs index doc-8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
```

```
⠋ Indexing document doc-8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789...
✔ Indexed document doc-8f3a1b2c-... for RAG
```

### Full workflow: upload, classify, and index

```bash
# Step 1: Upload the document
eai docs upload ./evidence/patient-lab-results.pdf

# Step 2: Classify the document
eai docs classify ./evidence/patient-lab-results.pdf

# Step 3: Index for RAG (use the document ID from the upload response)
eai docs index doc-a7c9e4d1-b2c3-4567-89ab-cdef01234567

# Step 4: Query via AI chat
eai chat stream "What do the lab results show?" --workflow wf-medical-789
```

## Prerequisites

- **Authentication**: Run `eai login` before uploading documents. Upload requires a valid access token.
- **Environment**: `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and a tenant ID must be configured.
- **File access**: The file path must be accessible from the current working directory.

## Related Commands

- [`eai chat`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/chat/) -- query indexed documents through AI chat
- [`eai resources`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/resources/) -- manage Document resources (Object Type)
- [`eai login`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/login/) -- authenticate before uploading

---

# eai deploy

## Synopsis

```
eai deploy <subcommand> [options]
```

## Description

`eai deploy` manages the deployment lifecycle for your vertical application. It generates GitHub Actions workflow files, configures deployment secrets, triggers deployments, and monitors their progress.

Deployments target Azure App Service and are triggered via GitHub Actions. The `trigger` and `status` subcommands use the GitHub CLI (`gh`) under the hood.

## Subcommands

### eai deploy setup

Generate a deployment workflow file and optionally configure GitHub repository secrets. Creates `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml` if it does not already exist.

```
eai deploy setup [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--repo <repo>` | GitHub repository in `org/name` format. When provided, lists required secrets. | -- |

The generated workflow requires these GitHub environment secrets (in the `demo` environment):

| Secret | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `AZUREAPPSERVICE_CLIENTID` | Azure AD app registration client ID for deployment |
| `AZUREAPPSERVICE_TENANTID` | Azure AD tenant ID |
| `AZUREAPPSERVICE_SUBSCRIPTIONID` | Azure subscription ID |
| `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP` | Resource group name (e.g., `rg-demo-infrastructure`) |
| `AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME` | App Service name (e.g., `app-demo-eai-dev`) |

### eai deploy trigger

Trigger the deployment workflow on GitHub. Detects the repository from the git remote if `--repo` is not provided.

```
eai deploy trigger [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--repo <repo>` | GitHub repository in `org/name` format | Auto-detected from git remote |
| `--branch <branch>` | Branch to deploy | `main` |
| `--workflow <name>` | Workflow filename | `deploy-demo.yml` |

### eai deploy status

Check the status of recent deployments. Shows the last 5 workflow runs with their status, conclusion, branch, and timestamp.

```
eai deploy status [options]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--repo <repo>` | GitHub repository in `org/name` format | Auto-detected from git remote |

## Examples

### Generate deployment workflow

```bash
eai deploy setup
```

```
⠋ Generating deploy-demo.yml...
✔ Created .github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml

ℹ To configure GitHub secrets, re-run with --repo org/name
```

### Generate workflow and list required secrets

```bash
eai deploy setup --repo eai-tools/patient-intake
```

```
⠋ Generating deploy-demo.yml...
✔ Created .github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml

Configuring GitHub secrets
  Repository: eai-tools/patient-intake
ℹ Configure AZUREAPPSERVICE_CLIENTID: Azure AD app client ID for deployment
ℹ Configure AZUREAPPSERVICE_TENANTID: Azure AD tenant ID
ℹ Configure AZUREAPPSERVICE_SUBSCRIPTIONID: Azure subscription ID
ℹ Configure AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP: Resource group name
ℹ Configure AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: App Service name

ℹ Set secrets with: gh secret set SECRET_NAME --repo eai-tools/patient-intake
```

### Trigger a deployment

```bash
eai deploy trigger
```

```
⠋ Triggering deploy-demo.yml on eai-tools/patient-intake...
✔ Triggered deployment on eai-tools/patient-intake@main
ℹ Check status: eai deploy status --repo eai-tools/patient-intake
```

### Trigger deployment of a specific branch

```bash
eai deploy trigger --branch feature/new-intake-form
```

### Trigger a custom workflow

```bash
eai deploy trigger --workflow deploy-staging.yml --branch develop
```

### Check deployment status

```bash
eai deploy status
```

```
⠋ Checking deployment status...
✔ Recent deployments for eai-tools/patient-intake
  ✔ Deploy Patient Intake (main) — 3/9/2026, 10:15:00 AM
  ✔ Deploy Patient Intake (main) — 3/8/2026, 3:45:00 PM
  ✖ Deploy Patient Intake (main) — 3/7/2026, 9:00:00 AM
  ⟳ Deploy Patient Intake (feature/docs) — 3/7/2026, 8:30:00 AM
  ✔ Deploy Patient Intake (main) — 3/6/2026, 2:00:00 PM
```

## Prerequisites

- **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) must be installed and authenticated for `trigger` and `status` subcommands.
- **Git remote**: The repository is auto-detected from the `origin` remote. Use `--repo` to override.
- **Azure**: Deployment targets Azure App Service. Secrets must be configured in the GitHub repository.

## Generated Workflow

The generated `deploy-demo.yml` performs these steps:

1. Checkout code
2. Set up Node.js 20
3. Install dependencies (`npm ci`)
4. Build Object Types JSON
5. Build the Next.js application
6. Package standalone output as a zip
7. Authenticate with Azure using OIDC
8. Deploy to Azure App Service
9. Restart the App Service

## Related Commands

- [`eai verify`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/verify/) -- verify platform connectivity before deploying
- [`eai env`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/env/) -- manage environment variables for different environments
- [`eai init`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/init/) -- generates the initial deployment workflow during scaffolding

---

# eai verify

## Synopsis

```
eai verify
```

## Description

`eai verify` runs a series of connectivity and configuration checks against the EAI platform. It validates that your local environment can communicate with the API gateway, that authentication is working, that platform services are reachable, and that your local Object Types are loadable.

This command is useful after initial setup, when debugging connectivity issues, or before deploying to confirm your environment is healthy.

The command must be run from within an EAI project directory and requires `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` to be set in `.env.local` or the environment.

## Checks Performed

| Check | What it verifies |
|-------|-----------------|
| **API gateway** | The PublicAPI endpoint is reachable (HTTP request to `/health`). Reports latency. |
| **Authentication** | A valid authentication token exists in `~/.eai/`. Shows the authenticated user. |
| **Platform service** | The platform service responds to Object Type queries (requires auth + tenant ID). |
| **Data service** | The data service schema endpoint is reachable. Reports the number of published types. |
| **Local Object Types** | `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` is loadable and reports type/tenant counts. |

Checks 3 and 4 (platform service and data service) are only run if authentication is valid and a tenant ID is available.

## Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-h, --help` | Display help for the command. |

## Examples

### All checks passing

```bash
eai verify
```

```
Platform Connectivity Checks

✔ PublicAPI reachable (142ms)
✔ Authenticated as jane.doe@example.com
✔ Platform service reachable
✔ Data service reachable — 3 published types
✔ 3 types across 1 tenant scope(s)

✔ All 5 checks passed
```

### Partial failures

```bash
eai verify
```

```
Platform Connectivity Checks

✔ PublicAPI reachable (89ms)
⚠ Not authenticated — run `eai login`
✔ 2 types across 1 tenant scope(s)

⚠ 1 passed, 1 failed
```

### API gateway unreachable

```bash
eai verify
```

```
Platform Connectivity Checks

✖ PublicAPI not reachable: fetch failed
⚠ Not authenticated — run `eai login`
✔ 2 types across 1 tenant scope(s)

⚠ 1 passed, 2 failed
```

### No Object Types defined

```bash
eai verify
```

```
Platform Connectivity Checks

✔ PublicAPI reachable (95ms)
✔ Authenticated as jane.doe@example.com
✔ Platform service reachable
✔ Data service reachable — 0 published types
✖ No Object Types found: Cannot find module 'src/eai.config/object-types.ts'

⚠ 4 passed, 1 failed
```

## Troubleshooting

| Failure | Resolution |
|---------|------------|
| PublicAPI not reachable | Check `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` in `.env.local`. Run `eai env pull` to sync. Verify network connectivity. |
| Not authenticated | Run `eai login` to authenticate with Entra CIAM. |
| Platform service not reachable | Confirm your tenant ID is correct. Check `TENANT_*_ID` in `.env.local`. |
| Data service returned error | The tenant may not have published types yet. Run `eai types seed` to publish. |
| No Object Types found | Create or fix `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`. Run `eai init` for a scaffold. |

## Related Commands

- [`eai login`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/login/) -- authenticate to resolve auth check failures
- [`eai env pull`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/env/) -- sync environment variables to resolve config issues
- [`eai types validate`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/types/) -- validate Object Types before seeding
- [`eai dev`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/dev/) -- runs a subset of these checks before starting the dev server

---

# eai whoami

## Synopsis

```
eai whoami
```

## Description

`eai whoami` displays your current authentication status and project context. It shows the authenticated user, tenant information, token expiration, and -- if run from within an EAI project -- the project's app name, environment, API endpoint, and configured tenant and workflow IDs.

This command is useful for verifying which account you are logged in as, confirming your project configuration, and debugging authentication issues.

## Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-h, --help` | Display help for the command. |

## Examples

### Authenticated with project context

```bash
eai whoami
```

```
Authentication
✔ Logged in as jane.doe@example.com

  Tenant          eaidevmyentepriseai
  Tenant ID       50808ce0-f31b-4fd0-9861-74b83b8c112a
  Expires         3/10/2026, 2:30:00 PM
  Status          Active

Project
  App Name        patient-intake
  Environment     dev
  PublicAPI        https://test-api.myenterprise.ai
  Config Tenant   8f3a1b2c-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
  Workflow        wf-abc-123-def-456
```

### Authenticated without project context

When run outside of an EAI project directory, only the authentication section is shown.

```bash
eai whoami
```

```
Authentication
✔ Logged in as jane.doe@example.com

  Tenant          eaidevmyentepriseai
  Tenant ID       50808ce0-f31b-4fd0-9861-74b83b8c112a
  Expires         3/10/2026, 2:30:00 PM
  Status          Active
```

### Expired token

```bash
eai whoami
```

```
Authentication
⚠ Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.

  Tenant          eaidevmyentepriseai
  Tenant ID       50808ce0-f31b-4fd0-9861-74b83b8c112a
  Expires         3/8/2026, 10:00:00 AM
  Status          Expired
```

### Not logged in

```bash
eai whoami
```

```
Authentication
✖ Not logged in. Run `eai login` to authenticate.
```

## Output Fields

### Authentication section

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Tenant | The Entra CIAM tenant name |
| Tenant ID | The Entra CIAM tenant ID |
| Expires | Token expiration date and time |
| Status | `Active` if the token is valid, `Expired` if it has expired |

### Project section (shown when inside an EAI project)

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| App Name | The vertical application name from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` |
| Environment | Current environment (dev, test, prod) |
| PublicAPI | The platform API gateway URL |
| Config Tenant | The platform tenant ID for this project |
| Workflow | The configured workflow ID |

## Related Commands

- [`eai login`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/login/) -- authenticate or re-authenticate
- [`eai verify`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/verify/) -- run full connectivity checks
- [`eai env list`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/env/) -- view all environment variables
