# eai dev

## Synopsis

```
eai dev [options]
```

## Description

`eai dev` starts the local development server for your vertical application. Before launching, it runs a set of pre-flight connectivity checks to verify that your environment is properly configured:

1. **Environment file**: Confirms `.env.local` exists and is loaded.
2. **API connectivity**: Checks that the PublicAPI gateway is reachable.
3. **Auth configuration**: Verifies that Entra CIAM client and tenant IDs are set.

After checks pass, the CLI starts the Next.js development server (with Turbopack enabled by default) and forwards all environment variables from `.env.local` to the dev server process.

This command must be run from within an EAI project directory.

## Options

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `--port <port>` | Port number for the dev server | `3000` |
| `--turbo` | Use Turbopack for faster builds | `true` |
| `--no-turbo` | Disable Turbopack | -- |
| `--skip-checks` | Skip pre-flight connectivity checks | `false` |
| `-h, --help` | Display help for the command. | -- |

## Examples

### Start development server

```bash
eai dev
```

```
Starting patient-intake

✔ Loaded .env.local
✔ PublicAPI reachable at https://test-api.myenterprise.ai
✔ Auth configured for tenant 50808ce0-...

ℹ Starting Next.js at http://localhost:3000/patient-intake

  ▲ Next.js 15.1.0 (Turbopack)
  - Local:        http://localhost:3000
  - Environments: .env.local

 ✓ Ready in 1.2s
```

### Start on a custom port

```bash
eai dev --port 4000
```

```
Starting patient-intake

✔ Loaded .env.local
✔ PublicAPI reachable at https://test-api.myenterprise.ai
✔ Auth configured for tenant 50808ce0-...

ℹ Starting Next.js at http://localhost:4000/patient-intake
```

### Start without Turbopack

```bash
eai dev --no-turbo
```

### Skip pre-flight checks

```bash
eai dev --skip-checks
```

```
Starting patient-intake

ℹ Starting Next.js at http://localhost:3000/patient-intake

  ▲ Next.js 15.1.0
  - Local:        http://localhost:3000
```

### When checks reveal issues

```bash
eai dev
```

```
Starting patient-intake

⚠ No .env.local found. Run `eai env pull` to sync from cloud.
⚠ PublicAPI not reachable. CRUD/chat operations may fail.
ℹ Run `eai verify` to diagnose connectivity.
⚠ Entra auth not configured. Login will not work.

ℹ Starting Next.js at http://localhost:3000/patient-intake
```

The dev server still starts even when warnings are present, but API-dependent features (CRUD, chat, login) will not function until the issues are resolved.

## Pre-flight Checks

| Check | Warning condition | Resolution |
|-------|-------------------|------------|
| `.env.local` | File is missing or empty | Run `eai env pull` |
| PublicAPI | Endpoint does not respond within 5 seconds | Check `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API`, run `eai verify` |
| Auth config | `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID` or `ENTRA_TENANT_ID` not set | Run `eai env pull --include-secrets` |

## Related Commands

- [`eai verify`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/verify/) -- run the full set of platform connectivity checks
- [`eai env pull`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/env/) -- sync environment variables before starting dev
- [`eai login`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/login/) -- authenticate before using platform features
- [`eai types validate`](/eai-cli/reference/commands/types/) -- validate Object Types before testing locally

---

# API Surface

## Base URL

All API endpoints are relative to the Platform API base URL, configured via the `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` environment variable.

```
https://your-platform.example.com/v3/...
```

## Authentication

All endpoints require authentication unless otherwise noted. Include an access token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

Tokens are obtained through the Entra CIAM device code flow (CLI) or session-based authentication (web applications via BFF proxy).

## Resource Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}` | Required | List resources of a given Object Type. Supports pagination and sorting. |
| `GET` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}` | Required | Get a single resource by ID. |
| `POST` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}` | Required | Create a new resource. |
| `PUT` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}` | Required | Update an existing resource. Requires `version` for optimistic locking. |
| `DELETE` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}` | Required | Delete a resource by ID. |
| `POST` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}/actions/{action}` | Required | Execute a named action on a resource. |
| `POST` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/query` | Required | Cross-type query across multiple Object Types. |
| `GET` | `/v3/resources/schema/{tenantId}` | Required | Get published Object Type definitions for a tenant. |
| `GET` | `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}/history` | Required | Get the change history for a resource. |

### List Resources

```
GET /v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}?page=1&limit=20&sort=-created_at
```

**Query Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | integer | `1` | Page number (1-indexed) |
| `limit` | integer | `20` | Items per page (max 100) |
| `sort` | string | `-created_at` | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order. |

**Response:**

```json
{
  "docs": [
    {
      "id": "abc-123",
      "data": { "firstName": "Jane", "status": "active" },
      "created_at": "2025-03-15T10:30:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2025-03-15T10:30:00Z",
      "version": 1
    }
  ],
  "totalDocs": 42,
  "page": 1,
  "totalPages": 3,
  "limit": 20
}
```

### Create Resource

```
POST /v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "data": {
    "firstName": "Jane",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "status": "draft"
  }
}
```

**Response (201 Created):**

```json
{
  "id": "abc-123",
  "data": { "firstName": "Jane", "lastName": "Doe", "status": "draft" },
  "created_at": "2025-03-15T10:30:00Z",
  "version": 1
}
```

### Update Resource

```
PUT /v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "data": {
    "firstName": "Janet"
  },
  "version": 1
}
```

The `version` field is required for optimistic locking. If the resource has been modified since you last read it, the update will return `409 Conflict`.

### Execute Action

```
POST /v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}/actions/{action}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "params": {}
}
```

The `params` object is passed to the action handler. Most actions do not require additional parameters -- the side effects are defined in the Object Type schema.

### Cross-Type Query

```
POST /v3/resources/{tenantId}/query
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "object_types": ["Patient", "Encounter"],
  "where": {
    "status": { "equals": "active" }
  },
  "limit": 50
}
```

**Request Body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object_types` | string[] | Yes | Object Type names to query across |
| `where` | object | No | Filter conditions |
| `join` | object | No | Join conditions for linked types |
| `limit` | integer | No | Max results (default 20) |

## Chat Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v3/chat/{tenantId}/{workflowId}/{stage}` | Required | Send a chat message and receive a complete response. |
| `POST` | `/v3/chat/stream/{tenantId}/{workflowId}/{stage}` | Required | Stream a chat response using Server-Sent Events (SSE). |

### Send Chat Message

```
POST /v3/chat/{tenantId}/{workflowId}/{stage}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "message": "What is the status of application ABC-123?",
  "conversation_id": "conv-uuid",
  "params": {}
}
```

**Request Body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | Yes | The user's message |
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | Unique conversation identifier (UUID recommended) |
| `params` | object | No | Additional parameters passed to the workflow |

### Stream Chat (SSE)

```
POST /v3/chat/stream/{tenantId}/{workflowId}/{stage}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "message": "Summarize the patient's history.",
  "conversation_id": "conv-uuid",
  "params": {}
}
```

The response is a Server-Sent Events stream:

```
data: {"content": "Based on "}
data: {"content": "the patient's "}
data: {"content": "records..."}
data: [DONE]
```

Each `data` event contains a JSON object with a `content` or `text` field. The stream ends with `data: [DONE]`.

## Document Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v3/documents/classify` | Required | Upload and classify a document. |
| `POST` | `/v3/documents/rag-index` | Required | Index a document for retrieval-augmented generation. |

### Classify Document

```
POST /v3/documents/classify
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

files: <binary file data>
```

Upload a file as `multipart/form-data`. The platform returns classification results.

### Index Document for RAG

```
POST /v3/documents/rag-index
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "document_id": "doc-abc-123"
}
```

Indexes a previously uploaded document so its content can be retrieved during AI chat workflows.

## Auth Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/v3/auth/me` | Required | Get the current authenticated user's profile. |

### Get Current User

```
GET /v3/auth/me
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "id": "user-abc-123",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "role": "tenant-staff",
  "tenantId": "tenant-abc"
}
```

## User Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v3/users/provisionme` | Required | Self-provision the authenticated user into a tenant. |

### Provision User

```
POST /v3/users/provisionme
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "tenant_id": "tenant-abc-123"
}
```

Creates a user record in the specified tenant for the currently authenticated user. This is typically called once after the user's first sign-in.

## Error Response Format

All error responses follow a consistent JSON structure:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Property 'firstName' is required",
    "details": [
      {
        "field": "firstName",
        "rule": "required",
        "message": "This field is required"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `error.code` | string | Machine-readable error code |
| `error.message` | string | Human-readable error description |
| `error.details` | array | Optional array of field-level error details |

See the [Error Codes](/eai-cli/reference/error-codes/) reference for a complete list.

## Rate Limits

  Rate limits are applied per tenant, not per user. All users within a tenant share the same rate limit budget.

| Endpoint Category | Rate Limit | Window |
|---|---|---|
| Resource CRUD | 1000 requests | Per minute |
| Resource queries | 200 requests | Per minute |
| Chat (send) | 60 requests | Per minute |
| Chat (stream) | 30 requests | Per minute |
| Document upload | 30 requests | Per minute |
| Document indexing | 10 requests | Per minute |

When a rate limit is exceeded, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header indicating how many seconds to wait.

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 30 seconds."
  }
}
```

---

# Environment Variables

## Overview

Environment variables are stored in `.env.local` at the project root. The CLI reads this file automatically for all commands. You can pull environment variables from the platform with:

```bash
eai env pull --include-secrets
```

  Never commit `.env.local` to version control. Ensure it is listed in your `.gitignore` file.

## Platform API

| Variable | Description | Required | Default | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` | Base URL of the Platform API | Yes | -- | `https://api.example.com` |
| `EAI_ENV` | Current environment name | No | `dev` | `dev`, `staging`, `production` |

## Authentication (Entra CIAM)

| Variable | Description | Required | Default | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ENTRA_TENANT_ID` | Entra CIAM tenant ID (GUID) | Yes | -- | `a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890` |
| `ENTRA_TENANT_NAME` | Entra CIAM tenant name (used to build the authority URL) | Yes | -- | `myorg` |
| `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID` | Application (client) ID registered in Entra | Yes | -- | `f1e2d3c4-b5a6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890` |
| `AUTH_SECRET` | Secret used for session encryption in Next.js applications | Yes (web) | -- | `a-random-32-character-secret-key` |

The authority URL is constructed as: `https://{ENTRA_TENANT_NAME}.ciamlogin.com/{ENTRA_TENANT_ID}`

## Tenant Configuration

| Variable | Description | Required | Default | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TENANT_DEFAULT_ID` | Default tenant ID used when no specific tenant is specified | Yes | -- | `abc-123-def-456` |
| `TENANT_{KEY}_ID` | Tenant ID for a named tenant key (matches keys in `object-types.ts`) | No | -- | `TENANT_PATIENT_INTAKE_ID=abc-123` |

### Tenant Key Mapping

The CLI maps tenant keys from your `object-types.ts` file to environment variables using the pattern `TENANT_{KEY}_ID`. The key is converted to uppercase with hyphens replaced by underscores.

```typescript
// object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'patient-intake': [ /* ... */ ],    // → TENANT_PATIENT_INTAKE_ID
  'loan-processing': [ /* ... */ ],   // → TENANT_LOAN_PROCESSING_ID
};
```

```bash
# .env.local
TENANT_PATIENT_INTAKE_ID=abc-123-def
TENANT_LOAN_PROCESSING_ID=def-456-ghi
TENANT_DEFAULT_ID=abc-123-def
```

If a specific `TENANT_{KEY}_ID` is not found, the CLI falls back to `TENANT_DEFAULT_ID`.

## Workflow Configuration

| Variable | Description | Required | Default | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WORKFLOW_DEFAULT_ID` | Default AI workflow ID | No | -- | `wf-abc-123` |
| `WORKFLOW_{KEY}_ID` | Workflow ID for a named workflow | No | -- | `WORKFLOW_TRIAGE_ID=wf-def-456` |

## Next.js Public Variables

These variables are exposed to the browser in Next.js applications. They must be prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.

| Variable | Description | Required | Default | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` | Application name (used for display and config resolution) | Yes (web) | -- | `patient-intake` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Public URL of the Next.js application | No | -- | `https://myapp.example.com` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENTRA_TENANT_NAME` | Entra tenant name (for client-side auth redirects) | Yes (web) | -- | `myorg` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENTRA_CLIENT_ID` | Entra client ID (for client-side auth redirects) | Yes (web) | -- | `f1e2d3c4-b5a6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890` |

  `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables are embedded in the client bundle at build time. Do not use this prefix for secrets or sensitive values.

## Example .env.local

```bash
# Platform API
BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API=https://api.example.com
EAI_ENV=dev

# Authentication
ENTRA_TENANT_ID=a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
ENTRA_TENANT_NAME=myorg
ENTRA_CLIENT_ID=f1e2d3c4-b5a6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
AUTH_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-32-char-key

# Tenants
TENANT_DEFAULT_ID=abc-123-def-456
TENANT_PATIENT_INTAKE_ID=abc-123-def-456

# Workflows
WORKFLOW_DEFAULT_ID=wf-abc-123

# Next.js (web apps only)
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=patient-intake
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000
NEXT_PUBLIC_ENTRA_TENANT_NAME=myorg
NEXT_PUBLIC_ENTRA_CLIENT_ID=f1e2d3c4-b5a6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
```

## Variable Resolution Order

The CLI resolves environment variables in this order (later sources take precedence):

1. `.env.local` file in the project root
2. System environment variables (`process.env`)

This means you can override any `.env.local` value by setting a system environment variable:

```bash
# Override the default tenant for a single command
TENANT_DEFAULT_ID=different-tenant eai resources list Patient
```

## CI/CD Considerations

In CI/CD pipelines, set environment variables through your platform's secret management instead of `.env.local`:

- **GitHub Actions**: Use repository secrets and reference them as `${{ secrets.BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API }}`
- **Azure Pipelines**: Use variable groups or pipeline variables
- **Docker**: Pass variables via `--env-file` or individual `--env` flags

```yaml
# GitHub Actions example
env:
  BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API: ${{ secrets.BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API }}
  ENTRA_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.ENTRA_TENANT_ID }}
  ENTRA_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.ENTRA_CLIENT_ID }}
  TENANT_DEFAULT_ID: ${{ secrets.TENANT_DEFAULT_ID }}
```

---

# Error Codes

## HTTP Status Codes

The Platform API uses standard HTTP status codes. The most common ones you will encounter are listed below.

| Status | Meaning | When It Occurs |
|---|---|---|
| `200 OK` | Request succeeded | Successful GET, PUT, or action execution |
| `201 Created` | Resource created | Successful POST to create a resource |
| `204 No Content` | Deleted successfully | Successful DELETE |
| `400 Bad Request` | Malformed request | Invalid JSON, missing required fields in request body |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Not authenticated | Missing or expired access token |
| `403 Forbidden` | Not authorized | User's role is insufficient for the requested operation |
| `404 Not Found` | Resource not found | Invalid resource ID, Object Type, or tenant ID |
| `409 Conflict` | Version conflict | Optimistic locking failure -- the resource was modified since you last read it |
| `422 Unprocessable Entity` | Validation failed | Schema validation error, action pre-condition not met |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded | Too many requests in the current window |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Server error | Unexpected error on the platform side |

## Platform API Error Codes

All error responses include a machine-readable `code` field. Use this value for programmatic error handling.

### Authentication Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_TOKEN_MISSING` | 401 | No authorization token provided | The `Authorization` header is missing | Include `Authorization: Bearer {token}` in the request |
| `AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 401 | Access token has expired | The access token's expiry time has passed | Refresh the token or run `eai login` |
| `AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID` | 401 | Access token is invalid | The token is malformed or was issued by an untrusted authority | Run `eai login` to obtain a new token |
| `AUTH_REFRESH_FAILED` | 401 | Token refresh failed | The refresh token is expired or revoked | Run `eai login` to re-authenticate |

### Authorization Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FORBIDDEN_ROLE` | 403 | Insufficient role for this operation | The user's role is lower than the action's `requiredRole` | Contact a tenant admin to upgrade the user's role |
| `FORBIDDEN_TENANT` | 403 | User does not belong to this tenant | The authenticated user is not provisioned in the target tenant | Run `eai verify` or provision the user into the tenant |
| `FORBIDDEN_RESOURCE` | 403 | Access denied to this resource | A `tenant-user` is trying to access another user's resource | Use a `tenant-staff` or `tenant-admin` account |

### Resource Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Resource not found | The resource ID does not exist or belongs to a different tenant | Verify the ID and tenant |
| `OBJECT_TYPE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Object Type not found | The Object Type name is not published for this tenant | Run `eai types seed` to publish the Object Type, or check the name spelling |
| `VERSION_CONFLICT` | 409 | Resource has been modified | The `version` in the update request does not match the current version | Re-fetch the resource to get the latest version, then retry |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 422 | Validation failed | One or more fields failed schema validation | Check the `details` array for specific field errors |
| `ACTION_PRECONDITION_FAILED` | 422 | Action pre-conditions not met | Required fields are empty or the resource is not in the required status | Check `validationRules` in the action definition |
| `DUPLICATE_RESOURCE` | 409 | Resource already exists | A uniqueness constraint was violated | Check for existing resources with the same unique field values |

### Chat Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Workflow not found | The workflow ID does not exist for this tenant | Verify the `WORKFLOW_DEFAULT_ID` or `--workflow` value |
| `CHAT_STAGE_INVALID` | 400 | Invalid chat stage | The stage name is not defined in the workflow | Check available stages for the workflow |
| `CHAT_STREAM_ERROR` | 500 | Stream connection failed | The AI service encountered an error while streaming | Retry the request; check AI service status if persistent |

### Document Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | File exceeds maximum size | The uploaded file is larger than the platform allows | Reduce file size or split into smaller documents |
| `DOCUMENT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` | 400 | Unsupported file type | The file format is not supported for classification | Check supported formats (PDF, DOCX, PNG, JPG, etc.) |
| `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Document not found | The document ID does not exist | Verify the document was uploaded successfully |
| `INDEX_FAILED` | 500 | Document indexing failed | The RAG indexing process encountered an error | Retry; check that the document is in a supported format |

### Rate Limit Errors

| Code | HTTP Status | Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Rate limit exceeded | Too many requests from this tenant in the current window | Wait for the `Retry-After` period, then retry |

## CLI-Specific Errors

These errors are raised by the CLI itself, not the Platform API.

### Project Errors

| Error Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `Not in an EAI project.` | The current directory (or its ancestors) does not contain `eai.config.ts`, `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`, or a `package.json` with EAI dependencies | `cd` into your project directory, or run `eai init` to create a new project |
| `No object-types.ts found.` | The CLI could not find an Object Type definitions file | Create `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` in your project |
| `Failed to load Object Types` | The `object-types.ts` file has a syntax error or exports an unexpected structure | Check the file for TypeScript errors; ensure it exports `objectTypes` |

### Authentication Errors

| Error Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `Not authenticated.` | No stored token found at `~/.eai/tokens.json` | Run `eai login` |
| `Token expired. Please run eai login.` | Both the access token and refresh token have expired | Run `eai login` |
| `Device code flow timed out.` | The user did not complete sign-in within the timeout period | Run `eai login` again and complete the browser sign-in promptly |

### Environment Errors

| Error Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API not set.` | The Platform API URL is not configured | Run `eai env pull` or set `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` in `.env.local` |
| `Missing BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API or tenant ID.` | Either the API URL or a tenant ID is missing | Set both `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and `TENANT_DEFAULT_ID` in `.env.local` |
| `No tenant ID found for "{key}".` | No `TENANT_{KEY}_ID` environment variable matches the tenant key in `object-types.ts` | Add the matching `TENANT_{KEY}_ID` to `.env.local` |

### Validation Errors

| Error Message | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `name "{name}" must be PascalCase` | Object Type name does not match `/^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/` | Rename to PascalCase (e.g., `patientRecord` -> `PatientRecord`) |
| `missing displayName` | Object Type is missing the `displayName` field | Add a `displayName` string |
| `invalid status "{status}"` | Status is not `draft`, `published`, or `deprecated` | Use one of the three valid values |
| `duplicate property name "{name}"` | Two properties share the same name | Rename one of the duplicate properties |
| `select property "{name}" must have options` | A `select`-type property has an empty or missing `options` array | Add at least one option to the `options` array |

## Error Response Structure

All Platform API errors follow this structure:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Property 'firstName' is required",
    "details": [
      {
        "field": "firstName",
        "rule": "required",
        "message": "This field is required"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The `details` array is optional and only present for validation errors that affect specific fields.

  When debugging errors, use `--json` flag on CLI commands (e.g., `eai resources list Patient --json`) to see the full API response including error details.

---

# Glossary

## A

### Action

A named business operation declared in an [Object Type](#object-type) definition. Actions have a required role, validation rules (pre-conditions), and side effects (automated field changes). Actions are executed via the Platform API at `/v3/resources/{tenantId}/{objectType}/{id}/actions/{action}`.

See: [Data Model - Actions](/eai-cli/concepts/data-model/#actions), [Object Type Schema - Action Reference](/eai-cli/reference/object-type-schema/#action-reference)

## B

### BFF Proxy

**Backend-for-Frontend Proxy.** A server-side layer in Next.js applications that forwards requests to the [Platform API](#platform-api). The BFF proxy adds the user's access token (stored server-side) before forwarding, keeping credentials out of the browser.

See: [Architecture - BFF Proxy Pattern](/eai-cli/concepts/architecture/#bff-proxy-pattern)

## C

### Cardinality

The relationship multiplicity between two [Object Types](#object-type). Supported values: `one-to-one`, `one-to-many`, `many-to-one`, `many-to-many`. Defined on [Link Types](#link-type).

See: [Object Type Schema - Link Type Reference](/eai-cli/reference/object-type-schema/#link-type-reference)

### CLI

**Command Line Interface.** The `eai` tool (`@eai-tools/cli`) used to scaffold, validate, seed, deploy, and manage vertical business applications from the terminal. Installed globally via `npm install -g @eai-tools/cli`.

See: [Installation](/eai-cli/getting-started/installation/), [Quick Start](/eai-cli/getting-started/quickstart/)

## D

### Data Service

A backend service that manages data storage and retrieval for [resources](#resource). Part of the [platform service](#platform-service) layer. Not accessed directly -- all operations go through the [Platform API](#platform-api).

### Device Code Flow

An OAuth 2.0 authentication flow that allows the CLI to authenticate without requiring a browser on the same machine. The CLI displays a code and URL; the user opens the URL in any browser, enters the code, and signs in. Used by `eai login`.

See: [Architecture - Authentication Flow](/eai-cli/concepts/architecture/#authentication-flow), [Security Model - CLI Authentication](/eai-cli/concepts/security-model/#cli-authentication-device-code-flow)

## E

### Entra CIAM

**Microsoft Entra Customer Identity and Access Management.** The identity provider used for authentication in the EnterpriseAI platform. Handles user sign-up, sign-in, MFA, and token issuance.

See: [Security Model - Authentication](/eai-cli/concepts/security-model/#authentication)

## L

### Link Type

A declared relationship between two [Object Types](#object-type). Each link type has a name, target Object Type, [cardinality](#cardinality), and optional cascade delete behavior. Defined in the `linkTypes` array of an Object Type definition.

See: [Data Model - Links](/eai-cli/concepts/data-model/#links-relationships), [Object Type Schema - Link Type Reference](/eai-cli/reference/object-type-schema/#link-type-reference)

## O

### Object Type

The core data modeling abstraction in EnterpriseAI. An Object Type defines a category of [resource](#resource) with [properties](#property) (fields), [link types](#link-type) (relationships), [actions](#action) (business operations), and [side effects](#side-effect) (computed values). Defined in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` and published to the platform with `eai types seed`.

See: [Data Model](/eai-cli/concepts/data-model/), [Object Type Schema](/eai-cli/reference/object-type-schema/)

## P

### Platform API

The central API gateway for the EnterpriseAI platform. All client-facing traffic (from the CLI, Platform SDK, and web applications) goes through the Platform API at `/v3/*`. Endpoints cover resources, chat, documents, authentication, and user management.

See: [Architecture](/eai-cli/concepts/architecture/), [API Surface](/eai-cli/reference/api-surface/)

### Platform SDK

A TypeScript library (`@eai-tools/platform-sdk`) used inside Next.js applications to interact with the [Platform API](#platform-api). Unlike the CLI (which calls the API directly), the SDK routes requests through the [BFF proxy](#bff-proxy).

### Platform Service

The backend service that manages [resources](#resource), [Object Type](#object-type) schemas, [tenants](#tenant), and users. Not accessed directly -- all operations go through the [Platform API](#platform-api).

### Property

A field definition within an [Object Type](#object-type). Each property has a name, type (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `select`, `json`, `file`, or `relationship`), and optional constraints (`required`, `indexed`, `defaultValue`, `options`).

See: [Data Model - Properties](/eai-cli/concepts/data-model/#properties), [Object Type Schema - Field Type Reference](/eai-cli/reference/object-type-schema/#field-type-reference)

## R

### Resource

An instance of an [Object Type](#object-type). Resources are created, read, updated, and deleted through the Platform API. Each resource has an `id`, a `data` object (containing property values), a `version` (for optimistic locking), and timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`). Resources are always scoped to a [tenant](#tenant).

See: [API Surface - Resource Endpoints](/eai-cli/reference/api-surface/#resource-endpoints)

### Role

A permission level assigned to a user within a [tenant](#tenant). The platform defines three roles: `tenant-user`, `tenant-staff`, and `tenant-admin`. Roles control which resources a user can access and which [actions](#action) they can execute.

See: [Security Model - Roles](/eai-cli/concepts/security-model/#roles)

## S

### Side Effect

An automated field change applied when an [action](#action) is executed successfully. Side effect types: `set_field` (static value), `set_timestamp` (current time), `set_user` (authenticated user's ID). Side effects are atomic -- if any fails, the entire action is rolled back.

See: [Data Model - Side Effects](/eai-cli/concepts/data-model/#side-effects), [Object Type Schema - Side Effect Type Details](/eai-cli/reference/object-type-schema/#side-effect-type-details)

## T

### Tenant

An isolated organizational unit in the platform. Every [resource](#resource), conversation, and document is scoped to a tenant. Users belong to one or more tenants and have a [role](#role) within each. Tenants can be organized in a parent-child hierarchy. Tenant IDs are part of API URLs (`/v3/resources/{tenantId}/...`).

See: [Security Model - Multi-Tenant Data Isolation](/eai-cli/concepts/security-model/#multi-tenant-data-isolation)

## V

### Vertical

A **vertical business application** -- software designed for a specific industry or domain (healthcare, finance, government, etc.). Verticals encode domain-specific [Object Types](#object-type), workflows, and compliance rules. The EnterpriseAI platform and CLI are purpose-built for creating verticals.

See: [Verticals](/eai-cli/concepts/verticals/)

### Version (Optimistic Locking)

A numeric counter on each [resource](#resource) that increments with every update. When updating a resource, you must include the current `version` in the request. If the resource has been modified since you last read it (the version does not match), the update is rejected with a `409 Conflict` error.

See: [API Surface - Update Resource](/eai-cli/reference/api-surface/#update-resource)

---

# Object Type Schema

## TypeScript Interfaces

The following interfaces define the complete Object Type schema. These are exported from `src/lib/config.ts` in the CLI and used in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` in vertical applications.

### ObjectTypeDefinition

```typescript
interface ObjectTypeDefinition {
  /** PascalCase name (e.g., "Patient", "LoanApplication") */
  name: string;

  /** Human-readable label */
  displayName: string;

  /** Optional documentation */
  description?: string;

  /** Field definitions */
  properties: ObjectTypeProperty[];

  /** Relationships to other Object Types */
  linkTypes: ObjectTypeLinkType[];

  /** Business operations */
  actions: ObjectTypeAction[];

  /** Storage backend identifier (optional, platform-managed) */
  storageBackend?: string;

  /** Lifecycle status */
  status: 'draft' | 'published' | 'deprecated';
}
```

### ObjectTypeProperty

```typescript
interface ObjectTypeProperty {
  /** Field name (camelCase recommended) */
  name: string;

  /** Field type */
  type: 'text' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'date' | 'select' | 'json' | 'file' | 'relationship';

  /** Whether the field must be present when creating a resource */
  required: boolean;

  /** Whether the field is indexed for faster queries */
  indexed?: boolean;

  /** Default value applied when the field is not provided */
  defaultValue?: string | number | boolean;

  /** Required for "select" type. List of allowed values. */
  options?: Array<{ label: string; value: string }>;

  /** Optional documentation for the field */
  description?: string;
}
```

### ObjectTypeLinkType

```typescript
interface ObjectTypeLinkType {
  /** Relationship name (camelCase recommended) */
  name: string;

  /** The Object Type this link points to (PascalCase) */
  targetObjectType: string;

  /** Relationship cardinality */
  cardinality: 'one-to-one' | 'one-to-many' | 'many-to-one' | 'many-to-many';

  /** If true, deleting the source also deletes linked targets */
  cascadeDelete?: boolean;
}
```

### ObjectTypeAction

```typescript
interface ObjectTypeAction {
  /** Action identifier (snake_case recommended) */
  name: string;

  /** Human-readable label */
  displayName: string;

  /** Minimum role required to execute this action */
  requiredRole: 'tenant-user' | 'tenant-staff' | 'tenant-admin';

  /** Pre-conditions that must be met before execution */
  validationRules: {
    /** Fields that must have non-empty values */
    requiredFields?: string[];

    /** The resource must be in this status */
    requiredStatus?: string;
  };

  /** Automated field changes applied on successful execution */
  sideEffects: Array<{
    /** Side effect type */
    type: 'set_field' | 'set_timestamp' | 'set_user';

    /** Target field name (must exist in properties) */
    field: string;

    /** Static value (required for "set_field", ignored for others) */
    value?: string | number | boolean;
  }>;
}
```

## Field Type Reference

### text

Free-form string values.

```typescript
{ name: 'firstName', type: 'text', required: true }
{ name: 'notes', type: 'text', required: false, description: 'Free-form notes' }
```

**Validation**: No maximum length enforced by default. Empty strings are treated as missing when `required: true`.

### number

Numeric values (integer or decimal).

```typescript
{ name: 'age', type: 'number', required: true }
{ name: 'score', type: 'number', required: false, defaultValue: 0 }
```

**Validation**: Must be a valid JSON number. No range constraints at the schema level.

### boolean

True or false.

```typescript
{ name: 'isActive', type: 'boolean', required: true, defaultValue: true }
```

**Validation**: Must be `true` or `false`. String values like `"true"` are not accepted.

### date

ISO 8601 date strings.

```typescript
{ name: 'dateOfBirth', type: 'date', required: true }
{ name: 'submittedAt', type: 'date', required: false }
```

**Validation**: Must be a valid ISO 8601 string (e.g., `"2025-03-15"` or `"2025-03-15T10:30:00Z"`).

### select

One of a predefined set of options.

```typescript
{
  name: 'status',
  type: 'select',
  required: true,
  defaultValue: 'draft',
  options: [
    { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
    { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
    { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
    { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
  ],
}
```

**Validation**: The value must match one of the defined `options[].value` strings. The `options` array is required and must contain at least one entry.

### json

Arbitrary JSON objects.

```typescript
{ name: 'metadata', type: 'json', required: false }
```

**Validation**: Must be a valid JSON object, array, or primitive. No schema validation is applied to the contents.

### file

File references (typically a path or URL).

```typescript
{ name: 'attachment', type: 'file', required: false }
```

**Validation**: Must be a string. File upload and storage are handled by the document service.

### relationship

Reference to another resource by ID.

```typescript
{ name: 'assignedTo', type: 'relationship', required: false }
```

**Validation**: Must be a valid resource ID string. The platform does not enforce referential integrity at the property level -- use link types for managed relationships.

  For managed relationships with cardinality and cascade behavior, use **link types** instead of `relationship` properties. The `relationship` property type is for lightweight, unmanaged references.

## Link Type Reference

### Cardinality Rules

| Cardinality | Source Side | Target Side | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `one-to-one` | At most one target | At most one source | Patient -> InsurancePolicy |
| `one-to-many` | Many targets | At most one source | Doctor -> Patients |
| `many-to-one` | At most one target | Many sources | Patients -> PrimaryCareProvider |
| `many-to-many` | Many targets | Many sources | Students -> Courses |

### Cascade Delete

When `cascadeDelete: true`, deleting the source resource will also delete all linked target resources. Use with caution.

```typescript
{
  name: 'attachments',
  targetObjectType: 'Attachment',
  cardinality: 'one-to-many',
  cascadeDelete: true,  // Deleting the parent deletes all attachments
}
```

  Cascade deletes are **not reversible**. The platform does not support soft-delete for cascaded resources. Use `cascadeDelete: false` (the default) unless you are certain that linked resources should not exist independently.

## Action Reference

### Validation Rules

Actions support two pre-condition checks:

| Rule | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `requiredFields` | The specified fields must have non-empty, non-null values on the resource. |
| `requiredStatus` | The resource's `status` field (if it has one) must equal this value. |

Both rules are checked before execution. If either fails, the action is rejected with a `422 Unprocessable Entity` response.

### Side Effect Execution Order

Side effects are applied in the order they are defined in the array:

```typescript
sideEffects: [
  { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'approved' },   // 1st
  { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'approvedAt' },              // 2nd
  { type: 'set_user', field: 'approvedBy' },                   // 3rd
]
```

All side effects are applied atomically. If any side effect fails (e.g., the target field does not exist), the entire action is rolled back.

### Side Effect Type Details

#### set_field

Sets a field to a static value.

```typescript
{ type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'approved' }
```

- `field` must be a valid property name on the Object Type.
- `value` is required and must match the property's type.

#### set_timestamp

Sets a field to the current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

```typescript
{ type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'approvedAt' }
```

- `field` should be a `date`-type property (though `text` is also accepted).
- `value` is ignored; the platform injects the current timestamp.

#### set_user

Sets a field to the authenticated user's ID.

```typescript
{ type: 'set_user', field: 'approvedBy' }
```

- `field` should be a `text`-type or `relationship`-type property.
- `value` is ignored; the platform injects the user ID from the Bearer token.

## Schema Validation Rules

The `eai types validate` command checks the following rules:

| Rule | Severity | Description |
|---|---|---|
| PascalCase name | Error | Object Type `name` must match `/^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/` |
| Display name required | Error | `displayName` must be non-empty |
| Valid status | Error | `status` must be `draft`, `published`, or `deprecated` |
| No duplicate properties | Error | Property names must be unique within an Object Type |
| Valid property type | Error | Property `type` must be one of the eight valid types |
| Select options required | Error | `select`-type properties must have a non-empty `options` array |
| Options on non-select | Warning | Properties with `options` but a type other than `select` |
| Link target required | Error | Link types must have a `targetObjectType` |
| Valid cardinality | Error | Must be `one-to-one`, `one-to-many`, `many-to-one`, or `many-to-many` |
| Action name required | Error | Actions must have a `name` |
| Valid required role | Error | Must be `tenant-user`, `tenant-staff`, or `tenant-admin` |
| Valid side effect type | Error | Must be `set_field`, `set_timestamp`, or `set_user` |
| Side effect field exists | Warning | Side effect `field` should reference an existing property |

## File Structure

Object Types are defined in your project at:

```
my-vertical/
├── src/
│   └── eai.config/
│       └── object-types.ts    ← Define Object Types here
├── .env.local                 ← Tenant IDs and API URLs
└── package.json
```

The file must export an `objectTypes` variable:

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts

export const objectTypes: Record<string, ObjectTypeDefinition[]> = {
  'my-tenant-key': [
    { /* Object Type 1 */ },
    { /* Object Type 2 */ },
  ],
};
```

The keys in the record (`'my-tenant-key'`) are mapped to tenant IDs via environment variables (`TENANT_MY_TENANT_KEY_ID`).

---

# C# Examples

These examples show how to call the EAI Platform API from C# using `HttpClient` with `async/await` and `System.Text.Json` for serialization.

  All examples assume you have `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and your access token available as environment variables. Run `eai env pull` to populate your `.env.local` file.

## Setup

```csharp
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

public class EaiClient : IDisposable
{
    private readonly HttpClient _http;
    private readonly string _baseUrl;
    private readonly string _tenantId;
    private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions JsonOptions = new()
    {
        PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
        DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull,
    };

    public EaiClient(string baseUrl, string tenantId, string accessToken)
    {
        _baseUrl = baseUrl;
        _tenantId = tenantId;
        _http = new HttpClient();
        _http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization =
            new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", accessToken);
        _http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Accept.Add(
            new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("application/json"));
    }

    private async Task<T> SendAsync<T>(HttpMethod method, string path, object? body = null)
    {
        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(method, $"{_baseUrl}{path}");

        if (body is not null)
        {
            var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(body, JsonOptions);
            request.Content = new StringContent(json, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json");
        }

        using var response = await _http.SendAsync(request);
        var responseBody = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync();

        if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode)
            throw new EaiApiException((int)response.StatusCode, responseBody);

        return JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(responseBody, JsonOptions)!;
    }

    public void Dispose() => _http.Dispose();
}
```

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```csharp
public record UserProfile(
    string Id,
    string Email,
    string DisplayName,
    string[] Roles
);

// Add to EaiClient class
public async Task<UserProfile> GetAuthenticatedUserAsync()
{
    return await SendAsync<UserProfile>(HttpMethod.Get, "/v3/auth/me");
}

public async Task ProvisionUserAsync()
{
    await SendAsync<object>(HttpMethod.Post, "/v3/users/provisionme");
}

// Usage
var baseUrl = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API")!;
var tenantId = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TENANT_ID")!;
var token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN")!;

using var client = new EaiClient(baseUrl, tenantId, token);
var me = await client.GetAuthenticatedUserAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Logged in as {me.DisplayName} ({me.Email})");
```

## Resource CRUD

Create, list, get, update, and delete resources:

```csharp
public record Resource(
    string Id,
    string ObjectType,
    Dictionary<string, object> Data,
    DateTime CreatedAt,
    DateTime UpdatedAt
);

public record ResourceList(
    Resource[] Items,
    int Total,
    int Page,
    int PageSize
);

// Add these methods to EaiClient
public async Task<Resource> CreateResourceAsync(string objectType, object data)
{
    return await SendAsync<Resource>(
        HttpMethod.Post, $"/v3/resources/{_tenantId}/{objectType}", data);
}

public async Task<ResourceList> ListResourcesAsync(string objectType)
{
    return await SendAsync<ResourceList>(
        HttpMethod.Get, $"/v3/resources/{_tenantId}/{objectType}");
}

public async Task<Resource> GetResourceAsync(string objectType, string resourceId)
{
    return await SendAsync<Resource>(
        HttpMethod.Get, $"/v3/resources/{_tenantId}/{objectType}/{resourceId}");
}

public async Task<Resource> UpdateResourceAsync(
    string objectType, string resourceId, object data)
{
    return await SendAsync<Resource>(
        HttpMethod.Put, $"/v3/resources/{_tenantId}/{objectType}/{resourceId}", data);
}

public async Task DeleteResourceAsync(string objectType, string resourceId)
{
    await SendAsync<object>(
        HttpMethod.Delete, $"/v3/resources/{_tenantId}/{objectType}/{resourceId}");
}
```

### Full CRUD workflow

```csharp
// Create
var task = await client.CreateResourceAsync("Task", new
{
    Title = "Review pull request",
    Status = "open",
    Priority = "high",
});
Console.WriteLine($"Created task {task.Id}");

// List
var tasks = await client.ListResourcesAsync("Task");
Console.WriteLine($"Found {tasks.Total} tasks");

// Get
var fetched = await client.GetResourceAsync("Task", task.Id);
Console.WriteLine($"Task title: {fetched.Data["title"]}");

// Update
var updated = await client.UpdateResourceAsync("Task", task.Id, new
{
    Title = "Review pull request",
    Status = "in-progress",
    Priority = "high",
});
Console.WriteLine($"Updated status to {updated.Data["status"]}");

// Delete
await client.DeleteResourceAsync("Task", task.Id);
Console.WriteLine("Task deleted");
```

## Querying resources

Fetch the tenant schema to discover available object types:

```csharp
public record ObjectTypeSchema(string Name, object[] Properties);
public record SchemaResponse(ObjectTypeSchema[] ObjectTypes);

// Add to EaiClient
public async Task<SchemaResponse> GetSchemaAsync()
{
    return await SendAsync<SchemaResponse>(
        HttpMethod.Get, $"/v3/resources/schema/{_tenantId}");
}

var schema = await client.GetSchemaAsync();
var typeNames = schema.ObjectTypes.Select(ot => ot.Name);
Console.WriteLine($"Available object types: {string.Join(", ", typeNames)}");
```

## Chat

Send a message to an AI workflow:

  
```csharp
public record ChatResponse(
    string Message,
    string ConversationId,
    Dictionary<string, object>? Metadata
);

// Add to EaiClient
public async Task<ChatResponse> SendChatMessageAsync(
    string workflowId, string stage, string message)
{
    return await SendAsync<ChatResponse>(
        HttpMethod.Post,
        $"/v3/chat/{_tenantId}/{workflowId}/{stage}",
        new { Message = message });
}

var reply = await client.SendChatMessageAsync("wf-123", "default", "Summarize open tasks");
Console.WriteLine($"AI: {reply.Message}");
```
  
  
```csharp
// Add to EaiClient
public async Task StreamChatAsync(string workflowId, string stage, string message)
{
    var url = $"{_baseUrl}/v3/chat/stream/{_tenantId}/{workflowId}/{stage}";
    var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { Message = message }, JsonOptions);
    var content = new StringContent(json, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json");

    using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url) { Content = content };
    using var response = await _http.SendAsync(request, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead);
    response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

    await using var stream = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync();
    using var reader = new StreamReader(stream);

    var buffer = new char[256];
    int bytesRead;
    while ((bytesRead = await reader.ReadAsync(buffer, 0, buffer.Length)) > 0)
    {
        Console.Write(new string(buffer, 0, bytesRead));
    }

    Console.WriteLine();
}

await client.StreamChatAsync("wf-123", "default", "What is the project status?");
```
  

## Error handling

Define a custom exception and handle common error codes:

```csharp
public class EaiApiException : Exception
{
    public int StatusCode { get; }
    public string ResponseBody { get; }

    public EaiApiException(int statusCode, string responseBody)
        : base($"EAI API error {statusCode}: {responseBody}")
    {
        StatusCode = statusCode;
        ResponseBody = responseBody;
    }

    public bool IsUnauthorized => StatusCode == 401;
    public bool IsNotFound => StatusCode == 404;
    public bool IsRateLimited => StatusCode == 429;
}

// Usage with structured error handling
async Task<ResourceList> SafeListResources(EaiClient client, string objectType)
{
    try
    {
        return await client.ListResourcesAsync(objectType);
    }
    catch (EaiApiException ex) when (ex.IsUnauthorized)
    {
        Console.Error.WriteLine("Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.");
        throw;
    }
    catch (EaiApiException ex) when (ex.IsRateLimited)
    {
        Console.Error.WriteLine("Rate limited. Retrying after delay...");
        await Task.Delay(2000);
        return await client.ListResourcesAsync(objectType);
    }
    catch (EaiApiException ex)
    {
        Console.Error.WriteLine($"API error: {ex.Message}");
        throw;
    }
}
```

---

# Go Examples

These examples show how to call the EAI Platform API from Go using the standard library. All requests use `context.Context` for cancellation and `encoding/json` for serialization.

  All examples assume you have `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and your access token available as environment variables. Run `eai env pull` to populate your `.env.local` file.

## Setup

```go
package eai

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"time"
)

type Client struct {
	BaseURL    string
	TenantID   string
	Token      string
	HTTPClient *http.Client
}

func NewClient() *Client {
	return &Client{
		BaseURL:  os.Getenv("BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API"),
		TenantID: os.Getenv("TENANT_ID"),
		Token:    os.Getenv("EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN"),
		HTTPClient: &http.Client{
			Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
		},
	}
}

func (c *Client) doRequest(ctx context.Context, method, path string, body any) ([]byte, error) {
	var reqBody io.Reader
	if body != nil {
		data, err := json.Marshal(body)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("marshal request body: %w", err)
		}
		reqBody = bytes.NewReader(data)
	}

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, c.BaseURL+path, reqBody)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("create request: %w", err)
	}

	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.Token)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

	resp, err := c.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("send request: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	respBody, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read response: %w", err)
	}

	if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
		return nil, &ApiError{StatusCode: resp.StatusCode, Body: string(respBody)}
	}

	return respBody, nil
}
```

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```go
type UserProfile struct {
	ID          string   `json:"id"`
	Email       string   `json:"email"`
	DisplayName string   `json:"displayName"`
	Roles       []string `json:"roles"`
}

func (c *Client) GetAuthenticatedUser(ctx context.Context) (*UserProfile, error) {
	data, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodGet, "/v3/auth/me", nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var user UserProfile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &user); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode user profile: %w", err)
	}
	return &user, nil
}

func (c *Client) ProvisionUser(ctx context.Context) error {
	_, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodPost, "/v3/users/provisionme", nil)
	return err
}

// Usage
func main() {
	client := NewClient()
	ctx := context.Background()

	user, err := client.GetAuthenticatedUser(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("auth failed: %v", err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("Logged in as %s (%s)\n", user.DisplayName, user.Email)
}
```

## Resource CRUD

Create, list, get, update, and delete resources:

```go
type Resource struct {
	ID         string         `json:"id"`
	ObjectType string         `json:"objectType"`
	Data       map[string]any `json:"data"`
	CreatedAt  time.Time      `json:"createdAt"`
	UpdatedAt  time.Time      `json:"updatedAt"`
}

type ResourceList struct {
	Items    []Resource `json:"items"`
	Total    int        `json:"total"`
	Page     int        `json:"page"`
	PageSize int        `json:"pageSize"`
}

func (c *Client) CreateResource(ctx context.Context, objectType string, data any) (*Resource, error) {
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/v3/resources/%s/%s", c.TenantID, objectType)
	respBody, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, data)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var resource Resource
	return &resource, json.Unmarshal(respBody, &resource)
}

func (c *Client) ListResources(ctx context.Context, objectType string) (*ResourceList, error) {
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/v3/resources/%s/%s", c.TenantID, objectType)
	respBody, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var list ResourceList
	return &list, json.Unmarshal(respBody, &list)
}

func (c *Client) GetResource(ctx context.Context, objectType, resourceID string) (*Resource, error) {
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/v3/resources/%s/%s/%s", c.TenantID, objectType, resourceID)
	respBody, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var resource Resource
	return &resource, json.Unmarshal(respBody, &resource)
}

func (c *Client) UpdateResource(ctx context.Context, objectType, resourceID string, data any) (*Resource, error) {
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/v3/resources/%s/%s/%s", c.TenantID, objectType, resourceID)
	respBody, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodPut, path, data)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var resource Resource
	return &resource, json.Unmarshal(respBody, &resource)
}

func (c *Client) DeleteResource(ctx context.Context, objectType, resourceID string) error {
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/v3/resources/%s/%s/%s", c.TenantID, objectType, resourceID)
	_, err := c.doRequest(ctx, http.MethodDelete, path, nil)
	return err
}
```

### Full CRUD workflow

```go

	"title":    "Review pull request",
	"status":   "open",
	"priority": "high",
})

	log.Fatalf("create: %v", err)
}

if err != nil {
	log.Fatalf("list: %v", err)

if err != nil {
	log.Fatalf("get: %v", err)
}
fmt.Printf("Task title: %s\n", fetched.Data["title"])

// Update

	"title":    "Review pull request",
	"status":   "in-progress",
	"priority": "high",
})
if err != nil {
	log.Fatalf("update: %v", err)
}
fmt.Printf("Updated status to %s\n", updated.Data["status"])

// Delete
if err := client.DeleteResource(ctx, "Task", task.ID); err != nil {
	log.Fatalf("delete: %v", err)
}
fmt.Println("Task deleted")
```

  
  
```go
func (c *Client) StreamChat(ctx context.Context, workflowID, stage, message string) error {
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/v3/chat/stream/%s/%s/%s", c.TenantID, workflowID, stage)
	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"message": message})

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, c.BaseURL+path, bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create request: %w", err)
	}
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.Token)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

	resp, err := c.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("send request: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
		errBody, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		return &ApiError{StatusCode: resp.StatusCode, Body: string(errBody)}
	}

	buf := make([]byte, 256)
	for {
		n, err := resp.Body.Read(buf)
		if n > 0 {
			fmt.Print(string(buf[:n]))
		}
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("read stream: %w", err)
		}
	}
	fmt.Println()
	return nil
}
```
  

## Error handling

Define a custom error type and handle common status codes:

```go
type ApiError struct {
	StatusCode int
	Body       string
}

func (e *ApiError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("EAI API error %d: %s", e.StatusCode, e.Body)
}

func (e *ApiError) IsUnauthorized() bool { return e.StatusCode == 401 }
func (e *ApiError) IsNotFound() bool     { return e.StatusCode == 404 }
func (e *ApiError) IsRateLimited() bool  { return e.StatusCode == 429 }

// Usage with structured error handling
tasks, err := client.ListResources(ctx, "Task")
if err != nil {
	var apiErr *ApiError
	if errors.As(err, &apiErr) {
		switch {
		case apiErr.IsUnauthorized():
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.")
		case apiErr.IsRateLimited():
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Rate limited. Retrying after delay...")
			time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
			tasks, err = client.ListResources(ctx, "Task")
		default:
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "API error: %v\n", apiErr)
		}
	} else {
		log.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
	}
}
if tasks != nil {
	fmt.Printf("Found %d tasks\n", tasks.Total)
}
```

# Java Examples

These examples show how to call the EAI Platform API from Java 11+ using the built-in `java.net.http.HttpClient` and Jackson for JSON serialization.

  All examples assume you have `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and your access token available as environment variables. Run `eai env pull` to populate your `.env.local` file.

## Setup

```java
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;
import java.time.Duration;

public class EaiClient {

    private final HttpClient httpClient;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper;
    private final String baseUrl;
    private final String tenantId;
    private final String accessToken;

    public EaiClient(String baseUrl, String tenantId, String accessToken) {
        this.baseUrl = baseUrl;
        this.tenantId = tenantId;
        this.accessToken = accessToken;
        this.mapper = new ObjectMapper();
        this.httpClient = HttpClient.newBuilder()
            .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
            .build();
    }

    private JsonNode sendRequest(String method, String path, Object body) throws Exception {
        HttpRequest.Builder builder = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
            .uri(URI.create(baseUrl + path))
            .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken)
            .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30));

        if (body != null) {
            String json = mapper.writeValueAsString(body);
            builder.method(method, HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(json));
        } else {
            builder.method(method, HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.noBody());
        }

        HttpResponse<String> response = httpClient.send(
            builder.build(), HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());

        if (response.statusCode() >= 400) {
            throw new EaiApiException(response.statusCode(), response.body());
        }

        return response.body().isEmpty() ? null : mapper.readTree(response.body());
    }
}
```

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```java
public JsonNode getAuthenticatedUser() throws Exception {
    return sendRequest("GET", "/v3/auth/me", null);
}

public void provisionUser() throws Exception {
    sendRequest("POST", "/v3/users/provisionme", null);
}

// Usage
public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    String baseUrl = System.getenv("BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API");
    String tenantId = System.getenv("TENANT_ID");
    String token = System.getenv("EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN");

    EaiClient client = new EaiClient(baseUrl, tenantId, token);

    JsonNode me = client.getAuthenticatedUser();
    System.out.printf("Logged in as %s (%s)%n",
        me.get("displayName").asText(),
        me.get("email").asText());
}
```

```java
        "/v3/resources/" + tenantId + "/" + objectType, data);

public JsonNode listResources(String objectType) throws Exception {

}

public JsonNode updateResource(String objectType, String resourceId, Object data)
        throws Exception {
    return sendRequest("PUT",
        "/v3/resources/" + tenantId + "/" + objectType + "/" + resourceId, data);
}

public void deleteResource(String objectType, String resourceId) throws Exception {
    sendRequest("DELETE",
        "/v3/resources/" + tenantId + "/" + objectType + "/" + resourceId, null);
}
```

## Chat

Send a message to an AI workflow. Both blocking and streaming modes are supported:

  
```java
public JsonNode sendChatMessage(String workflowId, String stage, String message)
        throws Exception {
    return sendRequest("POST",
        "/v3/chat/" + tenantId + "/" + workflowId + "/" + stage,
        Map.of("message", message));
}

JsonNode reply = client.sendChatMessage("wf-123", "default", "Summarize open tasks");
System.out.println("AI: " + reply.get("message").asText());
```
  
  
```java
import java.net.http.HttpResponse.BodyHandlers;
import java.io.InputStream;

public void streamChat(String workflowId, String stage, String message)
        throws Exception {
    String path = "/v3/chat/stream/" + tenantId + "/" + workflowId + "/" + stage;
    String json = mapper.writeValueAsString(Map.of("message", message));

    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
        .uri(URI.create(baseUrl + path))
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken)
        .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(json))
        .build();

    HttpResponse<InputStream> response = httpClient.send(
        request, BodyHandlers.ofInputStream());

    if (response.statusCode() >= 400) {
        throw new EaiApiException(response.statusCode(), "Stream request failed");
    }

    try (InputStream stream = response.body()) {
        byte[] buffer = new byte[256];
        int bytesRead;
        while ((bytesRead = stream.read(buffer)) != -1) {
            System.out.print(new String(buffer, 0, bytesRead));
        }
    }

    System.out.println();
}

client.streamChat("wf-123", "default", "What is the project status?");
```
  
  
```java
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;

public CompletableFuture<JsonNode> sendChatMessageAsync(
        String workflowId, String stage, String message) {
    String path = "/v3/chat/" + tenantId + "/" + workflowId + "/" + stage;
    String json;
    try {
        json = mapper.writeValueAsString(Map.of("message", message));
    } catch (Exception e) {
        return CompletableFuture.failedFuture(e);
    }

    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
        .uri(URI.create(baseUrl + path))
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken)
        .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(json))
        .build();

    return httpClient.sendAsync(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())
        .thenApply(response -> {
            if (response.statusCode() >= 400) {
                throw new RuntimeException(
                    new EaiApiException(response.statusCode(), response.body()));
            }
            try {
                return mapper.readTree(response.body());
            } catch (Exception e) {
                throw new RuntimeException(e);
            }
        });
}

// Usage
client.sendChatMessageAsync("wf-123", "default", "Summarize open tasks")
    .thenAccept(reply -> System.out.println("AI: " + reply.get("message").asText()))
    .join();
```
  

## Error handling

Define a custom exception and handle common error codes:

```java
public class EaiApiException extends Exception {

    private final int statusCode;
    private final String responseBody;

    public EaiApiException(int statusCode, String responseBody) {
        super("EAI API error " + statusCode + ": " + responseBody);
        this.statusCode = statusCode;
        this.responseBody = responseBody;
    }

    public int getStatusCode() { return statusCode; }
    public String getResponseBody() { return responseBody; }
    public boolean isUnauthorized() { return statusCode == 401; }
    public boolean isNotFound() { return statusCode == 404; }
    public boolean isRateLimited() { return statusCode == 429; }
}

// Usage with structured error handling
try {
    JsonNode tasks = client.listResources("Task");
    System.out.printf("Found %d tasks%n", tasks.get("total").asInt());
} catch (EaiApiException ex) {
    if (ex.isUnauthorized()) {
        System.err.println("Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.");
    } else if (ex.isRateLimited()) {
        System.err.println("Rate limited. Retrying after delay...");
        Thread.sleep(2000);
        JsonNode tasks = client.listResources("Task");
        System.out.printf("Found %d tasks%n", tasks.get("total").asInt());
    } else {
        System.err.println("API error: " + ex.getMessage());
    }
}
```

# Python Examples

These examples demonstrate how to call the EAI Platform API from Python. Both synchronous (`requests`) and asynchronous (`httpx`) patterns are shown.

  All examples assume you have `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` and your access token available as environment variables. Run `eai env pull` to populate your `.env.local` file.

## Setup

  
```python
import os
import requests

BASE_URL = os.environ["BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API"]
TENANT_ID = os.environ["TENANT_ID"]
TOKEN = os.environ["EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN"]

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
})

def eai_request(method: str, path: str, json_body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Send a request to the EAI Platform API."""
    url = f"{BASE_URL}{path}"
    response = session.request(method, url, json=json_body)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json() if response.content else {}
```
  
  
```python
import os
import httpx

BASE_URL = os.environ["BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API"]
TENANT_ID = os.environ["TENANT_ID"]
TOKEN = os.environ["EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN"]

client = httpx.AsyncClient(
    base_url=BASE_URL,
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
)

async def eai_request(method: str, path: str, json_body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Send an async request to the EAI Platform API."""
    response = await client.request(method, path, json=json_body)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json() if response.content else {}
```
  

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```python
def get_authenticated_user() -> dict:
    """Fetch the current user's profile."""
    return eai_request("GET", "/v3/auth/me")

def provision_user() -> None:
    """Provision the current user on the platform."""
    eai_request("POST", "/v3/users/provisionme")

```

## Resource CRUD

Create, list, get, update, and delete resources:

```python

    """Create a new resource."""
    return eai_request("POST", f"/v3/resources/{TENANT_ID}/{object_type}", data)

def list_resources(object_type: str) -> dict:
    """List all resources of a given type."""
    return eai_request("GET", f"/v3/resources/{TENANT_ID}/{object_type}")

def get_resource(object_type: str, resource_id: str) -> dict:
    """Get a single resource by ID."""
    return eai_request("GET", f"/v3/resources/{TENANT_ID}/{object_type}/{resource_id}")

def update_resource(object_type: str, resource_id: str, data: dict) -> dict:
    """Update an existing resource."""
    return eai_request("PUT", f"/v3/resources/{TENANT_ID}/{object_type}/{resource_id}", data)

def delete_resource(object_type: str, resource_id: str) -> None:
    """Delete a resource."""
    eai_request("DELETE", f"/v3/resources/{TENANT_ID}/{object_type}/{resource_id}")
```

## Chat

Send a message to an AI workflow. Both blocking and streaming modes are supported:

  
```python
def send_chat_message(workflow_id: str, stage: str, message: str) -> dict:
    """Send a chat message and receive the full response."""
    return eai_request(
        "POST",
        f"/v3/chat/{TENANT_ID}/{workflow_id}/{stage}",
        {"message": message},
    )

reply = send_chat_message("wf-123", "default", "Summarize open tasks")
print(f"AI: {reply['message']}")
```
  
  
```python
def stream_chat(workflow_id: str, stage: str, message: str) -> None:
    """Stream a chat response token by token."""
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/v3/chat/stream/{TENANT_ID}/{workflow_id}/{stage}"
    with session.post(url, json={"message": message}, stream=True) as response:
        response.raise_for_status()
        for chunk in response.iter_content(decode_unicode=True):
            print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()  # Final newline

stream_chat("wf-123", "default", "What is the project status?")
```
  
  
```python
import httpx

async def stream_chat_async(workflow_id: str, stage: str, message: str) -> None:
    """Stream a chat response asynchronously."""
    url = f"/v3/chat/stream/{TENANT_ID}/{workflow_id}/{stage}"
    async with client.stream("POST", url, json={"message": message}) as response:
        response.raise_for_status()
        async for chunk in response.aiter_text():
            print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()

import asyncio
asyncio.run(stream_chat_async("wf-123", "default", "What is the project status?"))
```
  

## Error handling

Handle API errors with structured exception handling:

```python
import requests

class EaiApiError(Exception):
    """Structured error from the EAI Platform API."""

    def __init__(self, status_code: int, body: str):
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.body = body
        super().__init__(f"EAI API error {status_code}: {body}")

    @property
    def is_unauthorized(self) -> bool:
        return self.status_code == 401

    @property
    def is_not_found(self) -> bool:
        return self.status_code == 404

    @property
    def is_rate_limited(self) -> bool:
        return self.status_code == 429

def safe_request(method: str, path: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
    """Make an API call with structured error handling."""
    import time

    try:
        return eai_request(method, path, **kwargs)
    except requests.HTTPError as exc:
        status = exc.response.status_code
        body = exc.response.text
        error = EaiApiError(status, body)

        if error.is_unauthorized:
            print("Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.")
        elif error.is_rate_limited:
            print("Rate limited. Retrying after delay...")
            time.sleep(2)
            return eai_request(method, path, **kwargs)
        else:
            print(f"API error: {error}")

        raise error from exc

# Usage
result = safe_request("GET", f"/v3/resources/{TENANT_ID}/Task")
print(f"Found {result['total']} tasks")
```

# Rust Examples

These examples show how to call the EAI Platform API from Rust using `reqwest` for HTTP, `tokio` for async runtime, and `serde` for JSON serialization.

  Add the following to your `Cargo.toml` dependencies:

  ```toml
  [dependencies]
  reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }
  tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
  serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
  serde_json = "1"
  ```

## Setup

```rust
use reqwest::header::{HeaderMap, HeaderValue, AUTHORIZATION, CONTENT_TYPE};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::env;

pub struct EaiClient {
    http: reqwest::Client,
    base_url: String,
    tenant_id: String,
}

impl EaiClient {
    pub fn new() -> Result<Self, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        let token = env::var("EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN")?;
        let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
        headers.insert(
            AUTHORIZATION,
            HeaderValue::from_str(&format!("Bearer {}", token))?,
        );
        headers.insert(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"));

        let http = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .default_headers(headers)
            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30))
            .build()?;

        Ok(Self {
            http,
            base_url: env::var("BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API")?,
            tenant_id: env::var("TENANT_ID")?,
        })
    }

    fn url(&self, path: &str) -> String {
        format!("{}{}", self.base_url, path)
    }
}
```

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct UserProfile {
    pub id: String,
    pub email: String,
    pub display_name: String,
    pub roles: Vec<String>,
}

impl EaiClient {
    pub async fn get_authenticated_user(&self) -> Result<UserProfile, EaiError> {
        let resp = self.http.get(self.url("/v3/auth/me")).send().await?;
        let status = resp.status();
        if !status.is_success() {
            return Err(EaiError::Api {
                status: status.as_u16(),
                body: resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default(),
            });
        }
        Ok(resp.json().await?)
    }

    pub async fn provision_user(&self) -> Result<(), EaiError> {
        let resp = self.http.post(self.url("/v3/users/provisionme")).send().await?;
        if !resp.status().is_success() {
            return Err(EaiError::Api {
                status: resp.status().as_u16(),
                body: resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default(),
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// Usage
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let client = EaiClient::new()?;
    let user = client.get_authenticated_user().await?;
    println!("Logged in as {} ({})", user.display_name, user.email);
    Ok(())
}
```

## Resource CRUD

Create, list, get, update, and delete resources:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct Resource {
    pub id: String,
    pub object_type: String,
    pub data: serde_json::Value,
    pub created_at: String,
    pub updated_at: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ResourceList {
    pub items: Vec<Resource>,
    pub total: u64,
    pub page: u64,
    pub page_size: u64,
}

impl EaiClient {
    pub async fn create_resource(
        &self, object_type: &str, data: &serde_json::Value,
    ) -> Result<Resource, EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/resources/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, object_type);
        let resp = self.http.post(self.url(&path)).json(data).send().await?;
        Self::parse_response(resp).await
    }

    pub async fn list_resources(&self, object_type: &str) -> Result<ResourceList, EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/resources/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, object_type);
        let resp = self.http.get(self.url(&path)).send().await?;
        Self::parse_response(resp).await
    }

    pub async fn get_resource(
        &self, object_type: &str, resource_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<Resource, EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/resources/{}/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, object_type, resource_id);
        let resp = self.http.get(self.url(&path)).send().await?;
        Self::parse_response(resp).await
    }

    pub async fn update_resource(
        &self, object_type: &str, resource_id: &str, data: &serde_json::Value,
    ) -> Result<Resource, EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/resources/{}/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, object_type, resource_id);
        let resp = self.http.put(self.url(&path)).json(data).send().await?;
        Self::parse_response(resp).await
    }

    pub async fn delete_resource(
        &self, object_type: &str, resource_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/resources/{}/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, object_type, resource_id);
        let resp = self.http.delete(self.url(&path)).send().await?;
        if !resp.status().is_success() {
            return Err(EaiError::Api {
                status: resp.status().as_u16(),
                body: resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default(),
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn parse_response<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
        resp: reqwest::Response,
    ) -> Result<T, EaiError> {
        let status = resp.status();
        if !status.is_success() {
            return Err(EaiError::Api {
                status: status.as_u16(),
                body: resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default(),
            });
        }
        Ok(resp.json().await?)
    }
}
```

### Full CRUD workflow

```rust
use serde_json::json;

let task = client.create_resource("Task", &json!({
    "title": "Review pull request",
    "status": "open",
    "priority": "high"
})).await?;
println!("Created task {}", task.id);

let tasks = client.list_resources("Task").await?;
println!("Found {} tasks", tasks.total);

let fetched = client.get_resource("Task", &task.id).await?;
println!("Task title: {}", fetched.data["title"]);

let updated = client.update_resource("Task", &task.id, &json!({
    "title": "Review pull request",
    "status": "in-progress",
    "priority": "high"
})).await?;
println!("Updated status to {}", updated.data["status"]);

client.delete_resource("Task", &task.id).await?;
println!("Task deleted");
```

```rust
pub struct ObjectTypeSchema {
```
