## Chat

Send a message to an AI workflow:

  
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ChatResponse {
    pub message: String,
    pub conversation_id: String,
}

impl EaiClient {
    pub async fn send_chat_message(
        &self, workflow_id: &str, stage: &str, message: &str,
    ) -> Result<ChatResponse, EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/chat/{}/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, workflow_id, stage);
        let resp = self.http.post(self.url(&path))
            .json(&json!({"message": message}))
            .send().await?;
        Self::parse_response(resp).await
    }
}

let reply = client.send_chat_message("wf-123", "default", "Summarize open tasks").await?;
println!("AI: {}", reply.message);
```
  
  
```rust
use futures_util::StreamExt;

impl EaiClient {
    pub async fn stream_chat(
        &self, workflow_id: &str, stage: &str, message: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), EaiError> {
        let path = format!("/v3/chat/stream/{}/{}/{}", self.tenant_id, workflow_id, stage);
        let resp = self.http.post(self.url(&path))
            .json(&json!({"message": message}))
            .send().await?;

        if !resp.status().is_success() {
            return Err(EaiError::Api {
                status: resp.status().as_u16(),
                body: resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default(),
            });
        }

        let mut stream = resp.bytes_stream();
        while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
            let bytes = chunk.map_err(EaiError::Http)?;
            print!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes));
        }
        println!();
        Ok(())
    }
}

client.stream_chat("wf-123", "default", "What is the project status?").await?;
```
  

## Error handling

Define a custom error enum and handle common status codes:

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum EaiError {
    Http(reqwest::Error),
    Api { status: u16, body: String },
}

impl std::fmt::Display for EaiError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            EaiError::Http(e) => write!(f, "HTTP error: {}", e),
            EaiError::Api { status, body } => write!(f, "EAI API error {}: {}", status, body),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for EaiError {}

impl From<reqwest::Error> for EaiError {
    fn from(err: reqwest::Error) -> Self {
        EaiError::Http(err)
    }
}

impl EaiError {
    pub fn is_unauthorized(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, EaiError::Api { status: 401, .. })
    }
    pub fn is_not_found(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, EaiError::Api { status: 404, .. })
    }
    pub fn is_rate_limited(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, EaiError::Api { status: 429, .. })
    }
}

// Usage
match client.list_resources("Task").await {
    Ok(tasks) => println!("Found {} tasks", tasks.total),
    Err(ref e) if e.is_unauthorized() => {
        eprintln!("Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.");
    }
    Err(ref e) if e.is_rate_limited() => {
        eprintln!("Rate limited. Retrying after delay...");
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
        let tasks = client.list_resources("Task").await?;
        println!("Found {} tasks", tasks.total);
    }
    Err(e) => eprintln!("API error: {}", e),
}
```

# Shell Examples

These examples show how to call the EAI Platform API directly from the command line using `curl` and `jq`. They work in any Bash-compatible shell.

  All examples assume you have `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` set in your environment and a valid access token. Run `eai env pull` to populate your `.env.local` and `eai login` to authenticate.

## Setup

Export your environment variables before running any commands:

```bash
export BASE_URL="${BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API}"
export TENANT_ID="your-tenant-id"
export TOKEN="your-access-token"
```

You can source these from your `.env.local` file:

```bash
# Load variables from .env.local
set -a
source .env.local
set +a

export BASE_URL="${BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API}"
export TOKEN="${EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

Define a reusable helper function for authenticated requests:

```bash
eai_request() {
  local method="$1"
  local path="$2"
  local data="$3"

  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    curl -s -X "$method" \
      "${BASE_URL}${path}" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "$data"
  else
    curl -s -X "$method" \
      "${BASE_URL}${path}" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  fi
}
```

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```bash
# Get the authenticated user profile
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" | jq .

# Extract specific fields
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  | jq '{name: .displayName, email: .email, roles: .roles}'

# Provision the current user
curl -s -X POST "${BASE_URL}/v3/users/provisionme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

One-liner to verify you are logged in:

```bash
curl -sf "${BASE_URL}/v3/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  | jq -r '"Logged in as \(.displayName) (\(.email))"'
```

## Resource CRUD

Create, list, get, update, and delete resources using curl:

### Create a resource

```bash
curl -s -X POST "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Review pull request",
    "status": "open",
    "priority": "high"
  }' | jq .
```

Store the created resource ID in a variable for subsequent operations:

```bash
TASK_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title": "Review pull request", "status": "open", "priority": "high"}' \
  | jq -r '.id')

echo "Created task: ${TASK_ID}"
```

### List resources

```bash
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  | jq '.items[] | {id: .id, title: .data.title, status: .data.status}'
```

### Get a single resource

```bash
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/${TASK_ID}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" | jq .
```

### Update a resource

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/${TASK_ID}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Review pull request",
    "status": "in-progress",
    "priority": "high"
  }' | jq .
```

### Delete a resource

```bash
curl -s -X DELETE "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/${TASK_ID}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}"

echo "Task ${TASK_ID} deleted"
```

### Full CRUD script

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Create
echo "Creating task..."
TASK_ID=$(eai_request POST "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task" \
  '{"title": "Review pull request", "status": "open", "priority": "high"}' \
  | jq -r '.id')
echo "Created: ${TASK_ID}"

# List
echo "Listing tasks..."
TOTAL=$(eai_request GET "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task" | jq '.total')
echo "Found ${TOTAL} tasks"

# Get
echo "Fetching task..."
TITLE=$(eai_request GET "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/${TASK_ID}" \
  | jq -r '.data.title')
echo "Title: ${TITLE}"

# Update
echo "Updating task..."
eai_request PUT "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/${TASK_ID}" \
  '{"title": "Review pull request", "status": "in-progress", "priority": "high"}' \
  | jq '.data.status'

# Delete
echo "Deleting task..."
eai_request DELETE "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/${TASK_ID}"
echo "Done"
```

## Querying resources

Fetch the tenant schema and inspect available object types:

```bash
# List all object type names
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/schema/${TENANT_ID}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  | jq -r '.objectTypes[].name'

# Get full schema details for a specific type
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/schema/${TENANT_ID}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  | jq '.objectTypes[] | select(.name == "Task")'

# Count properties per object type
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v3/resources/schema/${TENANT_ID}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  | jq '.objectTypes[] | {name: .name, propertyCount: (.properties | length)}'
```

## Chat

Send a message to an AI workflow:

  
```bash
WORKFLOW_ID="wf-123"
STAGE="default"

# Send a chat message and get the full response
curl -s -X POST \
  "${BASE_URL}/v3/chat/${TENANT_ID}/${WORKFLOW_ID}/${STAGE}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Summarize open tasks"}' \
  | jq -r '.message'
```
  
  
```bash
WORKFLOW_ID="wf-123"
STAGE="default"

# Stream a chat response to stdout in real time
curl -sN -X POST \
  "${BASE_URL}/v3/chat/stream/${TENANT_ID}/${WORKFLOW_ID}/${STAGE}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "What is the project status?"}'
```
  
  
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

WORKFLOW_ID="wf-123"
STAGE="default"

echo "EAI Chat (type 'exit' to quit)"
echo "---"

while true; do
  printf "> "
  read -r user_input

  if [ "$user_input" = "exit" ]; then
    echo "Goodbye."
    break
  fi

  PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --arg msg "$user_input" '{"message": $msg}')

  REPLY=$(curl -s -X POST \
    "${BASE_URL}/v3/chat/${TENANT_ID}/${WORKFLOW_ID}/${STAGE}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$PAYLOAD" \
    | jq -r '.message')

  echo "AI: ${REPLY}"
  echo ""
done
```
  

## Error handling

Check HTTP status codes and handle errors in shell scripts:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

eai_safe_request() {
  local method="$1"
  local path="$2"
  local data="${3:-}"

  local http_code body
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X "$method" \
      "${BASE_URL}${path}" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "$data")
  else
    response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X "$method" \
      "${BASE_URL}${path}" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json")
  fi

  http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
  body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d')

  case "$http_code" in
    2*)
      echo "$body"
      ;;
    401)
      echo "Error: Token expired. Run 'eai login' to re-authenticate." >&2
      return 1
      ;;
    404)
      echo "Error: Resource not found." >&2
      return 1
      ;;
    429)
      echo "Warning: Rate limited. Retrying in 2 seconds..." >&2
      sleep 2
      eai_safe_request "$method" "$path" "$data"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Error: API returned HTTP ${http_code}" >&2
      echo "$body" | jq . >&2 2>/dev/null || echo "$body" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

# Usage
eai_safe_request GET "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task" | jq '.total'
eai_safe_request GET "/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/Task/nonexistent-id"
```

# TypeScript Examples

These examples show how to interact with the EAI Platform API from TypeScript using the native `fetch` API. Every request requires a Bearer token obtained through the Entra CIAM device code flow.

  All examples assume you have `BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API` set in your environment. Run `eai env pull` to populate your `.env.local` file.

## Setup

```typescript
const BASE_URL = process.env.BASE_URL_PUBLIC_API!;
const TENANT_ID = process.env.TENANT_ID!;
const TOKEN = process.env.EAI_ACCESS_TOKEN!;

interface RequestOptions {
  method?: string;
  body?: unknown;
}

async function eaiFetch<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
    method: options.method ?? "GET",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: options.body ? JSON.stringify(options.body) : undefined,
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorBody = await response.text();
    throw new Error(`API error ${response.status}: ${errorBody}`);
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<T>;
}
```

## Authentication

Verify your token and retrieve your user profile:

```typescript
interface UserProfile {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  displayName: string;
  roles: string[];
}

async function getAuthenticatedUser(): Promise<UserProfile> {
  return eaiFetch<UserProfile>("/v3/auth/me");
}

async function provisionUser(): Promise<void> {
  await eaiFetch<void>("/v3/users/provisionme", { method: "POST" });
}

// Usage
const me = await getAuthenticatedUser();
console.log(`Logged in as ${me.displayName} (${me.email})`);
```

## Resource CRUD

Define types for your resources and perform create, read, update, list, and delete operations:

```typescript
interface Resource {
  id: string;
  objectType: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}

interface ResourceList {
  items: Resource[];
  total: number;
  page: number;
  pageSize: number;
}

// Create a resource
async function createResource(objectType: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<Resource> {
  return eaiFetch<Resource>(`/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/${objectType}`, {
    method: "POST",
    body: data,
  });
}

// List resources of a given type
async function listResources(objectType: string): Promise<ResourceList> {
  return eaiFetch<ResourceList>(`/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/${objectType}`);
}

// Get a single resource by ID
async function getResource(objectType: string, resourceId: string): Promise<Resource> {
  return eaiFetch<Resource>(`/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/${objectType}/${resourceId}`);
}

// Update a resource
async function updateResource(
  objectType: string,
  resourceId: string,
  data: Record<string, unknown>,
): Promise<Resource> {
  return eaiFetch<Resource>(`/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/${objectType}/${resourceId}`, {
    method: "PUT",
    body: data,
  });
}

// Delete a resource
async function deleteResource(objectType: string, resourceId: string): Promise<void> {
  await eaiFetch<void>(`/v3/resources/${TENANT_ID}/${objectType}/${resourceId}`, {
    method: "DELETE",
  });
}
```

### Full CRUD workflow

```typescript
// Create
const task = await createResource("Task", {
  title: "Review pull request",
  status: "open",
  priority: "high",
});
console.log(`Created task ${task.id}`);

// List
const tasks = await listResources("Task");
console.log(`Found ${tasks.total} tasks`);

// Get
const fetched = await getResource("Task", task.id);
console.log(`Task title: ${fetched.data.title}`);

// Update
const updated = await updateResource("Task", task.id, {
  ...fetched.data,
  status: "in-progress",
});
console.log(`Updated status to ${updated.data.status}`);

// Delete
await deleteResource("Task", task.id);
console.log("Task deleted");
```

## Querying resources

Fetch the schema for a tenant and filter resources with query parameters:

```typescript
interface SchemaResponse {
  objectTypes: Array<{ name: string; properties: unknown[] }>;
}

async function getSchema(): Promise<SchemaResponse> {
  return eaiFetch<SchemaResponse>(`/v3/resources/schema/${TENANT_ID}`);
}

const schema = await getSchema();
console.log("Available object types:", schema.objectTypes.map((ot) => ot.name));
```

## Chat

Send a message to an AI workflow and receive a response. Both blocking and streaming modes are supported:

  
```typescript
interface ChatResponse {
  message: string;
  conversationId: string;
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

async function sendChatMessage(
  workflowId: string,
  stage: string,
  message: string,
): Promise<ChatResponse> {
  return eaiFetch<ChatResponse>(`/v3/chat/${TENANT_ID}/${workflowId}/${stage}`, {
    method: "POST",
    body: { message },
  });
}

const reply = await sendChatMessage("wf-123", "default", "Summarize open tasks");
console.log("AI:", reply.message);
```
  
  
```typescript
async function streamChat(
  workflowId: string,
  stage: string,
  message: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const response = await fetch(
    `${BASE_URL}/v3/chat/stream/${TENANT_ID}/${workflowId}/${stage}`,
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ message }),
    },
  );

  if (!response.ok || !response.body) {
    throw new Error(`Stream error: ${response.status}`);
  }

  const reader = response.body.getReader();
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();

  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    process.stdout.write(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true }));
  }

  console.log(); // Final newline
}

await streamChat("wf-123", "default", "What is the project status?");
```
  

## Error handling

Wrap API calls with structured error handling:

```typescript
class EaiApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly status: number,
    public readonly body: string,
  ) {
    super(`EAI API error ${status}: ${body}`);
    this.name = "EaiApiError";
  }

  get isUnauthorized(): boolean {
    return this.status === 401;
  }

  get isNotFound(): boolean {
    return this.status === 404;
  }

  get isRateLimited(): boolean {
    return this.status === 429;
  }
}

async function safeRequest<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  try {
    return await fn();
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof EaiApiError) {
      if (error.isUnauthorized) {
        console.error("Token expired. Run `eai login` to re-authenticate.");
      } else if (error.isRateLimited) {
        console.error("Rate limited. Retrying after delay...");
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
        return fn();
      } else {
        console.error(`API error: ${error.message}`);
      }
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

// Usage
const result = await safeRequest(() => listResources("Task"));
console.log(`Found ${result.total} tasks`);
```

# Accreditation

## Persona

**Role:** Accreditation Coordinator at a regional university.

You manage the institution's accreditation processes across multiple accrediting bodies -- regional, programmatic, and specialized. Each body defines standards that the university must demonstrate compliance with, and evidence must be collected, organized, and submitted on multi-year cycles. The last accreditation cycle involved hundreds of documents scattered across departments with no centralized tracking.

## Business Problem

Standards from different accrediting bodies are tracked in separate spreadsheets maintained by different offices. Evidence documents are stored in department-level shared drives, and there is no reliable way to confirm which standards have sufficient evidence and which have gaps. Accreditation reports are assembled manually in the months before a visit, creating a crisis-mode atmosphere. You need:

- A centralized standard registry organized by accrediting body and category.
- Evidence tracking linked to specific standards with submission dates.
- Report generation that aggregates compliance status and findings by period.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Standard** | body, code, description, category | has many Evidences | create, update, retire |
| **Evidence** | standard, document, description, submittedDate | belongs to Standard | upload, review, accept, reject |
| **AccreditationReport** | body, period, status, findings | links to Standards | generate, submit, revise |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init accreditation
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add Standard, Evidence, and AccreditationReport to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: accreditation
   ✔ Standard — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ Evidence — 4 props, 1 link, 4 actions
   ✔ AccreditationReport — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Create a standard**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Standard \
     --data '{"body": "HLC", "code": "5.B.1", "description": "The institution has a well-developed process for budgeting and financial planning", "category": "resources"}'
   ```

6. **Upload evidence**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Evidence \
     --data '{"standard": "std-5b1", "document": "/evidence/budget-process-2026.pdf", "description": "Annual budget planning process documentation", "submittedDate": "2026-02-15"}'
   ```

7. **List standards missing evidence**

   ```bash
   eai resources list Standard --filter 'category=resources'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'accreditation': [
    {
      name: 'Standard',
      displayName: 'Standard',
      description: 'An accreditation standard defined by an accrediting body that the institution must demonstrate compliance with',
      properties: [
        { name: 'body', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'HLC', value: 'hlc' },
            { label: 'ABET', value: 'abet' },
            { label: 'AACSB', value: 'aacsb' },
            { label: 'NCATE', value: 'ncate' },
            { label: 'ABA', value: 'aba' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'code', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'category', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Mission', value: 'mission' },
            { label: 'Integrity', value: 'integrity' },
            { label: 'Teaching & Learning', value: 'teaching-learning' },
            { label: 'Resources', value: 'resources' },
            { label: 'Institutional Effectiveness', value: 'institutional-effectiveness' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'evidences', target: 'Evidence', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'create', displayName: 'Create Standard' },
        { name: 'update', displayName: 'Update Standard' },
        { name: 'retire', displayName: 'Retire Standard' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Evidence',
      displayName: 'Evidence',
      description: 'A document or artifact submitted as evidence of compliance with an accreditation standard',
      properties: [
        { name: 'standard', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'document', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'submittedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'standard', target: 'Standard', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'upload', displayName: 'Upload Evidence' },
        { name: 'review', displayName: 'Review Evidence' },
        { name: 'accept', displayName: 'Accept Evidence' },
        { name: 'reject', displayName: 'Reject Evidence' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'AccreditationReport',
      displayName: 'Accreditation Report',
      description: 'A formal report submitted to an accrediting body summarizing compliance status and findings',
      properties: [
        { name: 'body', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'HLC', value: 'hlc' },
            { label: 'ABET', value: 'abet' },
            { label: 'AACSB', value: 'aacsb' },
            { label: 'NCATE', value: 'ncate' },
            { label: 'ABA', value: 'aba' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'period', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft',
          options: [
            { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
            { label: 'In Review', value: 'in-review' },
            { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
            { label: 'Accepted', value: 'accepted' },
            { label: 'Revision Required', value: 'revision-required' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'findings', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'standards', target: 'Standard', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'generate', displayName: 'Generate Report' },
        { name: 'submit', displayName: 'Submit Report' },
        { name: 'revise', displayName: 'Revise Report' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Multi-body standard tracking eliminates silos.** A single registry covers HLC, ABET, AACSB, and other bodies, giving the accreditation coordinator a unified compliance view.
- **Evidence linked to standards reveals gaps early.** Filtering standards by category and checking linked evidence surfaces compliance gaps months before a site visit, not weeks.
- **Report lifecycle prevents last-minute scrambles.** Structured report statuses -- from draft through submission -- enforce a review process that spreads the workload over the full accreditation cycle.
- **Category-based organization mirrors accreditor expectations.** Grouping standards by category (mission, teaching and learning, resources) aligns the internal tracking system with how accrediting bodies structure their evaluations.

# Admissions Portal

## Persona

**Role:** Director of Admissions Technology at a private university.

You oversee the technology stack supporting the admissions office, which processes 12,000 applications annually across undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. Each application involves document collection, committee review, and a final decision with potential conditions. The existing portal is aging and cannot accommodate new program types without extensive custom development.

## Business Problem

Applications arrive through a web portal, but supporting documents -- transcripts, recommendation letters, test scores -- are uploaded to a separate file share with no automated link to the application. Committee members review applications in a spreadsheet, and decisions are communicated via mail merge. There is no single view of an application's completeness or decision status. You need:

- A unified application record with program and term tracking.
- Document management linked to applications with verification status.
- Structured decision records that capture committee outcomes and conditions.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Application** | applicant, program, term, status | has many Documents, has one Decision | submit, review, request-info |
| **Document** | application, type, fileUrl, verified | belongs to Application | upload, verify, reject |
| **Decision** | application, committee, outcome, conditions | belongs to Application | recommend, approve, deny, defer |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init admissions-portal
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add Application, Document, and Decision to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: admissions-portal
   ✔ Application — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ Document — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ Decision — 4 props, 1 link, 4 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Create an application**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Application \
     --data '{"applicant": "jordan.lee@email.com", "program": "ms-data-science", "term": "Fall 2026", "status": "submitted"}'
   ```

6. **Upload a document record**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Document \
     --data '{"application": "app-001", "type": "transcript", "fileUrl": "/uploads/transcript-jordan-lee.pdf", "verified": false}'
   ```

7. **List applications by program**

   ```bash
   eai resources list Application --filter 'program=ms-data-science'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript

        { name: 'program', type: 'select' as const, required: true,

            { label: 'BS Computer Science', value: 'bs-computer-science' },
            { label: 'MS Data Science', value: 'ms-data-science' },

            { label: 'JD', value: 'jd' },

          ],

        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft',
          options: [
            { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
            { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
            { label: 'Complete', value: 'complete' },
            { label: 'Under Review', value: 'under-review' },
            { label: 'Decision Made', value: 'decision-made' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'documents', target: 'Document', cardinality: 'many' as const },
        { name: 'decision', target: 'Decision', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'submit', displayName: 'Submit Application' },
        { name: 'review', displayName: 'Begin Review' },
        { name: 'request-info', displayName: 'Request Additional Info' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Document',
      displayName: 'Document',
      description: 'A supporting document uploaded as part of an admissions application',
      properties: [
        { name: 'application', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Transcript', value: 'transcript' },
            { label: 'Recommendation Letter', value: 'recommendation' },
            { label: 'Personal Statement', value: 'personal-statement' },
            { label: 'Test Score', value: 'test-score' },
            { label: 'Resume', value: 'resume' },
            { label: 'Portfolio', value: 'portfolio' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'fileUrl', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'verified', type: 'boolean' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'application', target: 'Application', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'upload', displayName: 'Upload Document' },
        { name: 'verify', displayName: 'Verify Document' },
        { name: 'reject', displayName: 'Reject Document' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Decision',
      displayName: 'Decision',
      description: 'The admissions committee decision for a specific application',
      properties: [
        { name: 'application', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'committee', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'outcome', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Admit', value: 'admit' },
            { label: 'Admit with Conditions', value: 'admit-conditions' },
            { label: 'Waitlist', value: 'waitlist' },
            { label: 'Deny', value: 'deny' },
            { label: 'Defer', value: 'defer' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'conditions', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'application', target: 'Application', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'recommend', displayName: 'Recommend Decision' },
        { name: 'approve', displayName: 'Approve Admission' },
        { name: 'deny', displayName: 'Deny Admission' },
        { name: 'defer', displayName: 'Defer Decision' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Document completeness tracking prevents review delays.** Linking Documents to Applications with a verified flag lets the admissions office quickly identify incomplete applications before sending them to committee.
- **Program-specific filtering streamlines committee work.** Committee members can filter applications by program and term, focusing their review on the relevant applicant pool.
- **Conditional admissions are first-class records.** The Decision type captures conditions alongside outcomes, ensuring that conditional admits receive appropriate follow-up.
- **Unified application lifecycle.** From draft through submission to decision, every stage is captured in structured status fields, giving leadership real-time visibility into pipeline health.

# Course Management

## Persona

**Role:** Registrar Systems Administrator at a mid-sized university.

You maintain the systems that power course registration, enrollment management, and grade recording for 8,000 students across six academic departments. The current system is a decades-old platform that requires vendor support for even minor catalog changes. Faculty submit grades via email, and enrollment conflicts are resolved manually.

## Business Problem

Course catalog updates require a multi-week change request process with the legacy vendor. Faculty have no self-service access to enrollment rosters, and grade submission is a manual data entry process that introduces transcription errors. Students cannot see real-time enrollment availability. You need:

- A self-managed course catalog with department, credits, and instructor metadata.
- Enrollment tracking with semester-based status management.
- Grade recording linked to specific enrollments with feedback support.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Course** | name, code, department, credits, instructor | has many Enrollments | create, update, archive |
| **Enrollment** | student, course, semester, status | belongs to Course, has many Grades | enroll, drop, complete |
| **Grade** | enrollment, assignment, score, feedback | belongs to Enrollment | submit, update, finalize |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init course-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add Course, Enrollment, and Grade to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: course-management
   ✔ Course — 5 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ Enrollment — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ Grade — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Create a course**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Course \
     --data '{"name": "Introduction to Data Science", "code": "CS-201", "department": "computer-science", "credits": 3, "instructor": "Dr. Sarah Chen"}'
   ```

6. **Enroll a student**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Enrollment \
     --data '{"student": "alex.rivera@university.edu", "course": "CS-201", "semester": "Fall 2026", "status": "enrolled"}'
   ```

7. **List enrollments for a semester**

   ```bash
   eai resources list Enrollment --filter 'semester=Fall 2026'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript

      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'course', target: 'Course', cardinality: 'one' as const },
        { name: 'grades', target: 'Grade', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],

        { name: 'drop', displayName: 'Drop Course' },
        { name: 'complete', displayName: 'Mark Complete' },

      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Grade',
      displayName: 'Grade',
      description: 'A grade recorded for a specific assignment within an enrollment',
      properties: [
        { name: 'enrollment', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'assignment', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'score', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'feedback', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'enrollment', target: 'Enrollment', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'submit', displayName: 'Submit Grade' },
        { name: 'update', displayName: 'Update Grade' },
        { name: 'finalize', displayName: 'Finalize Grade' },

      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Self-managed course catalog eliminates vendor dependency.** Adding, updating, or archiving courses is a direct CLI operation, not a multi-week vendor change request.
- **Semester-scoped enrollments prevent data conflicts.** Tracking enrollments by semester ensures that historical records remain intact while new terms are managed independently.
- **Assignment-level grade recording reduces errors.** Capturing grades per assignment with feedback fields replaces bulk email submissions and manual data entry.
- **Department-based filtering supports academic reporting.** The department property on Courses enables registrar reports broken down by academic unit for accreditation and planning.

# Learning Analytics

## Persona

**Role:** Director of Student Success at a community college.

You lead a team of academic advisors responsible for identifying at-risk students and coordinating interventions. The college serves 15,000 students, and early intervention has been shown to improve retention rates by up to 20 percent. However, your team currently relies on midterm grade reports and instructor referrals -- both of which arrive too late for many students.

## Business Problem

Student performance data is locked inside the learning management system with no structured export. Advisors learn about struggling students only after midterm grades are posted, by which point some students have already disengaged. Interventions are tracked in advisor notebooks with no central record of what was tried or whether it worked. You need:

- Continuous performance tracking with configurable risk-level indicators.
- Structured intervention records with type, assignment, and status tracking.
- Outcome measurement that links interventions to measurable results.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **StudentPerformance** | student, course, metrics, riskLevel | has many Interventions | assess, flag-risk, clear-risk |
| **Intervention** | student, type, assignedTo, status | belongs to StudentPerformance, has one Outcome | create, assign, close |
| **Outcome** | intervention, result, followUpDate | belongs to Intervention | record, review, archive |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init learning-analytics
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add StudentPerformance, Intervention, and Outcome to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: learning-analytics
   ✔ StudentPerformance — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ Intervention — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ Outcome — 3 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Record a student performance entry**

   ```bash
   eai resources create StudentPerformance \
     --data '{"student": "taylor.nguyen@college.edu", "course": "MATH-101", "metrics": "attendance: 65%, assignments: 3/8 submitted", "riskLevel": "high"}'
   ```

6. **Create an intervention**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Intervention \
     --data '{"student": "taylor.nguyen@college.edu", "type": "advising-session", "assignedTo": "advisor.jones@college.edu", "status": "scheduled"}'
   ```

7. **List high-risk students**

   ```bash
   eai resources list StudentPerformance --filter 'riskLevel=high'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript

        { name: 'metrics', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'riskLevel', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'low',
          options: [
            { label: 'Low', value: 'low' },
            { label: 'Medium', value: 'medium' },
            { label: 'High', value: 'high' },
            { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'interventions', target: 'Intervention', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'assess', displayName: 'Assess Performance' },
        { name: 'flag-risk', displayName: 'Flag At-Risk' },
        { name: 'clear-risk', displayName: 'Clear Risk Flag' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Intervention',
      displayName: 'Intervention',
      description: 'An academic support action taken for an at-risk student',
      properties: [
        { name: 'student', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Advising Session', value: 'advising-session' },
            { label: 'Tutoring Referral', value: 'tutoring-referral' },
            { label: 'Peer Mentoring', value: 'peer-mentoring' },
            { label: 'Financial Aid Review', value: 'financial-aid-review' },
            { label: 'Wellness Referral', value: 'wellness-referral' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'assignedTo', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'scheduled',
          options: [
            { label: 'Scheduled', value: 'scheduled' },
            { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
            { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
            { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
            { label: 'No Show', value: 'no-show' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'studentPerformance', target: 'StudentPerformance', cardinality: 'one' as const },
        { name: 'outcome', target: 'Outcome', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'create', displayName: 'Create Intervention' },
        { name: 'assign', displayName: 'Assign Advisor' },
        { name: 'close', displayName: 'Close Intervention' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Outcome',
      displayName: 'Outcome',
      description: 'The measured result of an intervention with follow-up tracking',
      properties: [
        { name: 'intervention', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'result', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Improved', value: 'improved' },
            { label: 'No Change', value: 'no-change' },
            { label: 'Declined', value: 'declined' },
            { label: 'Withdrawn', value: 'withdrawn' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'followUpDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'intervention', target: 'Intervention', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'record', displayName: 'Record Outcome' },
        { name: 'review', displayName: 'Review Outcome' },
        { name: 'archive', displayName: 'Archive Outcome' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Early risk detection saves students.** Configurable risk levels on StudentPerformance records allow advisors to intervene weeks before midterm grades are posted.
- **Intervention type diversity addresses root causes.** Structured intervention types -- from tutoring to wellness referrals -- ensure that advisors match the right support to each student's situation.
- **Outcome measurement proves program effectiveness.** Linking Outcomes to Interventions creates the evidence base needed to justify funding and scale successful programs.
- **Follow-up tracking prevents students from slipping back.** The followUpDate on Outcomes ensures that improved students continue to receive attention until they are stable.

# Research Grants

## Persona

**Role:** Research Administration Officer at a research university.

You support faculty across 12 departments in preparing grant proposals, managing awarded funds, and ensuring compliance with sponsor requirements. The university submits over 300 proposals per year to federal agencies, foundations, and industry partners. Each awarded grant comes with its own budget structure, reporting requirements, and spending rules.

## Business Problem

Proposal tracking is fragmented -- principal investigators (PIs) manage their own submissions in personal spreadsheets, and the grants office learns about awards only when PIs forward notification emails. Budget tracking for active awards is done in a separate financial system that is not linked to the original proposal. Spending overruns on individual budget categories go undetected until quarterly reconciliation. You need:

- A centralized proposal registry with PI, agency, and status tracking.
- Award records linked to funded proposals with start and end dates.
- Budget items that track allocated versus spent amounts by category.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Proposal** | title, pi, agency, amount, status | has one Award | submit, revise, withdraw |
| **Award** | proposal, amount, startDate, endDate | belongs to Proposal, has many BudgetItems | activate, extend, close |
| **BudgetItem** | award, category, allocated, spent | belongs to Award | allocate, spend, reallocate |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init research-grants
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add Proposal, Award, and BudgetItem to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: research-grants
   ✔ Proposal — 5 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ Award — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ BudgetItem — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Create a proposal**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Proposal \
     --data '{"title": "Machine Learning for Climate Modeling", "pi": "Dr. Elena Vasquez", "agency": "nsf", "amount": 450000, "status": "submitted"}'
   ```

6. **Record an award**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Award \
     --data '{"proposal": "prop-001", "amount": 450000, "startDate": "2026-09-01", "endDate": "2029-08-31"}'
   ```

7. **Add a budget item**

   ```bash
   eai resources create BudgetItem \
     --data '{"award": "award-001", "category": "personnel", "allocated": 280000, "spent": 0}'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'research-grants': [
    {
      name: 'Proposal',
      displayName: 'Proposal',
      description: 'A research grant proposal submitted by a principal investigator to a funding agency',
      properties: [
        { name: 'title', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'pi', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'agency', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'NSF', value: 'nsf' },
            { label: 'NIH', value: 'nih' },
            { label: 'DOE', value: 'doe' },
            { label: 'DARPA', value: 'darpa' },
            { label: 'Foundation', value: 'foundation' },
            { label: 'Industry', value: 'industry' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft',
          options: [
            { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
            { label: 'Internal Review', value: 'internal-review' },
            { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
            { label: 'Under Review', value: 'under-review' },
            { label: 'Funded', value: 'funded' },
            { label: 'Declined', value: 'declined' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'award', target: 'Award', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'submit', displayName: 'Submit Proposal' },
        { name: 'revise', displayName: 'Revise Proposal' },
        { name: 'withdraw', displayName: 'Withdraw Proposal' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Award',
      displayName: 'Award',
      description: 'A funded research award linked to an approved proposal with a defined project period',
      properties: [
        { name: 'proposal', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'startDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'endDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'proposal', target: 'Proposal', cardinality: 'one' as const },
        { name: 'budgetItems', target: 'BudgetItem', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'activate', displayName: 'Activate Award' },
        { name: 'extend', displayName: 'Extend Award' },
        { name: 'close', displayName: 'Close Award' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'BudgetItem',
      displayName: 'Budget Item',
      description: 'A budget line item within a research award tracking allocated versus spent funds',
      properties: [
        { name: 'award', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'category', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Personnel', value: 'personnel' },
            { label: 'Equipment', value: 'equipment' },
            { label: 'Travel', value: 'travel' },
            { label: 'Supplies', value: 'supplies' },
            { label: 'Subcontracts', value: 'subcontracts' },
            { label: 'Indirect Costs', value: 'indirect-costs' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'allocated', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'spent', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'award', target: 'Award', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'allocate', displayName: 'Allocate Budget' },
        { name: 'spend', displayName: 'Record Spending' },
        { name: 'reallocate', displayName: 'Reallocate Funds' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Centralized proposal tracking improves institutional visibility.** The grants office can see all proposals across departments, enabling better resource allocation and avoiding duplicate submissions to the same program.
- **Award-to-proposal linking maintains the funding trail.** Every Award traces back to its originating Proposal, making it easy to compile success rates by PI, department, or funding agency.
- **Category-level budget monitoring catches overruns early.** Tracking allocated versus spent amounts on each BudgetItem allows administrators to flag spending issues before they escalate to sponsor audit findings.
- **Agency-based filtering supports compliance.** Different funding agencies have different reporting and spending rules; filtering by agency helps the grants office apply the correct compliance framework to each award.

# Insurance Claims

## Persona

**Role**: Full-stack developer at an insurtech company (250 employees) building a claims management platform for property and casualty insurers.

Each insurance carrier is onboarded as a separate tenant, maintaining independent claims data, adjuster assignments, and payment records. The platform must handle high claim volumes during catastrophic events while keeping carrier data strictly separated.

## Business Problem

Insurance claims processing involves multiple handoffs -- initial filing, documentation review, adjuster assignment, damage assessment, and payment authorization. When these steps live in separate systems, claims languish in queues, policyholders wait weeks for updates, and adjusters duplicate effort reviewing the same documentation. This scenario builds a unified claims pipeline from submission through payment.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Claim** | `policyNumber` (text), `type` (select: auto, property, liability, health), `amount` (number), `description` (text), `status` (select: filed, under-review, approved, denied, paid) | one-to-many → Adjudication, one-to-many → Payment | `fileClaim` |
| **Adjudication** | `adjuster` (text), `decision` (select: approve, deny, request-info), `approvedAmount` (number), `reasoning` (text), `reviewDate` (date) | many-to-one → Claim | `submitDecision` |
| **Payment** | `amount` (number), `method` (select: ach, check, direct-repair), `processedDate` (date), `status` (select: pending, processed, returned), `payee` (text) | many-to-one → Claim | `processPayment` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init insurance-claims
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Claim, Adjudication, and Payment types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: insurance-claims
   ✔ Claim — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Adjudication — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Payment — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create a sample claim**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Claim --data '{"policyNumber": "POL-2026-44821", "type": "property", "amount": 12500, "description": "Water damage from burst pipe in basement, affecting drywall and flooring", "status": "filed"}'
   ```

7. **List filed claims**

   ```bash
   eai resources list Claim
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'insurance-claims': [
    {
      name: 'Claim',
      displayName: 'Claim',
      description: 'An insurance claim filed by a policyholder for loss or damage',
      properties: [
        { name: 'policyNumber', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        {
          name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Auto', value: 'auto' },
            { label: 'Property', value: 'property' },
            { label: 'Liability', value: 'liability' },
            { label: 'Health', value: 'health' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          defaultValue: 'filed',
          options: [
            { label: 'Filed', value: 'filed' },
            { label: 'Under Review', value: 'under-review' },
            { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
            { label: 'Denied', value: 'denied' },
            { label: 'Paid', value: 'paid' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'adjudications', targetObjectType: 'Adjudication', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'payments', targetObjectType: 'Payment', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'fileClaim',
          displayName: 'File Claim',
          description: 'Submit a new insurance claim with supporting documentation',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'policyNumber', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Adjudication',
      displayName: 'Adjudication',
      description: 'An adjuster review and decision on an insurance claim',
      properties: [
        { name: 'adjuster', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        {
          name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Approve', value: 'approve' },
            { label: 'Deny', value: 'deny' },
            { label: 'Request Info', value: 'request-info' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'approvedAmount', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'reasoning', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'reviewDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'claim', targetObjectType: 'Claim', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitDecision',
          displayName: 'Submit Decision',
          description: 'Record the adjuster decision and approved amount for the claim',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'approvedAmount', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
            { name: 'reasoning', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Payment',
      displayName: 'Payment',
      description: 'A payment issued to settle an approved insurance claim',
      properties: [
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'ACH Transfer', value: 'ach' },
            { label: 'Check', value: 'check' },
            { label: 'Direct Repair', value: 'direct-repair' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'processedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          defaultValue: 'pending',
          options: [
            { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
            { label: 'Processed', value: 'processed' },
            { label: 'Returned', value: 'returned' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'payee', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'claim', targetObjectType: 'Claim', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'processPayment',
          displayName: 'Process Payment',
          description: 'Execute the claim payment to the policyholder or repair vendor',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'payee', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Complete claims lifecycle**: The Claim, Adjudication, and Payment types cover every stage from initial filing through settlement, eliminating the need for separate tracking systems.
- **Adjuster decision tracking**: Every adjudication records the adjuster, decision reasoning, and approved amount, providing a defensible audit trail for regulatory review and dispute resolution.
- **Flexible payment methods**: The Payment type supports ACH, check, and direct repair vendor payments, accommodating different claim types and policyholder preferences.
- **Carrier-level isolation**: Each insurance carrier operates in a separate tenant, ensuring that claims data, adjuster assignments, and payment records are never accessible across carrier boundaries.

# KYC Verification

## Persona

**Role**: Backend developer at a fintech company (150 employees) building a compliance platform for digital banking partners.

Each banking partner is onboarded as a separate tenant, ensuring that customer identity data, verification documents, and risk assessments are strictly isolated. The platform must support regulatory requirements across multiple jurisdictions.

## Business Problem

Financial institutions spend significant resources on Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance. Manual identity verification involves reviewing uploaded documents, cross-referencing customer data, and assigning risk scores -- all across disconnected systems. This scenario builds a unified KYC workflow where customer onboarding, document verification, and risk assessment happen in a single, auditable pipeline.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Customer** | `name` (text), `address` (text), `dateOfBirth` (date), `status` (select: pending, verified, rejected, review-required), `jurisdiction` (text) | one-to-many → IdentityDocument, one-to-many → RiskAssessment | -- |
| **IdentityDocument** | `type` (select: passport, drivers-license, national-id, utility-bill), `fileUrl` (text), `verified` (boolean), `verifiedBy` (text), `uploadedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Customer | `verifyDocument` |
| **RiskAssessment** | `score` (number), `factors` (text), `decision` (select: approve, reject, escalate), `reviewer` (text), `assessmentDate` (date) | many-to-one → Customer | `submitAssessment` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init kyc-verification
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Customer, IdentityDocument, and RiskAssessment types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: kyc-verification
   ✔ Customer — 5 props, 2 links, 0 actions
   ✔ IdentityDocument — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ RiskAssessment — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create a sample customer and document**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Customer --data '{"name": "Alex Johnson", "address": "123 Main St, New York, NY 10001", "dateOfBirth": "1990-07-22", "status": "pending", "jurisdiction": "US"}'

   eai resources create IdentityDocument --data '{"type": "drivers-license", "fileUrl": "/documents/dl-aj-001.pdf", "verified": false, "verifiedBy": "", "uploadedDate": "2026-03-05"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'kyc-verification': [
    {
      name: 'Customer',
      displayName: 'Customer',
      description: 'A customer undergoing identity verification for account onboarding',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'address', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dateOfBirth', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          defaultValue: 'pending',
          options: [
            { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
            { label: 'Verified', value: 'verified' },
            { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
            { label: 'Review Required', value: 'review-required' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'jurisdiction', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'identityDocuments', targetObjectType: 'IdentityDocument', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'riskAssessments', targetObjectType: 'RiskAssessment', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'IdentityDocument',
      displayName: 'Identity Document',
      description: 'An uploaded identity document submitted for verification',
      properties: [
        {
          name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Passport', value: 'passport' },
            { label: 'Drivers License', value: 'drivers-license' },
            { label: 'National ID', value: 'national-id' },
            { label: 'Utility Bill', value: 'utility-bill' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'fileUrl', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'verified', type: 'boolean' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'verifiedBy', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'uploadedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'customer', targetObjectType: 'Customer', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'verifyDocument',
          displayName: 'Verify Document',
          description: 'Mark the identity document as verified after manual or automated review',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'verified', type: 'boolean' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'verifiedBy', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'RiskAssessment',
      displayName: 'Risk Assessment',
      description: 'A compliance risk evaluation for a customer based on identity and transaction data',
      properties: [
        { name: 'score', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'factors', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Approve', value: 'approve' },
            { label: 'Reject', value: 'reject' },
            { label: 'Escalate', value: 'escalate' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'reviewer', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'assessmentDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'customer', targetObjectType: 'Customer', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitAssessment',
          displayName: 'Submit Assessment',
          description: 'Record the risk assessment decision and update customer verification status',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'score', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'factors', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **End-to-end verification pipeline**: The Customer, IdentityDocument, and RiskAssessment types model the full KYC lifecycle, from document submission through risk scoring to final decision.
- **Audit trail by design**: Every document verification and risk assessment records who performed the review and when, satisfying regulatory audit requirements without additional tooling.
- **Jurisdiction-aware processing**: The `jurisdiction` field on Customer enables location-specific compliance rules, supporting multi-market operations within a single platform instance.
- **Partner isolation**: Each banking partner operates in a separate tenant, ensuring that customer PII and verification decisions are never accessible across institutional boundaries.

# Loan Processing

## Persona

**Role**: Solutions architect at a community credit union consortium (12 credit unions, 300 employees total) building a shared loan origination platform.

Each credit union operates as a separate tenant with its own underwriting criteria and member data. The shared platform reduces development costs while maintaining complete data isolation between institutions.

## Business Problem

Loan applications move through multiple stages -- intake, credit evaluation, underwriting, and disbursement -- often across disconnected spreadsheets and email threads. Loan officers lack real-time visibility into application status, and credit check results are manually copied between systems. This scenario builds a structured loan processing pipeline where applications flow from submission through approval to disbursement with full traceability.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **LoanApplication** | `applicant` (text), `amount` (number), `term` (number), `purpose` (select: home, auto, personal, business), `status` (select: submitted, under-review, approved, denied, disbursed) | one-to-many → CreditCheck, one-to-many → Disbursement | `reviewApplication` |
| **CreditCheck** | `score` (number), `report` (text), `date` (date), `bureau` (text), `debtToIncomeRatio` (number) | many-to-one → LoanApplication | `runCreditCheck` |
| **Disbursement** | `amount` (number), `method` (select: ach, wire, check), `date` (date), `status` (select: pending, processed, failed), `referenceNumber` (text) | many-to-one → LoanApplication | `processDisbursement` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init loan-processing
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the LoanApplication, CreditCheck, and Disbursement types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: loan-processing
   ✔ LoanApplication — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ CreditCheck — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Disbursement — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create a sample loan application**

   ```bash
   eai resources create LoanApplication --data '{"applicant": "Maria Gonzalez", "amount": 25000, "term": 60, "purpose": "auto", "status": "submitted"}'
   ```

7. **Query applications by status**

   ```bash
   eai resources list LoanApplication
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'loan-processing': [
    {
      name: 'LoanApplication',
      displayName: 'Loan Application',
      description: 'A loan application submitted by a member for underwriting review',
      properties: [
        { name: 'applicant', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'term', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'purpose', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Home', value: 'home' },
            { label: 'Auto', value: 'auto' },
            { label: 'Personal', value: 'personal' },
            { label: 'Business', value: 'business' },
          ],
        },
        {
          name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          defaultValue: 'submitted',
          options: [
            { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
            { label: 'Under Review', value: 'under-review' },
            { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
            { label: 'Denied', value: 'denied' },
            { label: 'Disbursed', value: 'disbursed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'creditChecks', targetObjectType: 'CreditCheck', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'disbursements', targetObjectType: 'Disbursement', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'reviewApplication',
          displayName: 'Review Application',
          description: 'Advance the application to the next stage of the underwriting pipeline',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'CreditCheck',
      displayName: 'Credit Check',
      description: 'A credit bureau inquiry associated with a loan application',
      properties: [
        { name: 'score', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'report', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'bureau', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'debtToIncomeRatio', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'loanApplication', targetObjectType: 'LoanApplication', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'runCreditCheck',
          displayName: 'Run Credit Check',
          description: 'Initiate a credit bureau inquiry and record the results',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'bureau', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'applicantId', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Disbursement',
      displayName: 'Disbursement',
      description: 'A funds disbursement for an approved loan application',
      properties: [
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'ACH Transfer', value: 'ach' },
            { label: 'Wire Transfer', value: 'wire' },
            { label: 'Check', value: 'check' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          defaultValue: 'pending',
          options: [
            { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
            { label: 'Processed', value: 'processed' },
            { label: 'Failed', value: 'failed' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'referenceNumber', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'loanApplication', targetObjectType: 'LoanApplication', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'processDisbursement',
          displayName: 'Process Disbursement',
          description: 'Execute the funds transfer and record the reference number',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true },
            { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Full origination pipeline**: The LoanApplication, CreditCheck, and Disbursement types model the complete loan lifecycle from submission through funds transfer, replacing fragmented spreadsheet workflows.
- **Credit check integration**: The `runCreditCheck` action captures bureau-specific scores and debt-to-income ratios, giving underwriters structured data for consistent decision-making.
- **Consortium model**: Each credit union operates in its own tenant with independent underwriting criteria, while sharing the same platform infrastructure and codebase to reduce costs.
- **Disbursement traceability**: Every fund transfer is recorded with method, reference number, and status, providing a complete audit trail from approval to payment.
