# Telemedicine

## Persona

**Role**: Full-stack developer at a telehealth startup (50 employees) building a white-label virtual care platform for hospital systems.

Each hospital system is onboarded as a separate tenant, keeping their provider rosters, patient records, and consultation history fully isolated. The development team needs to ship a working consultation booking flow quickly while maintaining the flexibility to customize per customer.

## Business Problem

Patients struggle to access specialists, especially in rural areas. Phone-based scheduling is slow, and providers lack a unified view of patient history before a virtual visit. This scenario builds a telemedicine platform where patients can book consultations with available providers, and providers see relevant medical history before joining a video session.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Consultation** | `scheduledTime` (datetime), `status` (select: requested, confirmed, in-progress, completed, cancelled), `notes` (text), `duration` (number) | many-to-one → Provider, many-to-one → PatientRecord | `startConsultation` |
| **Provider** | `name` (text), `specialty` (text), `licenseNumber` (text), `availability` (text) | one-to-many → Consultation | `updateAvailability` |
| **PatientRecord** | `patientName` (text), `history` (text), `medications` (text), `allergies` (text), `lastVisitDate` (date) | one-to-many → Consultation | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init telemedicine
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Consultation, Provider, and PatientRecord types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: telemedicine
   ✔ Consultation — 4 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Provider — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ PatientRecord — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample providers and a patient record**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Provider --data '{"name": "Dr. Sarah Chen", "specialty": "Cardiology", "licenseNumber": "MD-204819", "availability": "Mon-Fri 9am-5pm EST"}'

   eai resources create PatientRecord --data '{"patientName": "Robert Martinez", "history": "Hypertension diagnosed 2022, managed with medication", "medications": "Lisinopril 10mg daily", "allergies": "Penicillin", "lastVisitDate": "2026-01-10"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'telemedicine': [
    {
      name: 'Consultation',
      displayName: 'Consultation',
      description: 'A virtual care session between a provider and patient',
      properties: [
        { name: 'scheduledTime', type: 'datetime' as const, required: true },
        {
          name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          defaultValue: 'requested',
          options: [
            { label: 'Requested', value: 'requested' },
            { label: 'Confirmed', value: 'confirmed' },
            { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
            { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
            { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'duration', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'provider', targetObjectType: 'Provider', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'patientRecord', targetObjectType: 'PatientRecord', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'startConsultation',
          displayName: 'Start Consultation',
          description: 'Transition consultation to in-progress and notify both parties',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Provider',
      displayName: 'Provider',
      description: 'A licensed healthcare provider offering virtual consultations',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'specialty', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'licenseNumber', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'availability', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'consultations', targetObjectType: 'Consultation', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'updateAvailability',
          displayName: 'Update Availability',
          description: 'Set the provider availability schedule for booking',
          inputs: [
            { name: 'availability', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'PatientRecord',
      displayName: 'Patient Record',
      description: 'Consolidated patient medical history for provider review',
      properties: [
        { name: 'patientName', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'history', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'medications', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'allergies', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'lastVisitDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'consultations', targetObjectType: 'Consultation', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Pre-visit context**: Consultations link directly to PatientRecord, giving providers immediate access to medical history, medications, and allergies before the session starts.
- **Provider availability management**: The `updateAvailability` action lets providers set their own schedules, reducing administrative overhead for booking coordinators.
- **White-label multi-tenancy**: Each hospital system is a separate tenant, allowing the startup to onboard new customers without code changes -- only a new tenant scope.
- **Status-driven workflow**: The Consultation status field drives the entire session lifecycle from request through completion, enabling real-time dashboards and notification triggers.

# Billing & Time Tracking

## Persona

**Role**: Developer at a 50-attorney law firm transitioning from legacy billing software.

Attorneys log time in personal notebooks or desktop timers and submit entries weekly. Billing rates vary by attorney, matter type, and client arrangement, but are tracked in a separate spreadsheet. Invoices are generated manually by the billing department, requiring reconciliation of time entries against rate tables. The firm needs an integrated system where time entry, rates, and invoicing are connected.

## Business Problem

Revenue leakage is the firm's biggest financial problem. Attorneys forget to log time, entries are submitted late with inaccurate descriptions, and the billing department spends days each month reconciling entries against the correct rates. Client disputes over invoices require pulling original time entries from multiple systems. This scenario builds a billing workflow that captures time entries linked to cases, applies the correct billing rates automatically, and generates invoices with line-item detail.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **TimeEntry** | `attorney` (text), `case` (text), `date` (date), `hours` (number), `description` (text), `status` (select: draft, submitted, billed) | many-to-one → Invoice | `submitEntry` |
| **BillingRate** | `attorney` (text), `type` (select: standard, discounted, pro-bono, contingency), `rate` (number), `effectiveDate` (date) | -- | -- |
| **Invoice** | `client` (text), `totalAmount` (number), `status` (select: draft, sent, paid, overdue, disputed), `dueDate` (date), `sentDate` (date) | one-to-many → TimeEntry | `sendInvoice` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init billing-time-tracking
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the TimeEntry, BillingRate, and Invoice types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: billing-time-tracking
   ✔ TimeEntry — 6 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ BillingRate — 4 props, 0 links, 0 actions
   ✔ Invoice — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create TimeEntry --data '{"attorney": "Lisa Park", "case": "Smith v. Acme Industries", "date": "2025-07-15", "hours": 2.5, "description": "Draft motion for summary judgment", "status": "draft"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'billing-time-tracking': [
    {
      name: 'TimeEntry',
      displayName: 'Time Entry',
      description: 'A billable time entry recorded by an attorney',
      properties: [
        { name: 'attorney', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'case', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'hours', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
          { label: 'Billed', value: 'billed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'invoice', targetObjectType: 'Invoice', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitEntry',
          displayName: 'Submit Entry',
          description: 'Submit a draft time entry for billing',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['attorney', 'case', 'hours', 'description'], requiredStatus: 'draft' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'submitted' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'BillingRate',
      displayName: 'Billing Rate',
      description: 'A billing rate for an attorney by arrangement type',
      properties: [
        { name: 'attorney', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Standard', value: 'standard' },
          { label: 'Discounted', value: 'discounted' },
          { label: 'Pro Bono', value: 'pro-bono' },
          { label: 'Contingency', value: 'contingency' },
        ]},
        { name: 'rate', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'effectiveDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Invoice',
      displayName: 'Invoice',
      description: 'A client invoice composed of billable time entries',
      properties: [
        { name: 'client', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'totalAmount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'sentDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Sent', value: 'sent' },
          { label: 'Paid', value: 'paid' },
          { label: 'Overdue', value: 'overdue' },
          { label: 'Disputed', value: 'disputed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'timeEntries', targetObjectType: 'TimeEntry', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'sendInvoice',
          displayName: 'Send Invoice',
          description: 'Send a draft invoice to the client',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['client', 'totalAmount', 'dueDate'], requiredStatus: 'draft' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'sent' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'sentDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Revenue capture**: Structured time entry submission with required descriptions reduces forgotten or under-documented billable time.
- **Rate management**: Billing rates are stored per attorney with effective dates, supporting rate changes and multiple arrangement types without manual lookups.
- **Invoice line-item detail**: Invoices link directly to their constituent time entries, making client disputes easy to resolve with original entry data.
- **Billing lifecycle**: Time entries flow from draft through submission to billed, and invoices move from draft through sent to paid, giving the billing department complete pipeline visibility.

# Case Management

## Persona

**Role**: Software developer at a litigation firm managing 150+ active cases across multiple practice areas.

Attorneys track case details in personal notes, documents are scattered across network drives, and hearing dates are managed through individual calendar systems. The firm has no centralized view of its caseload, document deadlines, or upcoming court dates. Paralegals spend hours each week compiling status reports by polling individual attorneys.

## Business Problem

Without a unified case management system, critical court deadlines are at risk of being missed, document versions conflict when multiple attorneys work on the same case, and client status inquiries require manual research. The firm needs a single platform where cases are tracked from filing through resolution, documents are organized and version-controlled per case, and hearing schedules are visible to the entire team. This scenario builds a case management workflow that provides firm-wide visibility into case status, documents, and court appearances.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Case** | `title` (text), `type` (select: civil, criminal, corporate, family, ip), `client` (text), `status` (select: active, pending, closed, on-hold), `filingDate` (date) | one-to-many → CaseDocument, one-to-many → Hearing | `closeCase` |
| **CaseDocument** | `title` (text), `type` (select: pleading, motion, brief, correspondence, evidence), `fileUrl` (text), `confidential` (boolean), `uploadedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Case | -- |
| **Hearing** | `date` (date), `court` (text), `judge` (text), `outcome` (text), `type` (select: motion, trial, settlement, status-conference) | many-to-one → Case | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init case-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Case, CaseDocument, and Hearing types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: case-management
   ✔ Case — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ CaseDocument — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Hearing — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Case --data '{"title": "Smith v. Acme Industries", "type": "civil", "client": "Robert Smith", "status": "active", "filingDate": "2025-03-20"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
  'case-management': [
    {
      name: 'Case',
      displayName: 'Case',
      description: 'A legal case tracked by the firm',
      properties: [
        { name: 'title', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Civil', value: 'civil' },
          { label: 'Criminal', value: 'criminal' },
          { label: 'Corporate', value: 'corporate' },
          { label: 'Family', value: 'family' },
          { label: 'IP', value: 'ip' },
        ]},
        { name: 'client', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'active', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'Closed', value: 'closed' },
          { label: 'On Hold', value: 'on-hold' },

        { name: 'documents', targetObjectType: 'CaseDocument', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },

    {
      name: 'CaseDocument',
      displayName: 'Case Document',
      description: 'A document filed or received in connection with a case',
      properties: [
        { name: 'title', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Pleading', value: 'pleading' },
          { label: 'Motion', value: 'motion' },
          { label: 'Brief', value: 'brief' },
          { label: 'Correspondence', value: 'correspondence' },
          { label: 'Evidence', value: 'evidence' },
        ]},
        { name: 'fileUrl', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'confidential', type: 'boolean' as const, required: true, defaultValue: false },
        { name: 'uploadedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'case', targetObjectType: 'Case', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Hearing',
      displayName: 'Hearing',
      description: 'A court hearing or appearance scheduled for a case',
      properties: [
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'court', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'judge', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'outcome', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Motion', value: 'motion' },
          { label: 'Trial', value: 'trial' },
          { label: 'Settlement', value: 'settlement' },
          { label: 'Status Conference', value: 'status-conference' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'case', targetObjectType: 'Case', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Firm-wide visibility**: All active cases, their documents, and upcoming hearings are accessible from a single platform, eliminating the need for manual status report compilation.
- **Document organization**: Case documents are categorized by type and linked to their case, with confidentiality flags controlling access to sensitive materials.
- **Court calendar integration**: Hearing records with court, judge, and type data provide the firm with a complete view of upcoming court obligations across all cases.
- **Case lifecycle tracking**: The structured status flow from active through to closed ensures every case is accounted for and properly resolved.

# Compliance Monitoring

## Persona

**Role**: Compliance technology developer at a financial services company subject to oversight from multiple regulatory bodies.

The compliance team tracks filing deadlines in spreadsheets, sends reminder emails manually, and maintains audit logs in shared documents. When regulators request proof of compliance, assembling the evidence is a multi-day effort. The company needs a system that tracks every obligation, automates deadline awareness, and maintains an immutable audit trail.

## Business Problem

Missed regulatory filings result in fines, enforcement actions, and reputational damage. The compliance team manages hundreds of recurring obligations across different regulations and entities, each with unique frequencies and deadlines. Without a structured system, obligations fall through the cracks, filings are submitted late, and there is no reliable audit trail showing when actions were taken and by whom. This scenario builds a compliance monitoring workflow that catalogs obligations, tracks filings against deadlines, and records every action in an audit trail.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Obligation** | `regulation` (text), `entity` (text), `description` (text), `frequency` (select: monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual, ad-hoc) | one-to-many → Filing | -- |
| **Filing** | `period` (text), `dueDate` (date), `submittedDate` (date), `status` (select: upcoming, in-progress, submitted, overdue) | many-to-one → Obligation, one-to-many → AuditTrail | `submitFiling` |
| **AuditTrail** | `action` (text), `user` (text), `timestamp` (date), `details` (text) | many-to-one → Filing | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init compliance-monitoring
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Obligation, Filing, and AuditTrail types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: compliance-monitoring
   ✔ Obligation — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Filing — 4 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ AuditTrail — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Obligation --data '{"regulation": "SEC Rule 17a-4", "entity": "US Broker-Dealer Division", "description": "Quarterly electronic records retention report", "frequency": "quarterly"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'compliance-monitoring': [
    {
      name: 'Obligation',
      displayName: 'Obligation',
      description: 'A regulatory obligation that requires periodic filings',
      properties: [
        { name: 'regulation', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'entity', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'frequency', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Monthly', value: 'monthly' },
          { label: 'Quarterly', value: 'quarterly' },
          { label: 'Semi-Annual', value: 'semi-annual' },
          { label: 'Annual', value: 'annual' },
          { label: 'Ad-Hoc', value: 'ad-hoc' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'filings', targetObjectType: 'Filing', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Filing',
      displayName: 'Filing',
      description: 'A specific filing instance for a regulatory obligation',
      properties: [
        { name: 'period', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'submittedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'upcoming', options: [
          { label: 'Upcoming', value: 'upcoming' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
          { label: 'Overdue', value: 'overdue' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'obligation', targetObjectType: 'Obligation', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'auditTrail', targetObjectType: 'AuditTrail', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const, cascadeDelete: true },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitFiling',
          displayName: 'Submit Filing',
          description: 'Mark a filing as submitted to the regulatory body',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'submitted' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'submittedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'AuditTrail',
      displayName: 'Audit Trail',
      description: 'An immutable record of an action taken on a filing',
      properties: [
        { name: 'action', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'user', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'timestamp', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'details', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'filing', targetObjectType: 'Filing', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Obligation catalog**: Every regulatory requirement is cataloged with its frequency and responsible entity, providing a complete compliance inventory.
- **Deadline-driven workflow**: Filings are indexed by due date, enabling dashboards that surface upcoming deadlines and overdue items at a glance.
- **Immutable audit trail**: Every action on a filing is recorded with the user and timestamp, creating regulator-ready evidence of compliance activities.
- **Multi-regulation support**: The obligation model supports different regulations and frequencies, scaling from a single filing requirement to hundreds across multiple regulatory frameworks.

# Contract Review

## Persona

**Role**: Legal technology developer at a corporate legal department handling 200+ contracts per quarter.

The legal team receives contract review requests via email, assigns them informally, and tracks approval status in a shared spreadsheet. Reviewers leave comments in document margins, but there is no central record of who reviewed what or when. The department needs a structured intake and review process with clear approval authority.

## Business Problem

Contract review bottlenecks delay business deals. Requests pile up without visibility into the queue, reviewers are assigned based on whoever is available rather than expertise, and approval decisions lack an audit trail. When auditors ask who approved a contract and under what conditions, the legal team scrambles to reconstruct the history from emails. This scenario builds a contract review workflow that tracks every contract from intake through review to approval with full accountability.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Contract** | `title` (text), `parties` (text), `type` (select: nda, services, license, employment, vendor), `value` (number), `status` (select: intake, in-review, approved, rejected) | one-to-many → ReviewTask, one-to-many → Approval | `sendForReview` |
| **ReviewTask** | `reviewer` (text), `dueDate` (date), `comments` (text), `status` (select: assigned, in-progress, completed) | many-to-one → Contract | `completeReview` |
| **Approval** | `approver` (text), `decision` (select: approved, rejected, conditional), `conditions` (text), `decidedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Contract | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init contract-review
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Contract, ReviewTask, and Approval types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: contract-review
   ✔ Contract — 4 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ ReviewTask — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Approval — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Contract --data '{"title": "SaaS License Agreement - Vendor X", "parties": "Acme Corp, Vendor X Inc", "type": "license", "value": 250000, "status": "intake"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'contract-review': [
    {
      name: 'Contract',
      displayName: 'Contract',
      description: 'A contract submitted for legal review and approval',
      properties: [
        { name: 'title', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'parties', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'NDA', value: 'nda' },
          { label: 'Services', value: 'services' },
          { label: 'License', value: 'license' },
          { label: 'Employment', value: 'employment' },
          { label: 'Vendor', value: 'vendor' },
        ]},
        { name: 'value', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'intake', options: [
          { label: 'Intake', value: 'intake' },
          { label: 'In Review', value: 'in-review' },
          { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
          { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'reviewTasks', targetObjectType: 'ReviewTask', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'approvals', targetObjectType: 'Approval', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'sendForReview',
          displayName: 'Send for Review',
          description: 'Move a contract from intake to the review queue',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['title', 'parties', 'type'], requiredStatus: 'intake' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'in-review' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ReviewTask',
      displayName: 'Review Task',
      description: 'A review assignment for a specific contract',
      properties: [
        { name: 'reviewer', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'comments', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'assigned', options: [
          { label: 'Assigned', value: 'assigned' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'contract', targetObjectType: 'Contract', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeReview',
          displayName: 'Complete Review',
          description: 'Mark a review task as completed with comments',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['comments'], requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Approval',
      displayName: 'Approval',
      description: 'An approval decision on a reviewed contract',
      properties: [
        { name: 'approver', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
          { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
          { label: 'Conditional', value: 'conditional' },
        ]},
        { name: 'conditions', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'decidedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'contract', targetObjectType: 'Contract', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Structured intake pipeline**: Contracts move through defined stages from intake to review to approval, eliminating the chaos of email-based requests.
- **Reviewer accountability**: Review tasks track who is assigned, when the review is due, and what comments were provided, creating a clear record of the review process.
- **Conditional approvals**: The approval model supports conditional decisions, capturing the specific conditions that must be met before a contract can proceed.
- **Audit-ready history**: Every review task and approval decision is linked to the contract, providing the complete audit trail that regulators and auditors require.

# E-Discovery

## Persona

**Role**: Litigation support developer at a law firm managing e-discovery for complex commercial disputes.

The firm handles discovery requests involving thousands of documents from multiple custodians. Collection tracking is done through email chains, document review happens in spreadsheets with inconsistent tagging, and production logs are maintained in word processors. The firm needs a structured e-discovery workflow that tracks documents from collection through review to production.

## Business Problem

E-discovery is one of the most expensive phases of litigation. Without structured workflows, documents are collected redundantly, review assignments overlap, and production sets are assembled manually from inconsistent review records. Defensibility requires demonstrating that every responsive document was reviewed and that privilege calls were made consistently. This scenario builds an e-discovery platform that manages collections by custodian, assigns documents for review with structured tagging, and tracks productions with delivery confirmation.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Collection** | `case` (text), `custodian` (text), `dateRange` (text), `documentCount` (number), `status` (select: pending, in-progress, completed, verified) | one-to-many → ReviewItem | `completeCollection` |
| **ReviewItem** | `document` (text), `reviewer` (text), `tags` (text), `decision` (select: responsive, non-responsive, privileged, needs-redaction), `reviewedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Collection | `makeDecision` |
| **Production** | `case` (text), `itemCount` (number), `format` (select: native, tiff, pdf), `deliveredDate` (date), `status` (select: preparing, delivered, acknowledged) | -- | `markDelivered` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init e-discovery
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Collection, ReviewItem, and Production types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: e-discovery
   ✔ Collection — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ ReviewItem — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Production — 5 props, 0 links, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Collection --data '{"case": "Smith v. Acme Industries", "custodian": "J. Anderson", "dateRange": "2023-01-01 to 2025-06-30", "documentCount": 1250, "status": "pending"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'e-discovery': [
    {
      name: 'Collection',
      displayName: 'Collection',
      description: 'A document collection from a specific custodian for a case',
      properties: [
        { name: 'case', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'custodian', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'dateRange', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'documentCount', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Verified', value: 'verified' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'reviewItems', targetObjectType: 'ReviewItem', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeCollection',
          displayName: 'Complete Collection',
          description: 'Mark a document collection as completed',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['custodian', 'documentCount'], requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ReviewItem',
      displayName: 'Review Item',
      description: 'A document assigned for review within a collection',
      properties: [
        { name: 'document', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'reviewer', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'tags', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'decision', type: 'select' as const, required: false, options: [
          { label: 'Responsive', value: 'responsive' },
          { label: 'Non-Responsive', value: 'non-responsive' },
          { label: 'Privileged', value: 'privileged' },
          { label: 'Needs Redaction', value: 'needs-redaction' },
        ]},
        { name: 'reviewedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'collection', targetObjectType: 'Collection', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'makeDecision',
          displayName: 'Make Decision',
          description: 'Record a review decision on a document',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['document', 'reviewer'] },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'reviewedDate' },
            { type: 'set_user', field: 'reviewer' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Production',
      displayName: 'Production',
      description: 'A set of documents produced to opposing counsel',
      properties: [
        { name: 'case', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'itemCount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'format', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Native', value: 'native' },
          { label: 'TIFF', value: 'tiff' },
          { label: 'PDF', value: 'pdf' },
        ]},
        { name: 'deliveredDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'preparing', options: [
          { label: 'Preparing', value: 'preparing' },
          { label: 'Delivered', value: 'delivered' },
          { label: 'Acknowledged', value: 'acknowledged' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'markDelivered',
          displayName: 'Mark Delivered',
          description: 'Record that a production has been delivered to opposing counsel',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['itemCount', 'format'], requiredStatus: 'preparing' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'delivered' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'deliveredDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Custodian-based collections**: Documents are organized by custodian and date range, providing clear provenance for every collected item.
- **Structured review decisions**: Standardized decision categories (responsive, non-responsive, privileged, needs-redaction) ensure consistent review across multiple reviewers.
- **Production tracking**: Each production set records its format, item count, and delivery date, creating a defensible record of what was produced and when.
- **Defensibility by design**: The complete chain from collection through review to production with timestamped decisions demonstrates a reasonable and proportional discovery process.

# Fleet Management

## Persona

**Role**: Fleet systems developer at a delivery company operating 75 vehicles across three depots.

Vehicle maintenance is scheduled based on calendar reminders rather than actual mileage, fuel costs are tracked only at the fleet level with no per-vehicle breakdown, and there is no centralized record of vehicle condition or service history. When a vehicle breaks down, the operations team has no data to predict which vehicles are at risk.

## Business Problem

Unexpected vehicle breakdowns disrupt delivery schedules and cost the company in towing fees, emergency repairs, and missed deliveries. Without mileage-based maintenance tracking, vehicles are either serviced too frequently (wasting money) or too infrequently (risking breakdowns). Fuel costs are rising but the company cannot identify which vehicles are inefficient. This scenario builds a fleet management workflow that tracks vehicle status and mileage, schedules maintenance based on usage data, and logs fuel consumption per vehicle.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Vehicle** | `make` (text), `model` (text), `year` (number), `mileage` (number), `status` (select: active, maintenance, retired) | one-to-many → MaintenanceRecord, one-to-many → FuelLog | -- |
| **MaintenanceRecord** | `type` (select: oil-change, tires, brakes, inspection, repair), `date` (date), `cost` (number), `vendor` (text), `mileageAtService` (number) | many-to-one → Vehicle | -- |
| **FuelLog** | `date` (date), `gallons` (number), `cost` (number), `odometer` (number) | many-to-one → Vehicle | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init fleet-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Vehicle, MaintenanceRecord, and FuelLog types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: fleet-management
   ✔ Vehicle — 5 props, 2 links, 0 actions
   ✔ MaintenanceRecord — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ FuelLog — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Vehicle --data '{"make": "Ford", "model": "Transit 250", "year": 2023, "mileage": 34500, "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript

  'fleet-management': [
    {
      name: 'Vehicle',
      displayName: 'Vehicle',
      description: 'A vehicle in the company fleet',
      properties: [
        { name: 'make', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'model', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'year', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'mileage', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'active', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Maintenance', value: 'maintenance' },
          { label: 'Retired', value: 'retired' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'maintenanceRecords', targetObjectType: 'MaintenanceRecord', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'fuelLogs', targetObjectType: 'FuelLog', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'MaintenanceRecord',
      displayName: 'Maintenance Record',
      description: 'A service or repair performed on a fleet vehicle',
      properties: [
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Oil Change', value: 'oil-change' },
          { label: 'Tires', value: 'tires' },
          { label: 'Brakes', value: 'brakes' },
          { label: 'Inspection', value: 'inspection' },
          { label: 'Repair', value: 'repair' },
        ]},
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'cost', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'vendor', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'mileageAtService', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'vehicle', targetObjectType: 'Vehicle', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'FuelLog',
      displayName: 'Fuel Log',
      description: 'A fuel fill-up record for a fleet vehicle',
      properties: [
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'gallons', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'cost', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'odometer', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'vehicle', targetObjectType: 'Vehicle', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Mileage-based maintenance**: Recording mileage at each service enables scheduling based on actual usage rather than arbitrary calendar intervals.
- **Per-vehicle cost analysis**: Maintenance costs and fuel consumption tracked per vehicle reveal which units are expensive to operate and may be candidates for replacement.
- **Fuel efficiency monitoring**: Odometer readings on fuel logs enable calculation of miles-per-gallon trends, identifying vehicles with declining efficiency.
- **Complete vehicle history**: Linking maintenance records and fuel logs to vehicles creates a comprehensive service history that supports resale value documentation and warranty claims.

# Last Mile Delivery

## Persona

**Role**: Platform developer at a last-mile delivery startup handling 1,000+ daily deliveries in an urban market.

Drivers receive assignments through a consumer messaging app, customers have no visibility into delivery timing, and proof of delivery is a photo texted to a dispatcher who saves it to a shared folder. When a customer claims non-delivery, there is no structured evidence to resolve the dispute. The startup needs a purpose-built delivery management platform.

## Business Problem

Last-mile delivery is defined by tight time windows and high customer expectations. When customers do not know when their delivery will arrive, they are unavailable at the door, causing failed deliveries and redelivery costs. When proof of delivery is informal, disputes are unresolvable. When driver assignments are managed through messaging apps, there is no audit trail, no performance data, and no way to reassign deliveries when a driver calls in sick. This scenario builds a last-mile delivery workflow that assigns packages to drivers with time windows, sends notifications to customers at key milestones, and captures structured proof of delivery.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **DeliveryAssignment** | `package` (text), `driver` (text), `timeWindow` (text), `address` (text), `status` (select: assigned, en-route, attempted, delivered, failed) | one-to-many → Notification, one-to-many → ProofOfDelivery | `markEnRoute` |
| **Notification** | `type` (select: assignment, en-route, delivered, failed), `sentAt` (date), `channel` (select: sms, email, push), `recipient` (text) | many-to-one → DeliveryAssignment | -- |
| **ProofOfDelivery** | `photo` (file), `signature` (text), `timestamp` (date), `notes` (text) | many-to-one → DeliveryAssignment | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init last-mile-delivery
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the DeliveryAssignment, Notification, and ProofOfDelivery types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: last-mile-delivery
   ✔ DeliveryAssignment — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Notification — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ ProofOfDelivery — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create DeliveryAssignment --data '{"package": "PKG-2025-08-001", "driver": "Ana Rodriguez", "timeWindow": "2:00 PM - 4:00 PM", "address": "456 Oak Ave, Apt 3B", "status": "assigned"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'last-mile-delivery': [
    {
      name: 'DeliveryAssignment',
      displayName: 'Delivery Assignment',
      description: 'A package assigned to a driver for last-mile delivery',
      properties: [
        { name: 'package', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'driver', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'timeWindow', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'address', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'assigned', options: [
          { label: 'Assigned', value: 'assigned' },
          { label: 'En Route', value: 'en-route' },
          { label: 'Attempted', value: 'attempted' },
          { label: 'Delivered', value: 'delivered' },
          { label: 'Failed', value: 'failed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'notifications', targetObjectType: 'Notification', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'proofOfDelivery', targetObjectType: 'ProofOfDelivery', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'markEnRoute',
          displayName: 'Mark En Route',
          description: 'Indicate the driver is en route to the delivery address',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['driver', 'address'], requiredStatus: 'assigned' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'en-route' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Notification',
      displayName: 'Notification',
      description: 'A notification sent to the customer about delivery status',
      properties: [
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Assignment', value: 'assignment' },
          { label: 'En Route', value: 'en-route' },
          { label: 'Delivered', value: 'delivered' },
          { label: 'Failed', value: 'failed' },
        ]},
        { name: 'sentAt', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'channel', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'SMS', value: 'sms' },
          { label: 'Email', value: 'email' },
          { label: 'Push', value: 'push' },
        ]},
        { name: 'recipient', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'deliveryAssignment', targetObjectType: 'DeliveryAssignment', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ProofOfDelivery',
      displayName: 'Proof of Delivery',
      description: 'Photo and signature evidence that a delivery was completed',
      properties: [
        { name: 'photo', type: 'file' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'signature', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'timestamp', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'deliveryAssignment', targetObjectType: 'DeliveryAssignment', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Customer communication**: Structured notifications at each delivery milestone (assigned, en route, delivered) keep customers informed and reduce failed delivery attempts.
- **Dispute resolution**: Photo and signature proof of delivery linked to specific assignments provides clear evidence when customers dispute receipt.
- **Multi-channel notifications**: Supporting SMS, email, and push notification channels ensures customers receive updates through their preferred communication method.
- **Driver performance data**: Timestamped status transitions on delivery assignments enable analysis of delivery times, success rates, and driver efficiency.

# Route Optimization

## Persona

**Role**: Logistics software engineer at a regional delivery company operating 40 vehicles across a metro area.

Dispatchers plan routes manually each morning by printing orders and grouping them by area on a physical map. Drivers receive paper route sheets, time windows are frequently missed because routes are not optimized for traffic or delivery priorities, and there is no real-time visibility into route progress. The company needs a digital route planning system.

## Business Problem

Manual route planning wastes driver time, fuel, and customer goodwill. Dispatchers spend two hours each morning building routes that an algorithm could generate in seconds. High-priority deliveries are not always scheduled first, time windows are violated because stop sequencing ignores travel time, and drivers have no way to report completion or delays digitally. This scenario builds a route optimization workflow that assigns stops to routes with time windows and priorities, tracks driver assignments, and monitors stop completion in real time.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Route** | `date` (date), `driver` (text), `vehicle` (text), `totalStops` (number), `distance` (number), `status` (select: planned, in-progress, completed) | one-to-many → Stop | `startRoute` |
| **Stop** | `address` (text), `timeWindow` (text), `priority` (select: standard, express, critical), `sequence` (number), `status` (select: pending, completed, failed, skipped) | many-to-one → Route | `completeStop` |
| **Driver** | `name` (text), `license` (text), `vehicle` (text), `availability` (select: available, on-route, off-duty) | one-to-many → Route | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init route-optimization
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Route, Stop, and Driver types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: route-optimization
   ✔ Route — 6 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Stop — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Driver — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Route --data '{"date": "2025-08-01", "driver": "Mike Torres", "vehicle": "Van-12", "totalStops": 18, "distance": 47.5, "status": "planned"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'route-optimization': [
    {
      name: 'Route',
      displayName: 'Route',
      description: 'A planned delivery route for a driver and vehicle',
      properties: [
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'driver', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'vehicle', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'totalStops', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'distance', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'planned', options: [
          { label: 'Planned', value: 'planned' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'stops', targetObjectType: 'Stop', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'startRoute',
          displayName: 'Start Route',
          description: 'Begin executing a planned route',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['driver', 'vehicle'], requiredStatus: 'planned' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'in-progress' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Stop',
      displayName: 'Stop',
      description: 'A delivery stop on a route',
      properties: [
        { name: 'address', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'timeWindow', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'priority', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'standard', options: [
          { label: 'Standard', value: 'standard' },
          { label: 'Express', value: 'express' },
          { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
        ]},
        { name: 'sequence', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Failed', value: 'failed' },
          { label: 'Skipped', value: 'skipped' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'route', targetObjectType: 'Route', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeStop',
          displayName: 'Complete Stop',
          description: 'Mark a delivery stop as completed',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'pending' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Driver',
      displayName: 'Driver',
      description: 'A delivery driver in the fleet',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'license', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'vehicle', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'availability', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'available', options: [
          { label: 'Available', value: 'available' },
          { label: 'On Route', value: 'on-route' },
          { label: 'Off Duty', value: 'off-duty' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'routes', targetObjectType: 'Route', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Structured stop sequencing**: Every stop has a sequence number and priority level, ensuring critical deliveries are handled first and routes are executed in order.
- **Real-time route progress**: Drivers complete stops digitally, giving dispatchers live visibility into which stops are done, pending, or failed.
- **Driver availability tracking**: Driver status (available, on-route, off-duty) enables dispatchers to assign routes based on current availability rather than guesswork.
- **Time window compliance**: Recording time windows on stops enables post-route analysis of on-time delivery performance for service level agreements.

# Shipment Tracking

## Persona

**Role**: Logistics platform developer at a freight brokerage managing 500+ shipments per month.

The operations team tracks shipments through carrier portals, updates customers via manual email, and records delivery confirmations in spreadsheets. There is no unified view of where shipments are, which ones are delayed, or whether deliveries were confirmed. The company needs a centralized shipment tracking platform.

## Business Problem

Customers call asking "where is my shipment?" and operations staff must log into individual carrier portals to find the answer. Delayed shipments are discovered only when customers complain, because there is no proactive monitoring. Delivery confirmations are not systematically recorded, leading to billing disputes over whether goods were actually received. This scenario builds a shipment tracking workflow that captures the full lifecycle from origin to delivery, records tracking events at each milestone, and logs delivery confirmations with recipient signatures.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Shipment** | `origin` (text), `destination` (text), `carrier` (text), `status` (select: booked, in-transit, out-for-delivery, delivered, exception), `estimatedDelivery` (date) | one-to-many → TrackingEvent, one-to-many → Delivery | `dispatchShipment` |
| **TrackingEvent** | `location` (text), `status` (text), `timestamp` (date), `description` (text) | many-to-one → Shipment | -- |
| **Delivery** | `recipient` (text), `signature` (text), `timestamp` (date), `notes` (text) | many-to-one → Shipment | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init shipment-tracking
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Shipment, TrackingEvent, and Delivery types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: shipment-tracking
   ✔ Shipment — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ TrackingEvent — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Delivery — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Shipment --data '{"origin": "Los Angeles, CA", "destination": "Chicago, IL", "carrier": "FastFreight Logistics", "status": "booked", "estimatedDelivery": "2025-08-05"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'shipment-tracking': [
    {
      name: 'Shipment',
      displayName: 'Shipment',
      description: 'A freight shipment moving from origin to destination',
      properties: [
        { name: 'origin', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'destination', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'carrier', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'booked', options: [
          { label: 'Booked', value: 'booked' },
          { label: 'In Transit', value: 'in-transit' },
          { label: 'Out for Delivery', value: 'out-for-delivery' },
          { label: 'Delivered', value: 'delivered' },
          { label: 'Exception', value: 'exception' },
        ]},
        { name: 'estimatedDelivery', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'trackingEvents', targetObjectType: 'TrackingEvent', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'deliveries', targetObjectType: 'Delivery', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'dispatchShipment',
          displayName: 'Dispatch Shipment',
          description: 'Mark a booked shipment as dispatched and in transit',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['origin', 'destination', 'carrier'], requiredStatus: 'booked' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'in-transit' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'TrackingEvent',
      displayName: 'Tracking Event',
      description: 'A status update event during shipment transit',
      properties: [
        { name: 'location', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'timestamp', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'shipment', targetObjectType: 'Shipment', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Delivery',
      displayName: 'Delivery',
      description: 'A delivery confirmation for a shipment',
      properties: [
        { name: 'recipient', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'signature', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'timestamp', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'shipment', targetObjectType: 'Shipment', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **End-to-end visibility**: Every shipment is tracked from booking through transit to delivery, answering "where is my shipment?" without calling the carrier.
- **Event-driven tracking**: Tracking events create a timestamped history of every location and status change, enabling proactive delay detection.
- **Delivery confirmation**: Recipient and signature data recorded at delivery provides proof of receipt that prevents billing disputes.
- **Exception handling**: The exception status flag surfaces problematic shipments that need immediate attention, separating them from normal transit flow.

# Warehouse Management

## Persona

**Role**: Warehouse systems developer at an e-commerce fulfillment center processing 2,000+ orders per day.

The warehouse team tracks inventory on whiteboards and in spreadsheets that are updated once per shift. Pick lists are printed on paper, and stock discrepancies are discovered only during quarterly physical counts. The company needs a digital inventory management system that provides real-time stock levels, manages pick orders, and records adjustments with audit trails.

## Business Problem

Overselling is the most costly problem: orders are accepted for items that are out of stock because inventory counts are stale. Pick errors occur because paper-based pick lists do not update in real time as other pickers complete orders. Stock adjustments from damage, returns, and shrinkage are recorded inconsistently, making it impossible to identify the source of inventory discrepancies. This scenario builds a warehouse management workflow that maintains real-time inventory by location, assigns pick orders to workers, and records every stock adjustment with a reason and audit trail.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **InventoryItem** | `product` (text), `location` (text), `quantity` (number), `lastCounted` (date), `sku` (text) | one-to-many → StockAdjustment | -- |
| **PickOrder** | `items` (text), `priority` (select: standard, express, same-day), `assignedTo` (text), `status` (select: queued, picking, packed, shipped) | -- | `completePicking` |
| **StockAdjustment** | `reason` (select: received, damaged, returned, shrinkage, correction), `quantity` (number), `adjustedBy` (text), `adjustedDate` (date) | many-to-one → InventoryItem | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init warehouse-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the InventoryItem, PickOrder, and StockAdjustment types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: warehouse-management
   ✔ InventoryItem — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ PickOrder — 4 props, 0 links, 1 action
   ✔ StockAdjustment — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create InventoryItem --data '{"product": "Wireless Mouse WM-500", "location": "Aisle 3, Shelf B, Bin 7", "quantity": 145, "lastCounted": "2025-07-01", "sku": "WM-500-BLK"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
  'warehouse-management': [
    {
      name: 'InventoryItem',
      displayName: 'Inventory Item',
      description: 'A product stored at a specific warehouse location',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'location', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'quantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'lastCounted', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'sku', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'adjustments', targetObjectType: 'StockAdjustment', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'PickOrder',
      displayName: 'Pick Order',
      description: 'An order to be picked from warehouse inventory',
      properties: [
        { name: 'items', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'priority', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'standard', options: [
          { label: 'Standard', value: 'standard' },
          { label: 'Express', value: 'express' },
          { label: 'Same-Day', value: 'same-day' },
        ]},
        { name: 'assignedTo', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'queued', options: [
          { label: 'Queued', value: 'queued' },
          { label: 'Picking', value: 'picking' },
          { label: 'Packed', value: 'packed' },
          { label: 'Shipped', value: 'shipped' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completePicking',
          displayName: 'Complete Picking',
          description: 'Mark a pick order as fully picked and ready for packing',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['assignedTo'], requiredStatus: 'picking' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'packed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'StockAdjustment',
      displayName: 'Stock Adjustment',
      description: 'A change to inventory quantity with reason and audit trail',
      properties: [
        { name: 'reason', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Received', value: 'received' },
          { label: 'Damaged', value: 'damaged' },
          { label: 'Returned', value: 'returned' },
          { label: 'Shrinkage', value: 'shrinkage' },
          { label: 'Correction', value: 'correction' },
        ]},
        { name: 'quantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'adjustedBy', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'adjustedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'inventoryItem', targetObjectType: 'InventoryItem', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Location-level tracking**: Inventory is tracked by specific warehouse location (aisle, shelf, bin), enabling efficient pick path routing and cycle counting.
- **Priority-based picking**: Pick orders with priority levels ensure same-day and express orders are processed before standard orders.
- **Auditable adjustments**: Every stock change records the reason, person, and date, creating a complete audit trail that explains inventory discrepancies.
- **SKU-indexed search**: Products are indexed by SKU for fast lookups, supporting barcode scanning workflows on the warehouse floor.
