# Defect Management

## Persona

**Role**: Quality systems developer at an automotive parts manufacturer producing 50,000 units per week.

The quality engineering team manages defect reports through email and shared drives. Root cause analyses are documented in unstructured text files, and there is no systematic way to verify that resolutions actually prevent recurrence. The company needs a structured defect management system to support their continuous improvement program and customer audit requirements.

## Business Problem

When a defect is reported, the investigation process is ad hoc. Engineers document findings in different formats, root cause analyses vary in rigor, and there is no feedback loop to verify that corrective actions worked. Customer audits require demonstrating a closed-loop defect management process, which currently takes weeks to compile from scattered documents. This scenario builds a defect management workflow that formalizes reporting, structures root cause analysis, and tracks resolutions through verification.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **DefectReport** | `product` (text), `batch` (text), `description` (text), `severity` (select: cosmetic, minor, major, critical), `reportedDate` (date), `status` (select: open, investigating, resolved, closed) | one-to-many → RootCauseAnalysis, one-to-many → Resolution | `beginInvestigation` |
| **RootCauseAnalysis** | `method` (select: 5-why, fishbone, fmea, fault-tree), `findings` (text), `contributingFactors` (text), `completedDate` (date) | many-to-one → DefectReport | -- |
| **Resolution** | `action` (text), `verifiedBy` (text), `closedDate` (date), `effective` (boolean), `status` (select: planned, implemented, verified) | many-to-one → DefectReport | `verifyResolution` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init defect-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the DefectReport, RootCauseAnalysis, and Resolution types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: defect-management
   ✔ DefectReport — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ RootCauseAnalysis — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Resolution — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create DefectReport --data '{"product": "Brake Caliper BC-400", "batch": "B-2025-0712", "description": "Surface pitting on machined face", "severity": "major", "reportedDate": "2025-07-12", "status": "open"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'defect-management': [
    {
      name: 'DefectReport',
      displayName: 'Defect Report',
      description: 'A formal defect report for a manufactured product',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'batch', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'severity', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Cosmetic', value: 'cosmetic' },
          { label: 'Minor', value: 'minor' },
          { label: 'Major', value: 'major' },
          { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
        ]},
        { name: 'reportedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'open', options: [
          { label: 'Open', value: 'open' },
          { label: 'Investigating', value: 'investigating' },
          { label: 'Resolved', value: 'resolved' },
          { label: 'Closed', value: 'closed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'rootCauseAnalyses', targetObjectType: 'RootCauseAnalysis', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'resolutions', targetObjectType: 'Resolution', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'beginInvestigation',
          displayName: 'Begin Investigation',
          description: 'Start root cause analysis on a defect report',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['product', 'description', 'severity'], requiredStatus: 'open' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'investigating' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'RootCauseAnalysis',
      displayName: 'Root Cause Analysis',
      description: 'A structured root cause analysis for a defect',
      properties: [
        { name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: '5-Why', value: '5-why' },
          { label: 'Fishbone', value: 'fishbone' },
          { label: 'FMEA', value: 'fmea' },
          { label: 'Fault Tree', value: 'fault-tree' },
        ]},
        { name: 'findings', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'contributingFactors', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'completedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'defectReport', targetObjectType: 'DefectReport', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Resolution',
      displayName: 'Resolution',
      description: 'A corrective action and its verification for a defect',
      properties: [
        { name: 'action', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'verifiedBy', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'closedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'effective', type: 'boolean' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'planned', options: [
          { label: 'Planned', value: 'planned' },
          { label: 'Implemented', value: 'implemented' },
          { label: 'Verified', value: 'verified' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'defectReport', targetObjectType: 'DefectReport', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'verifyResolution',
          displayName: 'Verify Resolution',
          description: 'Verify that the corrective action effectively prevents recurrence',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'implemented' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'verified' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'closedDate' },
            { type: 'set_user', field: 'verifiedBy' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Closed-loop process**: The workflow enforces a complete cycle from defect reporting through root cause analysis to verified resolution, satisfying audit requirements.
- **Structured analysis methods**: Root cause analyses specify the methodology used (5-Why, Fishbone, FMEA, Fault Tree), ensuring consistent investigation rigor.
- **Verification step**: Resolutions must be explicitly verified as effective before closure, preventing premature sign-off on corrective actions.
- **Batch traceability**: Linking defects to specific batches and products enables trend analysis across production runs and product lines.

---

# Equipment Maintenance

## Persona

**Role**: Industrial IoT developer at a plastics manufacturer operating 80+ machines across two plants.

Maintenance is entirely reactive -- machines break, technicians scramble to fix them, and the same failures repeat because there is no preventive maintenance schedule. Repair history lives in technicians' memories, spare parts usage is untracked, and downtime costs are estimated rather than measured. The company wants to shift from reactive to preventive maintenance.

## Business Problem

Unplanned downtime is the most expensive problem on the factory floor. Without maintenance schedules, equipment runs until failure. Without repair logs, the same issues are diagnosed from scratch each time. Without parts tracking, critical spares run out at the worst moments. This scenario builds an equipment maintenance system that schedules preventive maintenance, logs every repair with parts and duration, and provides a complete service history for each machine.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Equipment** | `name` (text), `type` (text), `location` (text), `lastService` (date), `status` (select: operational, maintenance, offline) | one-to-many → MaintenanceSchedule, one-to-many → RepairLog | -- |
| **MaintenanceSchedule** | `frequency` (select: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual), `nextDue` (date), `description` (text), `status` (select: active, paused) | many-to-one → Equipment | `completeMaintenance` |
| **RepairLog** | `issue` (text), `technician` (text), `duration` (number), `parts` (text), `cost` (number), `repairedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Equipment | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init equipment-maintenance
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Equipment, MaintenanceSchedule, and RepairLog types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: equipment-maintenance
   ✔ Equipment — 5 props, 2 links, 0 actions
   ✔ MaintenanceSchedule — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ RepairLog — 6 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Equipment --data '{"name": "Injection Molder #7", "type": "Injection Molding Machine", "location": "Plant A, Bay 3", "lastService": "2025-06-01", "status": "operational"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'equipment-maintenance': [
    {
      name: 'Equipment',
      displayName: 'Equipment',
      description: 'A piece of manufacturing equipment or machinery',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'location', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'lastService', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'operational', options: [
          { label: 'Operational', value: 'operational' },
          { label: 'Maintenance', value: 'maintenance' },
          { label: 'Offline', value: 'offline' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'maintenanceSchedules', targetObjectType: 'MaintenanceSchedule', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'repairLogs', targetObjectType: 'RepairLog', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'MaintenanceSchedule',
      displayName: 'Maintenance Schedule',
      description: 'A recurring preventive maintenance schedule for equipment',
      properties: [
        { name: 'frequency', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Daily', value: 'daily' },
          { label: 'Weekly', value: 'weekly' },
          { label: 'Monthly', value: 'monthly' },
          { label: 'Quarterly', value: 'quarterly' },
          { label: 'Annual', value: 'annual' },
        ]},
        { name: 'nextDue', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'active', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Paused', value: 'paused' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'equipment', targetObjectType: 'Equipment', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeMaintenance',
          displayName: 'Complete Maintenance',
          description: 'Record completion of a scheduled maintenance task',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'active' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'nextDue' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'RepairLog',
      displayName: 'Repair Log',
      description: 'A record of a repair performed on equipment',
      properties: [
        { name: 'issue', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'technician', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'duration', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'parts', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'cost', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'repairedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'equipment', targetObjectType: 'Equipment', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Preventive over reactive**: Scheduled maintenance with configurable frequencies shifts the plant from costly breakdowns to planned service windows.
- **Repair history**: A complete log of every repair, including parts used and time spent, enables pattern recognition for recurring failures.
- **Cost visibility**: Tracking repair costs and duration per machine helps justify equipment replacement decisions with hard data.
- **Machine-level profiles**: Linking schedules and repair logs to individual equipment creates a service history that follows each machine throughout its lifecycle.

# Production Tracking

## Persona

**Role**: Manufacturing software engineer at a food processing company running three shifts across two facilities.

Production managers track orders on whiteboards, batch completion times are logged in paper notebooks, and quality checks happen at the end of each batch with results filed in binders. The company needs real-time visibility into production progress, batch yields, and quality results to meet regulatory reporting requirements.

## Business Problem

Without digital tracking, production managers cannot answer basic questions: How many units of Product X were completed today? What is the yield rate for the current batch? Did the last quality check pass? Shift handoffs lose information, and regulatory auditors require manual compilation of batch records that takes days to assemble. This scenario builds a production tracking system that links orders to batches with real-time status updates and embeds quality checks directly into the batch workflow.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **ProductionOrder** | `product` (text), `quantity` (number), `priority` (select: standard, rush, critical), `dueDate` (date), `status` (select: planned, in-progress, completed, cancelled) | one-to-many → Batch | `startProduction` |
| **Batch** | `startTime` (date), `endTime` (date), `yield` (number), `targetQuantity` (number), `status` (select: running, completed, rejected) | many-to-one → ProductionOrder, one-to-many → QualityCheck | `completeBatch` |
| **QualityCheck** | `inspector` (text), `result` (select: pass, fail, conditional), `notes` (text), `checkedAt` (date) | many-to-one → Batch | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init production-tracking
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the ProductionOrder, Batch, and QualityCheck types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: production-tracking
   ✔ ProductionOrder — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Batch — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ QualityCheck — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create ProductionOrder --data '{"product": "Organic Granola 500g", "quantity": 5000, "priority": "standard", "dueDate": "2025-08-01", "status": "planned"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'production-tracking': [
    {
      name: 'ProductionOrder',
      displayName: 'Production Order',
      description: 'A manufacturing production order for a product',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'quantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'priority', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'standard', options: [
          { label: 'Standard', value: 'standard' },
          { label: 'Rush', value: 'rush' },
          { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
        ]},
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'planned', options: [
          { label: 'Planned', value: 'planned' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'batches', targetObjectType: 'Batch', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'startProduction',
          displayName: 'Start Production',
          description: 'Begin production on a planned order',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['product', 'quantity'], requiredStatus: 'planned' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'in-progress' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Batch',
      displayName: 'Batch',
      description: 'A production batch within a production order',
      properties: [
        { name: 'startTime', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'endTime', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'yield', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'targetQuantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'running', options: [
          { label: 'Running', value: 'running' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'productionOrder', targetObjectType: 'ProductionOrder', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'qualityChecks', targetObjectType: 'QualityCheck', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeBatch',
          displayName: 'Complete Batch',
          description: 'Mark a batch as completed with final yield numbers',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['yield'], requiredStatus: 'running' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'endTime' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'QualityCheck',
      displayName: 'Quality Check',
      description: 'A quality check performed on a production batch',
      properties: [
        { name: 'inspector', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'result', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Pass', value: 'pass' },
          { label: 'Fail', value: 'fail' },
          { label: 'Conditional', value: 'conditional' },
        ]},
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'checkedAt', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'batch', targetObjectType: 'Batch', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Order-to-batch hierarchy**: Production orders break down into trackable batches, giving managers real-time visibility into how much of an order is complete.
- **Yield tracking**: Recording actual yield against target quantity enables continuous improvement and early detection of production inefficiencies.
- **Embedded quality checks**: Quality results are linked directly to the batch they were performed on, creating the traceability required for regulatory audits.
- **Shift-proof handoffs**: Digital batch records persist across shifts, eliminating the information loss that occurs with paper-based tracking during handovers.

# Quality Control

## Persona

**Role**: Industrial software developer at a consumer electronics manufacturer with three production lines.

The quality assurance team records inspection results on clipboards, enters them into spreadsheets at end of shift, and emails defect reports to the engineering team. Corrective actions are tracked in a shared document with no accountability for completion. The company needs a real-time quality control system that connects inspections to defects and ensures corrective actions are followed through.

## Business Problem

Defect data arrives hours after problems occur, making it impossible to catch systemic issues before an entire batch is affected. When defects are found, corrective actions are assigned informally and often forgotten. There is no structured data linking a defect back to the specific inspection, production line, or inspector who found it. This scenario builds a quality control workflow that captures inspections in real time, logs defects with severity and location data, and tracks corrective actions to completion.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Inspection** | `product` (text), `line` (text), `inspector` (text), `date` (date), `result` (select: pass, fail, conditional), `status` (select: draft, submitted) | one-to-many → Defect | `submitInspection` |
| **Defect** | `type` (text), `severity` (select: minor, major, critical), `location` (text), `description` (text) | many-to-one → Inspection, one-to-many → CorrectiveAction | -- |
| **CorrectiveAction** | `action` (text), `assignedTo` (text), `dueDate` (date), `completedDate` (date), `status` (select: open, in-progress, completed, verified) | many-to-one → Defect | `completeAction` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init quality-control
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Inspection, Defect, and CorrectiveAction types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: quality-control
   ✔ Inspection — 6 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Defect — 4 props, 2 links, 0 actions
   ✔ CorrectiveAction — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Inspection --data '{"product": "Widget X-200", "line": "Line A", "inspector": "Tom Rivera", "date": "2025-07-10", "result": "fail", "status": "draft"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'quality-control': [
    {
      name: 'Inspection',
      displayName: 'Inspection',
      description: 'A quality inspection performed on a production line',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'line', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'inspector', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'result', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Pass', value: 'pass' },
          { label: 'Fail', value: 'fail' },
          { label: 'Conditional', value: 'conditional' },
        ]},
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'defects', targetObjectType: 'Defect', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitInspection',
          displayName: 'Submit Inspection',
          description: 'Finalize and submit an inspection report',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['product', 'line', 'result'], requiredStatus: 'draft' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'submitted' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Defect',
      displayName: 'Defect',
      description: 'A defect found during quality inspection',
      properties: [
        { name: 'type', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'severity', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Minor', value: 'minor' },
          { label: 'Major', value: 'major' },
          { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
        ]},
        { name: 'location', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'inspection', targetObjectType: 'Inspection', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'correctiveActions', targetObjectType: 'CorrectiveAction', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'CorrectiveAction',
      displayName: 'Corrective Action',
      description: 'An action taken to address a quality defect',
      properties: [
        { name: 'action', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'assignedTo', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'completedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'open', options: [
          { label: 'Open', value: 'open' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Verified', value: 'verified' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'defect', targetObjectType: 'Defect', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeAction',
          displayName: 'Complete Action',
          description: 'Mark a corrective action as completed',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'completedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Real-time defect capture**: Inspectors record findings immediately on the line instead of waiting for end-of-shift data entry, enabling faster response to quality issues.
- **Full traceability**: Every defect links back to the specific inspection, product, and production line where it was found, supporting root cause analysis.
- **Corrective action accountability**: Assigned actions have due dates and status tracking, ensuring quality issues are resolved rather than forgotten.
- **Severity-based prioritization**: Defect severity levels enable the quality team to focus on critical issues first and allocate resources appropriately.

# Supply Chain

## Persona

**Role**: Supply chain developer at a mid-size manufacturer sourcing raw materials from 40+ suppliers.

The procurement team manages supplier relationships through email, tracks purchase orders in spreadsheets, and verifies incoming deliveries against paper packing slips. Lead time data is anecdotal, quality ratings are informal, and there is no way to quickly evaluate which suppliers are reliable. The company needs a digital supply chain management system.

## Business Problem

Production stoppages due to late or low-quality deliveries cost the company significant revenue. Procurement decisions are based on relationships rather than data because supplier performance metrics are not tracked systematically. Purchase orders sent via email are difficult to reconcile against actual deliveries, and quality issues with received materials are not linked back to the supplier. This scenario builds a supply chain workflow that maintains supplier profiles with performance data, tracks purchase orders through fulfillment, and records delivery quality.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Supplier** | `name` (text), `materials` (text), `leadTime` (number), `qualityRating` (number), `contact` (text), `status` (select: active, probation, inactive) | one-to-many → PurchaseOrder | -- |
| **PurchaseOrder** | `items` (text), `total` (number), `orderDate` (date), `expectedDate` (date), `status` (select: draft, submitted, confirmed, delivered, cancelled) | many-to-one → Supplier, one-to-many → Delivery | `submitOrder` |
| **Delivery** | `receivedDate` (date), `quantity` (number), `qualityStatus` (select: accepted, partial, rejected), `notes` (text) | many-to-one → PurchaseOrder | `acceptDelivery` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init supply-chain
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Supplier, PurchaseOrder, and Delivery types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: supply-chain
   ✔ Supplier — 6 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ PurchaseOrder — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Delivery — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Supplier --data '{"name": "Pacific Steel Corp", "materials": "Cold-rolled steel coils", "leadTime": 14, "qualityRating": 4.5, "contact": "orders@pacificsteel.com", "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'supply-chain': [
    {
      name: 'Supplier',
      displayName: 'Supplier',
      description: 'A raw material or component supplier',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'materials', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'leadTime', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'qualityRating', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'contact', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'active', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Probation', value: 'probation' },
          { label: 'Inactive', value: 'inactive' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'purchaseOrders', targetObjectType: 'PurchaseOrder', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'PurchaseOrder',
      displayName: 'Purchase Order',
      description: 'A purchase order placed with a supplier',
      properties: [
        { name: 'items', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'total', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'orderDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'expectedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
          { label: 'Confirmed', value: 'confirmed' },
          { label: 'Delivered', value: 'delivered' },
          { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'supplier', targetObjectType: 'Supplier', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'deliveries', targetObjectType: 'Delivery', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitOrder',
          displayName: 'Submit Order',
          description: 'Submit a draft purchase order to the supplier',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['items', 'total', 'expectedDate'], requiredStatus: 'draft' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'submitted' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'orderDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Delivery',
      displayName: 'Delivery',
      description: 'A delivery received against a purchase order',
      properties: [
        { name: 'receivedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'quantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'qualityStatus', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Accepted', value: 'accepted' },
          { label: 'Partial', value: 'partial' },
          { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
        ]},
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'purchaseOrder', targetObjectType: 'PurchaseOrder', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'acceptDelivery',
          displayName: 'Accept Delivery',
          description: 'Record acceptance of a delivery and update quality status',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['quantity', 'qualityStatus'] },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'receivedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Data-driven procurement**: Supplier quality ratings and lead time tracking enable objective evaluation when choosing between vendors for new orders.
- **Order lifecycle visibility**: Purchase orders move through a structured status flow from draft to delivery, making it clear where every order stands.
- **Delivery quality tracking**: Recording quality status on each delivery creates a feedback loop that directly informs supplier ratings and future sourcing decisions.
- **Lead time accuracy**: Comparing expected delivery dates against actual received dates builds a real-world lead time dataset for better production planning.

# Beneficiary Tracking

## Persona

**Role**: Developer at a social services non-profit serving 2,000+ beneficiaries across multiple programs.

Case managers track beneficiary information in filing cabinets and spreadsheets. Service delivery is logged in daily reports that are never aggregated, and outcome data is compiled manually at grant reporting time. The organization needs a digital system to track beneficiaries from enrollment through service delivery to measurable outcomes.

## Business Problem

Funders increasingly require evidence of impact, but the organization cannot answer basic questions: How many beneficiaries were served last quarter? What services did a specific beneficiary receive? Are outcomes improving over time? Without structured data, grant reports are based on estimates rather than actual counts, and case managers have no visibility into a beneficiary's complete service history. This scenario builds a beneficiary tracking workflow that captures enrollment, logs every service interaction, and measures outcomes against defined targets.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Beneficiary** | `name` (text), `demographics` (text), `needs` (text), `enrollmentDate` (date), `status` (select: enrolled, active, graduated, inactive) | one-to-many → Service, one-to-many → Outcome | `activateBeneficiary` |
| **Service** | `type` (text), `provider` (text), `date` (date), `outcome` (text), `duration` (number) | many-to-one → Beneficiary | -- |
| **Outcome** | `metric` (text), `baseline` (number), `current` (number), `target` (number), `measuredDate` (date) | many-to-one → Beneficiary | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init beneficiary-tracking
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Beneficiary, Service, and Outcome types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: beneficiary-tracking
   ✔ Beneficiary — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Service — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Outcome — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Beneficiary --data '{"name": "Maria Santos", "demographics": "Age 34, single parent, two children", "needs": "Job training, childcare assistance", "enrollmentDate": "2025-05-01", "status": "enrolled"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'beneficiary-tracking': [
    {
      name: 'Beneficiary',
      displayName: 'Beneficiary',
      description: 'An individual enrolled in the organization programs',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'demographics', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'needs', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'enrollmentDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'enrolled', options: [
          { label: 'Enrolled', value: 'enrolled' },
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Graduated', value: 'graduated' },
          { label: 'Inactive', value: 'inactive' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'services', targetObjectType: 'Service', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'outcomes', targetObjectType: 'Outcome', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'activateBeneficiary',
          displayName: 'Activate Beneficiary',
          description: 'Move an enrolled beneficiary to active status after intake assessment',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['name', 'enrollmentDate'], requiredStatus: 'enrolled' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'active' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Service',
      displayName: 'Service',
      description: 'A service delivered to a beneficiary',
      properties: [
        { name: 'type', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'provider', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'outcome', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'duration', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'beneficiary', targetObjectType: 'Beneficiary', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Outcome',
      displayName: 'Outcome',
      description: 'A measurable outcome tracked for a beneficiary',
      properties: [
        { name: 'metric', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'baseline', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'current', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'target', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'measuredDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'beneficiary', targetObjectType: 'Beneficiary', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Complete beneficiary profiles**: Enrollment, demographics, and needs are captured in a single record, giving case managers a holistic view of each individual.
- **Service history**: Every service interaction is logged with date, provider, and duration, enabling accurate counts for grant reporting.
- **Outcome measurement**: Tracking baseline, current, and target values for each metric demonstrates progress and impact to funders with real data.
- **Enrollment lifecycle**: The structured status flow from enrolled through active to graduated tracks each beneficiary's journey through the program.

# Donor Management

## Persona

**Role**: Developer at a mid-size non-profit with 5,000+ donors and an annual fundraising goal of $2M.

The development team tracks donors in a legacy database, processes donations through a separate payment system, and manages campaigns in spreadsheets. Donor engagement history is fragmented, making it impossible to identify lapsed donors, calculate lifetime giving, or measure campaign effectiveness. The organization needs a unified donor management system.

## Business Problem

Donor retention is the lifeblood of sustainable fundraising, but the organization cannot identify which donors are at risk of lapsing because giving history is spread across multiple systems. Campaign performance is evaluated weeks after completion because donation data must be manually reconciled. Major gift officers lack a complete picture of a donor's history when preparing for cultivation meetings. This scenario builds a donor management workflow that maintains donor profiles with giving history, tracks individual donations linked to campaigns, and measures campaign performance in real time.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Donor** | `name` (text), `contact` (text), `totalGiving` (number), `firstGiftDate` (date), `status` (select: active, lapsed, major, prospect) | one-to-many → Donation | -- |
| **Donation** | `amount` (number), `campaign` (text), `date` (date), `method` (select: online, check, wire, in-kind), `acknowledged` (boolean) | many-to-one → Donor | `acknowledgeDonation` |
| **Campaign** | `name` (text), `goal` (number), `raised` (number), `startDate` (date), `endDate` (date), `status` (select: planning, active, completed) | -- | `launchCampaign` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init donor-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Donor, Donation, and Campaign types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: donor-management
   ✔ Donor — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Donation — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Campaign — 6 props, 0 links, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Donor --data '{"name": "Elizabeth Warren", "contact": "e.warren@email.com", "totalGiving": 15000, "firstGiftDate": "2020-12-15", "status": "major"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'donor-management': [
    {
      name: 'Donor',
      displayName: 'Donor',
      description: 'A donor or prospective donor to the organization',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'contact', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'totalGiving', type: 'number' as const, required: false, defaultValue: 0 },
        { name: 'firstGiftDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'prospect', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Lapsed', value: 'lapsed' },
          { label: 'Major', value: 'major' },
          { label: 'Prospect', value: 'prospect' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'donations', targetObjectType: 'Donation', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Donation',
      displayName: 'Donation',
      description: 'A gift received from a donor',
      properties: [
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'campaign', type: 'text' as const, required: false, indexed: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Online', value: 'online' },
          { label: 'Check', value: 'check' },
          { label: 'Wire', value: 'wire' },
          { label: 'In-Kind', value: 'in-kind' },
        ]},
        { name: 'acknowledged', type: 'boolean' as const, required: true, defaultValue: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'donor', targetObjectType: 'Donor', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'acknowledgeDonation',
          displayName: 'Acknowledge Donation',
          description: 'Mark a donation as acknowledged with a thank-you sent',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['amount', 'date'] },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'acknowledged', value: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Campaign',
      displayName: 'Campaign',
      description: 'A fundraising campaign with a defined goal and timeline',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'goal', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'raised', type: 'number' as const, required: false, defaultValue: 0 },
        { name: 'startDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'endDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'planning', options: [
          { label: 'Planning', value: 'planning' },
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'launchCampaign',
          displayName: 'Launch Campaign',
          description: 'Activate a campaign that is in the planning phase',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['name', 'goal', 'startDate', 'endDate'], requiredStatus: 'planning' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'active' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Lifetime giving visibility**: Donor profiles with total giving and first gift date enable segmentation by giving level and identification of lapsed donors.
- **Campaign performance tracking**: Linking donations to campaigns with goal and raised amounts provides real-time visibility into fundraising progress.
- **Acknowledgment workflow**: The `acknowledgeDonation` action ensures every gift receives a thank-you, a critical practice for donor retention.
- **Donor segmentation**: Status categories (active, lapsed, major, prospect) enable targeted outreach strategies for different donor populations.

# Grant Reporting

## Persona

**Role**: Grants management developer at a non-profit managing 25 active grants totaling $4M in annual funding.

The grants team tracks deliverables in individual spreadsheets per funder, stores compliance documentation in shared folders organized by grant name, and compiles reports manually before each deadline. When a funder changes reporting requirements, the team scrambles to adapt because there is no centralized view of what is owed, to whom, and by when.

## Business Problem

Missing a grant reporting deadline or failing a compliance check can result in funding clawbacks and damaged funder relationships. Each grant has unique milestones, reporting frequencies, and compliance requirements that are tracked in isolation. The grants team cannot see which milestones are coming due across all grants, and compliance evidence is scattered. This scenario builds a grant reporting workflow that tracks milestones with evidence, monitors compliance requirements, and provides a unified view of reporting obligations across all funders.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Grant** | `funder` (text), `amount` (number), `purpose` (text), `startDate` (date), `endDate` (date), `status` (select: pending, active, closed, suspended) | one-to-many → Milestone, one-to-many → ComplianceCheck | `activateGrant` |
| **Milestone** | `description` (text), `dueDate` (date), `evidence` (text), `status` (select: upcoming, in-progress, completed, overdue) | many-to-one → Grant | `completeMilestone` |
| **ComplianceCheck** | `requirement` (text), `notes` (text), `checkedDate` (date), `status` (select: compliant, non-compliant, pending-review) | many-to-one → Grant | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init grant-reporting
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Grant, Milestone, and ComplianceCheck types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: grant-reporting
   ✔ Grant — 6 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Milestone — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ ComplianceCheck — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Grant --data '{"funder": "Ford Foundation", "amount": 500000, "purpose": "Community health worker training program", "startDate": "2025-01-01", "endDate": "2027-12-31", "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'grant-reporting': [
    {
      name: 'Grant',
      displayName: 'Grant',
      description: 'A funding grant from a foundation or government entity',
      properties: [
        { name: 'funder', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'purpose', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'startDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'endDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Closed', value: 'closed' },
          { label: 'Suspended', value: 'suspended' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'milestones', targetObjectType: 'Milestone', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'complianceChecks', targetObjectType: 'ComplianceCheck', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'activateGrant',
          displayName: 'Activate Grant',
          description: 'Mark a pending grant as active after agreement execution',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['funder', 'amount', 'startDate', 'endDate'], requiredStatus: 'pending' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'active' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Milestone',
      displayName: 'Milestone',
      description: 'A deliverable or reporting milestone for a grant',
      properties: [
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'evidence', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'upcoming', options: [
          { label: 'Upcoming', value: 'upcoming' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Overdue', value: 'overdue' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'grant', targetObjectType: 'Grant', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeMilestone',
          displayName: 'Complete Milestone',
          description: 'Mark a milestone as completed with supporting evidence',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['evidence'], requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ComplianceCheck',
      displayName: 'Compliance Check',
      description: 'A compliance verification for a grant requirement',
      properties: [
        { name: 'requirement', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'checkedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending-review', options: [
          { label: 'Compliant', value: 'compliant' },
          { label: 'Non-Compliant', value: 'non-compliant' },
          { label: 'Pending Review', value: 'pending-review' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'grant', targetObjectType: 'Grant', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Cross-grant visibility**: All milestones across all grants are indexed by due date, providing a single view of upcoming deliverables regardless of funder.
- **Evidence-based completion**: Milestones require evidence documentation before they can be marked complete, ensuring the grants team has supporting materials ready for funder review.
- **Compliance monitoring**: Ongoing compliance checks are linked to their grant, making it easy to demonstrate adherence to funder requirements during audits.
- **Grant lifecycle management**: The structured status flow from pending through active to closed tracks each grant from award notification through closeout.

# Impact Measurement

## Persona

**Role**: Data systems developer at an education non-profit running 12 programs across four regions.

Program managers collect outcome data in spreadsheets that use different formats and definitions. Impact reports are assembled quarterly by a single analyst who spends weeks standardizing data before any analysis can begin. The board and funders want real-time dashboards, but the underlying data infrastructure does not support it.

## Business Problem

Every program defines and measures success differently. One program tracks graduation rates, another tracks employment placement, and a third tracks literacy scores -- all in incompatible formats. When the CEO needs to report aggregate impact to the board, the data team manually harmonizes metrics across programs. This scenario builds an impact measurement platform that defines programs with standardized metrics, collects indicator data at regular intervals, and produces structured reports that can feed dashboards and funder communications.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Program** | `name` (text), `description` (text), `budget` (number), `startDate` (date), `status` (select: planning, active, completed, suspended) | one-to-many → ImpactMetric, one-to-many → Report | -- |
| **ImpactMetric** | `indicator` (text), `target` (number), `actual` (number), `period` (text), `unit` (text) | many-to-one → Program | -- |
| **Report** | `period` (text), `narrative` (text), `status` (select: draft, review, published), `publishedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Program | `publishReport` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init impact-measurement
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Program, ImpactMetric, and Report types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: impact-measurement
   ✔ Program — 4 props, 2 links, 0 actions
   ✔ ImpactMetric — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Report — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Program --data '{"name": "Youth STEM Academy", "description": "After-school STEM education for grades 6-8", "budget": 150000, "startDate": "2025-01-15", "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'impact-measurement': [
    {
      name: 'Program',
      displayName: 'Program',
      description: 'A program operated by the organization',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'budget', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'startDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'planning', options: [
          { label: 'Planning', value: 'planning' },
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Suspended', value: 'suspended' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'impactMetrics', targetObjectType: 'ImpactMetric', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'reports', targetObjectType: 'Report', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ImpactMetric',
      displayName: 'Impact Metric',
      description: 'A quantitative impact measurement for a program',
      properties: [
        { name: 'indicator', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'target', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'actual', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'period', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'unit', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'program', targetObjectType: 'Program', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Report',
      displayName: 'Report',
      description: 'A periodic impact report for a program',
      properties: [
        { name: 'period', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'narrative', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'publishedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Review', value: 'review' },
          { label: 'Published', value: 'published' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'program', targetObjectType: 'Program', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'publishReport',
          displayName: 'Publish Report',
          description: 'Publish a reviewed impact report for stakeholder distribution',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['narrative'], requiredStatus: 'review' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'published' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'publishedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Standardized metrics**: A consistent structure for impact indicators across all programs eliminates the data harmonization bottleneck that delays reporting.
- **Target vs. actual tracking**: Every metric records both the target and actual values, making it immediately clear which programs are on track and which need attention.
- **Report lifecycle**: Impact reports move through draft, review, and published stages, ensuring quality control before stakeholder distribution.
- **Program-level aggregation**: Linking metrics and reports to programs enables both program-specific deep dives and organization-wide impact summaries.

# Volunteer Coordination

## Persona

**Role**: Developer at a community organization with 300+ active volunteers supporting events and programs year-round.

Volunteer signups happen through email and paper forms. Shift assignments are managed in a shared calendar that only coordinators can access, and hours are self-reported on paper timesheets that are transcribed monthly. The organization cannot tell how many volunteer hours were contributed last year or which volunteers are most active.

## Business Problem

Volunteer engagement suffers when people sign up but never hear back, or when they arrive at an event with no clear assignment. Hour tracking is unreliable because self-reported paper timesheets are often submitted weeks late with estimated hours. Funders and board members ask for volunteer hour totals that take days to compile. This scenario builds a volunteer coordination workflow that maintains volunteer profiles with skills and availability, schedules shifts for events, and logs verified hours.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Volunteer** | `name` (text), `skills` (text), `availability` (text), `totalHours` (number), `status` (select: active, on-leave, alumni) | one-to-many → HourLog | -- |
| **Shift** | `event` (text), `date` (date), `volunteersNeeded` (number), `description` (text), `status` (select: open, filled, completed, cancelled) | one-to-many → HourLog | `completeShift` |
| **HourLog** | `hours` (number), `supervisor` (text), `verified` (boolean), `notes` (text), `loggedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Volunteer, many-to-one → Shift | `verifyHours` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init volunteer-coordination
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Volunteer, Shift, and HourLog types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: volunteer-coordination
   ✔ Volunteer — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Shift — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ HourLog — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Volunteer --data '{"name": "Carlos Mendez", "skills": "Event setup, registration desk, first aid", "availability": "Weekends and evenings", "totalHours": 120, "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'volunteer-coordination': [
    {
      name: 'Volunteer',
      displayName: 'Volunteer',
      description: 'A registered volunteer with the organization',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'skills', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'availability', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'totalHours', type: 'number' as const, required: false, defaultValue: 0 },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'active', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'On Leave', value: 'on-leave' },
          { label: 'Alumni', value: 'alumni' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'hourLogs', targetObjectType: 'HourLog', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Shift',
      displayName: 'Shift',
      description: 'A scheduled volunteer shift for an event or program',
      properties: [
        { name: 'event', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'volunteersNeeded', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'open', options: [
          { label: 'Open', value: 'open' },
          { label: 'Filled', value: 'filled' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'hourLogs', targetObjectType: 'HourLog', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeShift',
          displayName: 'Complete Shift',
          description: 'Mark a shift as completed after the event',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'filled' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'HourLog',
      displayName: 'Hour Log',
      description: 'A record of hours worked by a volunteer during a shift',
      properties: [
        { name: 'hours', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'supervisor', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'verified', type: 'boolean' as const, required: true, defaultValue: false },
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'loggedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'volunteer', targetObjectType: 'Volunteer', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'shift', targetObjectType: 'Shift', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'verifyHours',
          displayName: 'Verify Hours',
          description: 'Supervisor verification of logged volunteer hours',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['hours', 'supervisor'] },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'verified', value: true },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Skills-based matching**: Volunteer profiles with skills and availability enable coordinators to match the right people to the right shifts.
- **Verified hour tracking**: Supervisor verification on hour logs replaces unreliable self-reported timesheets with accountable records.
- **Shift lifecycle management**: Shifts flow from open through filled to completed, giving coordinators visibility into staffing levels for upcoming events.
- **Aggregate reporting**: Linking hour logs to both volunteers and shifts enables reports by individual, event, or time period for funder and board reporting.

# Lease Management

## Persona

**Role**: Backend developer at a commercial real estate firm managing 300+ active lease agreements.

The firm needs a system to track lease terms, automate renewal reminders, and reconcile monthly rent payments. The current process relies on calendar reminders and manual bank statement matching, leading to missed renewals and late payment follow-ups.

## Business Problem

Commercial leases involve complex terms, escalation clauses, and renewal windows that span months. When renewal deadlines are missed, tenants default to month-to-month arrangements at unfavorable rates. Payment reconciliation against lease terms is entirely manual. This scenario builds a lease management workflow that tracks agreements, surfaces upcoming renewals, and links payments to their corresponding lease periods.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **LeaseAgreement** | `property` (text), `tenant` (text), `terms` (text), `startDate` (date), `endDate` (date), `monthlyRent` (number), `status` (select: draft, active, expired) | one-to-many → Renewal, one-to-many → Payment | `executeLease` |
| **Renewal** | `proposedTerms` (text), `proposedRent` (number), `status` (select: pending, accepted, declined), `dueDate` (date) | many-to-one → LeaseAgreement | `acceptRenewal` |
| **Payment** | `amount` (number), `dueDate` (date), `paidDate` (date), `status` (select: pending, paid, overdue, waived) | many-to-one → LeaseAgreement | `recordPayment` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init lease-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the LeaseAgreement, Renewal, and Payment types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: lease-management
   ✔ LeaseAgreement — 7 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Renewal — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ Payment — 4 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create LeaseAgreement --data '{"property": "Suite 400, 100 Main St", "tenant": "Acme Corp", "terms": "36-month NNN", "startDate": "2025-01-01", "endDate": "2027-12-31", "monthlyRent": 8500, "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'lease-management': [
    {
      name: 'LeaseAgreement',
      displayName: 'Lease Agreement',
      description: 'A commercial lease agreement between landlord and tenant',
      properties: [
        { name: 'property', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'tenant', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'terms', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'startDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'endDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'monthlyRent', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Expired', value: 'expired' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'renewals', targetObjectType: 'Renewal', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'payments', targetObjectType: 'Payment', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'executeLease',
          displayName: 'Execute Lease',
          description: 'Mark a draft lease as active after both parties sign',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['property', 'tenant', 'startDate', 'endDate'], requiredStatus: 'draft' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'active' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Renewal',
      displayName: 'Renewal',
      description: 'A proposed renewal for an existing lease agreement',
      properties: [
        { name: 'proposedTerms', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'proposedRent', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'Accepted', value: 'accepted' },
          { label: 'Declined', value: 'declined' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'leaseAgreement', targetObjectType: 'LeaseAgreement', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'acceptRenewal',
          displayName: 'Accept Renewal',
          description: 'Accept the proposed renewal terms',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'pending' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'accepted' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Payment',
      displayName: 'Payment',
      description: 'A rent payment linked to a lease agreement',
      properties: [
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'dueDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'paidDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'Paid', value: 'paid' },
          { label: 'Overdue', value: 'overdue' },
          { label: 'Waived', value: 'waived' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'leaseAgreement', targetObjectType: 'LeaseAgreement', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'recordPayment',
          displayName: 'Record Payment',
          description: 'Mark a payment as received',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'pending' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'paid' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'paidDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Renewal pipeline**: Linking renewals to lease agreements surfaces upcoming deadlines and prevents costly month-to-month rollovers.
- **Payment reconciliation**: Each payment is linked to its lease, enabling automated matching against expected rent amounts and due dates.
- **Structured transitions**: The `executeLease` and `acceptRenewal` actions enforce proper sequencing so agreements cannot be activated or renewed out of order.
- **Audit-ready records**: Timestamped payment records and status transitions create a clear audit trail for financial reporting.
