# Maintenance Requests

## Persona

**Role**: Software engineer at a property management company overseeing 50+ residential buildings.

The maintenance team currently tracks requests through a shared email inbox. Work orders are assigned by phone, and there is no systematic way to evaluate vendor performance. The team needs a structured system to capture tenant requests, dispatch work orders, and track vendor reliability.

## Business Problem

Maintenance requests get lost in email threads, tenants receive no status updates, and property managers lack data on response times and vendor quality. Emergency repairs compete with routine maintenance for attention without any priority system. This scenario builds a maintenance workflow that captures requests with priority levels, generates trackable work orders, and links vendors to their performance history.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **MaintenanceRequest** | `property` (text), `tenant` (text), `description` (text), `priority` (select: emergency, high, medium, low), `status` (select: open, assigned, completed) | one-to-many → WorkOrder | `assignRequest` |
| **WorkOrder** | `scheduledDate` (date), `completedDate` (date), `cost` (number), `status` (select: pending, in-progress, completed, cancelled) | many-to-one → MaintenanceRequest, many-to-one → Vendor | `completeWork` |
| **Vendor** | `name` (text), `specialty` (text), `rating` (number), `contact` (text), `hourlyRate` (number) | one-to-many → WorkOrder | -- |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init maintenance-requests
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the MaintenanceRequest, WorkOrder, and Vendor types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: maintenance-requests
   ✔ MaintenanceRequest — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action
   ✔ WorkOrder — 4 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Vendor — 5 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create MaintenanceRequest --data '{"property": "Building A, Unit 12", "tenant": "John Smith", "description": "Leaking kitchen faucet", "priority": "medium", "status": "open"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'maintenance-requests': [
    {
      name: 'MaintenanceRequest',
      displayName: 'Maintenance Request',
      description: 'A tenant-submitted maintenance request for a property',
      properties: [
        { name: 'property', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'tenant', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'priority', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Emergency', value: 'emergency' },
          { label: 'High', value: 'high' },
          { label: 'Medium', value: 'medium' },
          { label: 'Low', value: 'low' },
        ]},
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'open', options: [
          { label: 'Open', value: 'open' },
          { label: 'Assigned', value: 'assigned' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'workOrders', targetObjectType: 'WorkOrder', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'assignRequest',
          displayName: 'Assign Request',
          description: 'Assign a maintenance request to a vendor via work order',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'open' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'assigned' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'WorkOrder',
      displayName: 'Work Order',
      description: 'A dispatched work order assigned to a vendor',
      properties: [
        { name: 'scheduledDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'completedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'cost', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'request', targetObjectType: 'MaintenanceRequest', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'vendor', targetObjectType: 'Vendor', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'completeWork',
          displayName: 'Complete Work',
          description: 'Mark a work order as completed by the vendor',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'completed' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'completedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Vendor',
      displayName: 'Vendor',
      description: 'A maintenance vendor or contractor',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'specialty', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'rating', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'contact', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'hourlyRate', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'workOrders', targetObjectType: 'WorkOrder', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Priority-based triage**: Maintenance requests are categorized by severity, ensuring emergency issues are routed ahead of routine repairs.
- **Vendor accountability**: Linking work orders to vendors with ratings and cost tracking enables data-driven vendor selection over time.
- **End-to-end traceability**: Every request flows from tenant submission through assignment to completion, with timestamped status transitions at each step.
- **Cost visibility**: Recording costs on work orders gives property managers real-time insight into maintenance spend per building and vendor.

# Property Inspection

## Persona

**Role**: Developer at a facilities management company conducting 500+ inspections per year across commercial properties.

The inspection team uses paper checklists and photo uploads to shared drives. Reports are compiled manually in word processors, and tracking which issues were resolved requires cross-referencing emails. The company needs a digital inspection workflow that captures findings in real time and tracks issues to resolution.

## Business Problem

Paper-based inspections create a lag between finding issues and reporting them. Photos are disconnected from checklist items, historical inspection data is difficult to compare, and unresolved issues fall through the cracks between inspection cycles. This scenario builds an inspection platform where inspectors complete structured checklists on-site, attach photos to specific findings, and any issues discovered are tracked through to resolution.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Inspection** | `property` (text), `inspector` (text), `date` (date), `type` (select: annual, quarterly, move-in, move-out), `status` (select: scheduled, in-progress, completed) | one-to-many → ChecklistItem, one-to-many → Issue | `beginInspection` |
| **ChecklistItem** | `area` (text), `condition` (select: good, fair, poor, critical), `notes` (text), `photos` (file) | many-to-one → Inspection | -- |
| **Issue** | `description` (text), `severity` (select: minor, moderate, major, critical), `resolution` (text), `resolvedDate` (date), `status` (select: open, in-progress, resolved) | many-to-one → Inspection | `resolveIssue` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init property-inspection
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Inspection, ChecklistItem, and Issue types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: property-inspection
   ✔ Inspection — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ ChecklistItem — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Issue — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Inspection --data '{"property": "100 Commerce Blvd", "inspector": "Maria Garcia", "date": "2025-06-15", "type": "quarterly", "status": "scheduled"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'property-inspection': [
    {
      name: 'Inspection',
      displayName: 'Inspection',
      description: 'A scheduled property inspection event',
      properties: [
        { name: 'property', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'inspector', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Annual', value: 'annual' },
          { label: 'Quarterly', value: 'quarterly' },
          { label: 'Move-In', value: 'move-in' },
          { label: 'Move-Out', value: 'move-out' },
        ]},
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'scheduled', options: [
          { label: 'Scheduled', value: 'scheduled' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'checklistItems', targetObjectType: 'ChecklistItem', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const, cascadeDelete: true },
        { name: 'issues', targetObjectType: 'Issue', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'beginInspection',
          displayName: 'Begin Inspection',
          description: 'Mark a scheduled inspection as in progress',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'scheduled' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'in-progress' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ChecklistItem',
      displayName: 'Checklist Item',
      description: 'A single item on an inspection checklist',
      properties: [
        { name: 'area', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'condition', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Good', value: 'good' },
          { label: 'Fair', value: 'fair' },
          { label: 'Poor', value: 'poor' },
          { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
        ]},
        { name: 'notes', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'photos', type: 'file' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'inspection', targetObjectType: 'Inspection', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Issue',
      displayName: 'Issue',
      description: 'A problem found during inspection that requires resolution',
      properties: [
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'severity', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Minor', value: 'minor' },
          { label: 'Moderate', value: 'moderate' },
          { label: 'Major', value: 'major' },
          { label: 'Critical', value: 'critical' },
        ]},
        { name: 'resolution', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'resolvedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'open', options: [
          { label: 'Open', value: 'open' },
          { label: 'In Progress', value: 'in-progress' },
          { label: 'Resolved', value: 'resolved' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'inspection', targetObjectType: 'Inspection', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'resolveIssue',
          displayName: 'Resolve Issue',
          description: 'Mark an issue as resolved with a resolution description',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['resolution'], requiredStatus: 'in-progress' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'resolved' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'resolvedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Structured checklists**: Standardized condition ratings across areas make inspections consistent and comparable over time.
- **Photo documentation**: File attachments on checklist items link visual evidence directly to specific findings, eliminating loose photo folders.
- **Issue tracking to resolution**: Issues discovered during inspections are tracked through to completion with required resolution descriptions, preventing items from being forgotten.
- **Inspection history**: Linking checklist items and issues to inspections creates a full audit trail for each property over time.

# Property Management

## Persona

**Role**: Full-stack developer at a mid-size property management firm (200+ units across 15 buildings).

The development team is replacing a patchwork of spreadsheets and legacy desktop software with a centralized platform that handles property listings, tenant records, and lease lifecycle tracking. The system must support multi-building portfolios with per-property scoping for on-site managers.

## Business Problem

Property managers juggle tenant communications, unit availability, and lease renewals across multiple buildings with no single source of truth. Vacancy data lives in one spreadsheet, tenant contact information in another, and lease terms in PDF folders. This scenario builds a unified property management workflow where units, tenants, and leases are linked together, giving managers instant visibility into occupancy, upcoming renewals, and tenant history.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Property** | `address` (text), `type` (select: residential, commercial, mixed-use), `units` (number), `status` (select: active, inactive) | one-to-many → Tenant, one-to-many → Lease | -- |
| **Tenant** | `name` (text), `contact` (text), `leaseStart` (date), `unit` (text) | many-to-one → Property | -- |
| **Lease** | `property` (text), `tenant` (text), `rent` (number), `term` (number), `status` (select: active, expired, pending) | many-to-one → Property, many-to-one → Tenant | `activateLease` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init property-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Property, Tenant, and Lease types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: property-management
   ✔ Property — 4 props, 2 links, 0 actions
   ✔ Tenant — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Lease — 5 props, 2 links, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Property --data '{"address": "742 Evergreen Terrace", "type": "residential", "units": 24, "status": "active"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'property-management': [
    {
      name: 'Property',
      displayName: 'Property',
      description: 'A managed property in the portfolio',
      properties: [
        { name: 'address', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'type', type: 'select' as const, required: true, options: [
          { label: 'Residential', value: 'residential' },
          { label: 'Commercial', value: 'commercial' },
          { label: 'Mixed-Use', value: 'mixed-use' },
        ]},
        { name: 'units', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'active', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Inactive', value: 'inactive' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'tenants', targetObjectType: 'Tenant', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'leases', targetObjectType: 'Lease', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Tenant',
      displayName: 'Tenant',
      description: 'A tenant occupying a unit in a property',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'contact', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'leaseStart', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'unit', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'property', targetObjectType: 'Property', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Lease',
      displayName: 'Lease',
      description: 'A lease agreement between a tenant and property',
      properties: [
        { name: 'property', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'tenant', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'rent', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'term', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending', options: [
          { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
          { label: 'Expired', value: 'expired' },
          { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'property', targetObjectType: 'Property', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
        { name: 'tenant', targetObjectType: 'Tenant', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'activateLease',
          displayName: 'Activate Lease',
          description: 'Mark a pending lease as active after signing',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-staff',
          validationRules: { requiredStatus: 'pending' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'active' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Portfolio-wide visibility**: Linking properties, tenants, and leases provides a single view of occupancy, rent rolls, and upcoming renewals across all buildings.
- **Lease lifecycle management**: The `activateLease` action enforces a structured transition from pending to active, preventing premature occupancy.
- **Multi-building scoping**: Each property operates within the same tenant but is individually addressable, supporting on-site managers with property-level filtering.
- **Rapid onboarding**: New properties and tenants can be added via CLI or the application UI, with validation ensuring data consistency from day one.

# Real Estate CRM

## Persona

**Role**: Developer at a real estate brokerage with 30+ agents managing buyer and seller pipelines.

Agents currently track leads in personal spreadsheets, schedule showings via text messages, and manage offers through email chains. The brokerage has no visibility into pipeline health, showing activity, or conversion rates. They need a centralized CRM that flows from lead capture through showings to offer submission.

## Business Problem

Without a shared system, leads fall through the cracks when agents are busy, showing feedback is never recorded, and the brokerage cannot analyze which properties generate the most interest. Offer negotiations happen in email threads with no structured tracking of amounts, conditions, or counteroffers. This scenario builds a real estate CRM that captures leads with budget and preferences, links them to property showings with feedback, and tracks offers through negotiation to acceptance or rejection.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Lead** | `name` (text), `contact` (text), `budget` (number), `preferences` (text), `source` (text), `status` (select: new, contacted, qualified, closed) | one-to-many → Showing, one-to-many → Offer | `qualifyLead` |
| **Showing** | `property` (text), `date` (date), `feedback` (text), `interestLevel` (select: high, medium, low, none) | many-to-one → Lead | -- |
| **Offer** | `property` (text), `amount` (number), `conditions` (text), `status` (select: draft, submitted, countered, accepted, rejected), `submittedDate` (date) | many-to-one → Lead | `submitOffer` |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the project**

   ```bash
   eai init real-estate-crm
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define your Object Types**

   Create the Lead, Showing, and Offer types in `src/eai.config/object-types.ts` (see code example below).

4. **Validate the type definitions**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: real-estate-crm
   ✔ Lead — 6 props, 2 links, 1 action
   ✔ Showing — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions
   ✔ Offer — 5 props, 1 link, 1 action

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Seed types to the platform**

   ```bash
   eai types seed
   ```

6. **Create sample resources**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Lead --data '{"name": "Sarah Chen", "contact": "sarah@email.com", "budget": 450000, "preferences": "3BR, near downtown, garage", "source": "website", "status": "new"}'
   ```

7. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'real-estate-crm': [
    {
      name: 'Lead',
      displayName: 'Lead',
      description: 'A prospective buyer or renter in the pipeline',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'contact', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'budget', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'preferences', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'source', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'new', options: [
          { label: 'New', value: 'new' },
          { label: 'Contacted', value: 'contacted' },
          { label: 'Qualified', value: 'qualified' },
          { label: 'Closed', value: 'closed' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'showings', targetObjectType: 'Showing', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
        { name: 'offers', targetObjectType: 'Offer', cardinality: 'one-to-many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'qualifyLead',
          displayName: 'Qualify Lead',
          description: 'Mark a lead as qualified after initial contact and budget verification',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['name', 'contact', 'budget'], requiredStatus: 'contacted' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'qualified' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Showing',
      displayName: 'Showing',
      description: 'A property showing scheduled for a lead',
      properties: [
        { name: 'property', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'date', type: 'date' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'feedback', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'interestLevel', type: 'select' as const, required: false, options: [
          { label: 'High', value: 'high' },
          { label: 'Medium', value: 'medium' },
          { label: 'Low', value: 'low' },
          { label: 'None', value: 'none' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'lead', targetObjectType: 'Lead', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Offer',
      displayName: 'Offer',
      description: 'A purchase or rental offer submitted by a lead',
      properties: [
        { name: 'property', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'conditions', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'submittedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'draft', options: [
          { label: 'Draft', value: 'draft' },
          { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
          { label: 'Countered', value: 'countered' },
          { label: 'Accepted', value: 'accepted' },
          { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
        ]},
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'lead', targetObjectType: 'Lead', cardinality: 'many-to-one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        {
          name: 'submitOffer',
          displayName: 'Submit Offer',
          description: 'Submit a draft offer to the seller',
          requiredRole: 'tenant-user',
          validationRules: { requiredFields: ['property', 'amount'], requiredStatus: 'draft' },
          sideEffects: [
            { type: 'set_field', field: 'status', value: 'submitted' },
            { type: 'set_timestamp', field: 'submittedDate' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Full pipeline visibility**: Leads flow from initial capture through showings to offers, giving the brokerage a complete view of agent activity and conversion rates.
- **Showing feedback capture**: Recording interest levels on showings enables agents to prioritize follow-ups and helps the brokerage identify high-demand properties.
- **Offer lifecycle tracking**: Structured offer statuses replace email-based negotiation tracking, making it clear where each deal stands at any point.
- **Lead qualification gates**: The `qualifyLead` action requires budget verification before a lead can advance, ensuring agents focus on serious buyers.

# E-Commerce Returns

## Persona

**Role:** E-Commerce Operations Manager at an online fashion retailer.

You oversee the returns process for an online store that ships 50,000 orders per month. Return rates hover around 25 percent -- typical for fashion -- and each return involves a return request, a refund decision, and a restocking or disposal decision. The current process relies on a ticketing system that was not designed for returns, leading to delayed refunds and inconsistent restocking decisions.

## Business Problem

Customer service agents process returns manually, copying data between the ticketing system and the order management platform. Refund timelines vary from two to fourteen days because there is no structured workflow. Returned items sit in a staging area with no systematic process for evaluating condition and deciding whether to restock, refurbish, or dispose. You need:

- Structured return request intake linked to original orders.
- Refund processing with method tracking and timeline visibility.
- Restocking decisions that capture item condition and disposition.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **ReturnRequest** | order, items, reason, status | has one Refund, has many RestockItems | initiate, approve, reject |
| **Refund** | return, amount, method, processedDate | belongs to ReturnRequest | process, reverse |
| **RestockItem** | return, product, condition, action | belongs to ReturnRequest | inspect, restock, dispose |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init ecommerce-returns
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add ReturnRequest, Refund, and RestockItem to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: ecommerce-returns
   ✔ ReturnRequest — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ Refund — 4 props, 1 link, 2 actions
   ✔ RestockItem — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Create a return request**

   ```bash
   eai resources create ReturnRequest \
     --data '{"order": "ORD-78432", "items": "Blue Denim Jacket (M)", "reason": "wrong-size", "status": "pending"}'
   ```

6. **Process a refund**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Refund \
     --data '{"return": "ret-001", "amount": 89.99, "method": "original-payment", "processedDate": "2026-03-10"}'
   ```

7. **List pending returns**

   ```bash
   eai resources list ReturnRequest --filter 'status=pending'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'ecommerce-returns': [
    {
      name: 'ReturnRequest',
      displayName: 'Return Request',
      description: 'A customer request to return one or more items from an order',
      properties: [
        { name: 'order', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'items', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'reason', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Wrong Size', value: 'wrong-size' },
            { label: 'Defective', value: 'defective' },
            { label: 'Not as Described', value: 'not-as-described' },
            { label: 'Changed Mind', value: 'changed-mind' },
            { label: 'Arrived Late', value: 'arrived-late' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending',
          options: [
            { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
            { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
            { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
            { label: 'Received', value: 'received' },
            { label: 'Completed', value: 'completed' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'refund', target: 'Refund', cardinality: 'one' as const },
        { name: 'restockItems', target: 'RestockItem', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'initiate', displayName: 'Initiate Return' },
        { name: 'approve', displayName: 'Approve Return' },
        { name: 'reject', displayName: 'Reject Return' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Refund',
      displayName: 'Refund',
      description: 'A refund issued to a customer as part of a return request',
      properties: [
        { name: 'return', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'method', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Original Payment', value: 'original-payment' },
            { label: 'Store Credit', value: 'store-credit' },
            { label: 'Gift Card', value: 'gift-card' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'processedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'returnRequest', target: 'ReturnRequest', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'process', displayName: 'Process Refund' },
        { name: 'reverse', displayName: 'Reverse Refund' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'RestockItem',
      displayName: 'Restock Item',
      description: 'A returned product evaluated for restocking, refurbishment, or disposal',
      properties: [
        { name: 'return', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'condition', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'New', value: 'new' },
            { label: 'Like New', value: 'like-new' },
            { label: 'Worn', value: 'worn' },
            { label: 'Damaged', value: 'damaged' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'action', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Restock', value: 'restock' },
            { label: 'Refurbish', value: 'refurbish' },
            { label: 'Donate', value: 'donate' },
            { label: 'Dispose', value: 'dispose' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'returnRequest', target: 'ReturnRequest', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'inspect', displayName: 'Inspect Item' },
        { name: 'restock', displayName: 'Restock Item' },
        { name: 'dispose', displayName: 'Dispose Item' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Reason-categorized returns reveal product issues.** Structured return reasons enable merchandising teams to identify quality problems and listing inaccuracies at scale.
- **Refund method flexibility improves customer satisfaction.** Supporting multiple refund methods -- original payment, store credit, gift card -- lets agents choose the best option for each situation.
- **Condition-based restocking reduces inventory waste.** The RestockItem type captures the condition of each returned product, ensuring that disposition decisions are consistent and data-driven.
- **Order-linked returns close the loop.** Tying each ReturnRequest to an order ID enables end-to-end visibility from purchase to return to refund.

# Inventory Management

## Persona

**Role:** Supply Chain Analyst at a specialty retail company.

You manage inventory across 12 warehouse locations and 45 retail stores. Each location maintains independent stock levels, and reorder decisions are currently made by store managers using intuition rather than data. Stockouts on popular items cost sales, while overstocking on slow movers ties up capital. You need a centralized system that connects stock data, reorder logic, and supplier performance.

## Business Problem

Stock visibility is siloed by location. Store managers email the central warehouse when they run low, but there is no automated reorder trigger. Supplier lead times are tracked informally, and there is no systematic way to evaluate supplier performance. You need:

- Real-time stock tracking by product and location with reorder point thresholds.
- Automated reorder requests that route to the correct supplier.
- Supplier profiles with lead time and performance rating data.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **StockItem** | product, location, quantity, reorderPoint | has many ReorderRequests | update-quantity, set-reorder-point, flag-low-stock |
| **ReorderRequest** | item, quantity, supplier, status | belongs to StockItem, links to Supplier | create, approve, fulfill, cancel |
| **Supplier** | name, contact, leadTime, rating | has many ReorderRequests | onboard, update-rating, deactivate |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init inventory-management
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add StockItem, ReorderRequest, and Supplier to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: inventory-management
   ✔ StockItem — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ ReorderRequest — 4 props, 2 links, 4 actions
   ✔ Supplier — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Add a stock item**

   ```bash
   eai resources create StockItem \
     --data '{"product": "Organic Coffee Beans 1kg", "location": "Warehouse-Central", "quantity": 240, "reorderPoint": 50}'
   ```

6. **Create a reorder request**

   ```bash
   eai resources create ReorderRequest \
     --data '{"item": "stock-001", "quantity": 500, "supplier": "supplier-green-valley", "status": "pending"}'
   ```

7. **List low-stock items**

   ```bash
   eai resources list StockItem --filter 'quantity<50'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'inventory-management': [
    {
      name: 'StockItem',
      displayName: 'Stock Item',
      description: 'A product at a specific location with quantity and reorder threshold tracking',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'location', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'quantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'reorderPoint', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'reorderRequests', target: 'ReorderRequest', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'update-quantity', displayName: 'Update Quantity' },
        { name: 'set-reorder-point', displayName: 'Set Reorder Point' },
        { name: 'flag-low-stock', displayName: 'Flag Low Stock' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'ReorderRequest',
      displayName: 'Reorder Request',
      description: 'A request to replenish stock from a supplier for a specific item',
      properties: [
        { name: 'item', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'quantity', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'supplier', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending',
          options: [
            { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
            { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
            { label: 'Ordered', value: 'ordered' },
            { label: 'Fulfilled', value: 'fulfilled' },
            { label: 'Cancelled', value: 'cancelled' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'stockItem', target: 'StockItem', cardinality: 'one' as const },
        { name: 'supplier', target: 'Supplier', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'create', displayName: 'Create Request' },
        { name: 'approve', displayName: 'Approve Request' },
        { name: 'fulfill', displayName: 'Mark Fulfilled' },
        { name: 'cancel', displayName: 'Cancel Request' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Supplier',
      displayName: 'Supplier',
      description: 'A vendor that supplies products, tracked with lead time and performance data',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'contact', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'leadTime', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'rating', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'reorderRequests', target: 'ReorderRequest', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'onboard', displayName: 'Onboard Supplier' },
        { name: 'update-rating', displayName: 'Update Rating' },
        { name: 'deactivate', displayName: 'Deactivate Supplier' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Reorder point thresholds automate replenishment.** Each StockItem carries a reorderPoint, enabling automated low-stock detection and reorder request generation.
- **Supplier-linked reorder requests streamline procurement.** ReorderRequests reference both the StockItem and the Supplier, creating a clear path from stock need to vendor fulfillment.
- **Supplier performance tracking informs sourcing decisions.** The rating field on Suppliers provides data-driven input for contract renewals and vendor consolidation.
- **Location-level visibility eliminates guesswork.** Tracking stock by product and location enables analysts to identify imbalances and optimize distribution across the network.

# Loyalty Program

## Persona

**Role:** Loyalty Program Director at a regional retail chain.

You manage a customer rewards program across 80 stores. Members earn points on purchases, advance through tiers based on spending, and redeem points for discounts and exclusive products. The existing program runs on a legacy vendor platform with limited flexibility -- adding new reward types requires a multi-week vendor engagement.

## Business Problem

The legacy platform charges per-transaction fees that scale poorly, does not support custom tier rules, and provides limited visibility into member behavior. Marketing wants to launch seasonal promotions and partner rewards, but the vendor's configuration options are too rigid. You need:

- A flexible member registry with tier management and point balances.
- Transaction-level point tracking that supports multiple earning sources.
- A reward catalog with availability controls and dynamic point costs.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Member** | customer, tier, points, joinDate | has many PointTransactions | enroll, upgrade-tier, deactivate |
| **PointTransaction** | member, amount, source, description | belongs to Member | earn, redeem, adjust |
| **Reward** | name, pointsCost, category, availability | (standalone) | create, update-availability, retire |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init loyalty-program
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add Member, PointTransaction, and Reward to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: loyalty-program
   ✔ Member — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ PointTransaction — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ Reward — 4 props, 0 links, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Enroll a member**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Member \
     --data '{"customer": "maria.garcia@example.com", "tier": "silver", "points": 0, "joinDate": "2026-03-01"}'
   ```

6. **Record a point transaction**

   ```bash
   eai resources create PointTransaction \
     --data '{"member": "member-001", "amount": 150, "source": "purchase", "description": "In-store purchase at Downtown location"}'
   ```

7. **List available rewards**

   ```bash
   eai resources list Reward --filter 'availability=available'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'loyalty-program': [
    {
      name: 'Member',
      displayName: 'Member',
      description: 'A loyalty program member with a tier level and point balance',
      properties: [
        { name: 'customer', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'tier', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'bronze',
          options: [
            { label: 'Bronze', value: 'bronze' },
            { label: 'Silver', value: 'silver' },
            { label: 'Gold', value: 'gold' },
            { label: 'Platinum', value: 'platinum' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'points', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'joinDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'pointTransactions', target: 'PointTransaction', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'enroll', displayName: 'Enroll Member' },
        { name: 'upgrade-tier', displayName: 'Upgrade Tier' },
        { name: 'deactivate', displayName: 'Deactivate Member' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'PointTransaction',
      displayName: 'Point Transaction',
      description: 'A record of points earned, redeemed, or adjusted for a loyalty member',
      properties: [
        { name: 'member', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'amount', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'source', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Purchase', value: 'purchase' },
            { label: 'Promotion', value: 'promotion' },
            { label: 'Referral', value: 'referral' },
            { label: 'Redemption', value: 'redemption' },
            { label: 'Adjustment', value: 'adjustment' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'description', type: 'text' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'member', target: 'Member', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'earn', displayName: 'Earn Points' },
        { name: 'redeem', displayName: 'Redeem Points' },
        { name: 'adjust', displayName: 'Adjust Points' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Reward',
      displayName: 'Reward',
      description: 'A redeemable reward in the loyalty program catalog',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'pointsCost', type: 'number' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'category', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Discount', value: 'discount' },
            { label: 'Free Product', value: 'free-product' },
            { label: 'Experience', value: 'experience' },
            { label: 'Partner Offer', value: 'partner-offer' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'availability', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'available',
          options: [
            { label: 'Available', value: 'available' },
            { label: 'Limited', value: 'limited' },
            { label: 'Sold Out', value: 'sold-out' },
            { label: 'Retired', value: 'retired' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [],
      actions: [
        { name: 'create', displayName: 'Create Reward' },
        { name: 'update-availability', displayName: 'Update Availability' },
        { name: 'retire', displayName: 'Retire Reward' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Flexible tier management.** Member tiers are defined as select options, making it straightforward to add new tiers or adjust the tier structure without schema changes.
- **Multi-source point earning.** PointTransactions track the source of every point change, enabling marketing to measure which earning channels drive the most engagement.
- **Reward catalog independence.** Rewards are standalone objects with availability controls, allowing the marketing team to launch, limit, and retire rewards without affecting member records.
- **Full transaction history.** Every point earn, redeem, and adjustment is recorded, providing the audit trail needed for financial reconciliation and fraud detection.

# Product Compliance

## Persona

**Role:** Compliance Manager at a multi-national retail company.

You are responsible for ensuring that every product sold across multiple markets meets local regulatory standards. Your catalog includes thousands of SKUs, each requiring certifications that vary by market -- safety labels, environmental ratings, import approvals. Expired certifications mean products must be pulled from shelves, costing the business revenue and reputation.

## Business Problem

Certification tracking is spread across vendor-provided PDFs, internal spreadsheets, and email threads with testing labs. When a certification expires, the team often discovers it only after a regulatory audit. There is no centralized view of which products are compliant in which markets. You need:

- A product catalog enriched with market-specific compliance metadata.
- Certification tracking with expiry dates and renewal alerts.
- An audit log that records every compliance-related event for each product.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **Product** | name, sku, category, market | has many Certifications, has many AuditLogs | register, update-market, discontinue |
| **Certification** | product, standard, status, expiryDate | belongs to Product | issue, renew, revoke |
| **AuditLog** | product, event, user, timestamp | belongs to Product | (system-generated) |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init product-compliance
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add Product, Certification, and AuditLog to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: product-compliance
   ✔ Product — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ Certification — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions
   ✔ AuditLog — 4 props, 1 link, 0 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Register a product**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Product \
     --data '{"name": "EcoBlend Detergent", "sku": "ECO-DET-500", "category": "household", "market": "EU"}'
   ```

6. **Add a certification**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Certification \
     --data '{"product": "ECO-DET-500", "standard": "EU-Ecolabel", "status": "active", "expiryDate": "2027-06-30"}'
   ```

7. **List certifications expiring soon**

   ```bash
   eai resources list Certification --filter 'status=active'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'product-compliance': [
    {
      name: 'Product',
      displayName: 'Product',
      description: 'A retail product tracked for regulatory compliance across markets',
      properties: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'sku', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'category', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Household', value: 'household' },
            { label: 'Electronics', value: 'electronics' },
            { label: 'Food & Beverage', value: 'food-beverage' },
            { label: 'Apparel', value: 'apparel' },
            { label: 'Health & Beauty', value: 'health-beauty' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'market', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'US', value: 'US' },
            { label: 'EU', value: 'EU' },
            { label: 'UK', value: 'UK' },
            { label: 'APAC', value: 'APAC' },
          ],
        },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'certifications', target: 'Certification', cardinality: 'many' as const },
        { name: 'auditLogs', target: 'AuditLog', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'register', displayName: 'Register Product' },
        { name: 'update-market', displayName: 'Update Market' },
        { name: 'discontinue', displayName: 'Discontinue Product' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Certification',
      displayName: 'Certification',
      description: 'A regulatory certification issued for a product against a specific standard',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'standard', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'pending',
          options: [
            { label: 'Pending', value: 'pending' },
            { label: 'Active', value: 'active' },
            { label: 'Expired', value: 'expired' },
            { label: 'Revoked', value: 'revoked' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'expiryDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'product', target: 'Product', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'issue', displayName: 'Issue Certification' },
        { name: 'renew', displayName: 'Renew Certification' },
        { name: 'revoke', displayName: 'Revoke Certification' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'AuditLog',
      displayName: 'Audit Log',
      description: 'A system-generated record of compliance-related events for a product',
      properties: [
        { name: 'product', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'event', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'user', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'timestamp', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'product', target: 'Product', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Market-specific compliance tracking.** Each product is tied to a market, enabling compliance teams to filter by region and see exactly which certifications apply.
- **Expiry-driven renewal workflows.** The expiryDate on Certifications enables automated alerts so that renewals happen before products fall out of compliance.
- **Immutable audit history.** AuditLog entries have no actions, ensuring the compliance event history is tamper-resistant and audit-ready.
- **SKU-level granularity.** Indexed SKU fields allow fast lookups across large catalogs, connecting certification status directly to inventory and sales systems.

# Supplier Onboarding

## Persona

**Role:** Procurement Lead at a large retail group.

You manage the process of evaluating, onboarding, and monitoring suppliers across multiple product categories. Each year, your team processes over 200 vendor applications. Approved vendors sign contracts with specific terms, and their performance is reviewed quarterly. The current process involves PDF application forms, manual contract filing, and ad-hoc performance conversations.

## Business Problem

Vendor applications arrive as email attachments with no standardized format. Contract terms are stored in a shared drive with no link to the original application. Performance reviews happen informally, and there is no structured score that feeds back into contract renewal decisions. You need:

- A standardized vendor application pipeline with status tracking.
- Contract management linked to approved vendors with term visibility.
- Quarterly performance reviews that produce a score tied to contract renewals.

## Object Types

| Name | Key Properties | Links | Actions |
|------|---------------|-------|---------|
| **VendorApplication** | company, category, status, submittedDate | has one Contract | submit, review, approve, reject |
| **Contract** | vendor, terms, startDate, endDate | belongs to VendorApplication, has many PerformanceReviews | execute, amend, terminate |
| **PerformanceReview** | vendor, period, metrics, score | belongs to Contract | schedule, complete, flag-issue |

## CLI Workflow

1. **Scaffold the vertical**

   ```bash
   eai init supplier-onboarding
   ```

2. **Authenticate and pull environment**

   ```bash
   eai login
   eai env pull --include-secrets
   ```

3. **Define Object Types**

   Add VendorApplication, Contract, and PerformanceReview to `src/eai.config/object-types.ts`.

4. **Validate and seed**

   ```bash
   eai types validate
   eai types seed
   ```

   ```
   Tenant: supplier-onboarding
   ✔ VendorApplication — 4 props, 1 link, 4 actions
   ✔ Contract — 4 props, 2 links, 3 actions
   ✔ PerformanceReview — 4 props, 1 link, 3 actions

   ✔ All Object Types are valid
   ```

5. **Submit a vendor application**

   ```bash
   eai resources create VendorApplication \
     --data '{"company": "Artisan Foods Co.", "category": "food-beverage", "status": "submitted", "submittedDate": "2026-03-01"}'
   ```

6. **Create a contract**

   ```bash
   eai resources create Contract \
     --data '{"vendor": "artisan-foods", "terms": "Net 30, minimum order 500 units", "startDate": "2026-04-01", "endDate": "2027-03-31"}'
   ```

7. **List applications under review**

   ```bash
   eai resources list VendorApplication --filter 'status=under-review'
   ```

8. **Start local development**

   ```bash
   eai dev
   ```

## Code Example

```typescript
// src/eai.config/object-types.ts
export const objectTypes = {
  'supplier-onboarding': [
    {
      name: 'VendorApplication',
      displayName: 'Vendor Application',
      description: 'An application submitted by a company seeking to become an approved supplier',
      properties: [
        { name: 'company', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'category', type: 'select' as const, required: true,
          options: [
            { label: 'Food & Beverage', value: 'food-beverage' },
            { label: 'Apparel', value: 'apparel' },
            { label: 'Electronics', value: 'electronics' },
            { label: 'Home Goods', value: 'home-goods' },
            { label: 'Health & Beauty', value: 'health-beauty' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'status', type: 'select' as const, required: true, defaultValue: 'submitted',
          options: [
            { label: 'Submitted', value: 'submitted' },
            { label: 'Under Review', value: 'under-review' },
            { label: 'Approved', value: 'approved' },
            { label: 'Rejected', value: 'rejected' },
            { label: 'On Hold', value: 'on-hold' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'submittedDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'contract', target: 'Contract', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'submit', displayName: 'Submit Application' },
        { name: 'review', displayName: 'Begin Review' },
        { name: 'approve', displayName: 'Approve Vendor' },
        { name: 'reject', displayName: 'Reject Application' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'Contract',
      displayName: 'Contract',
      description: 'A supply agreement between the retail group and an approved vendor',
      properties: [
        { name: 'vendor', type: 'text' as const, required: true, indexed: true },
        { name: 'terms', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'startDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'endDate', type: 'date' as const, required: true },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'vendorApplication', target: 'VendorApplication', cardinality: 'one' as const },
        { name: 'performanceReviews', target: 'PerformanceReview', cardinality: 'many' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'execute', displayName: 'Execute Contract' },
        { name: 'amend', displayName: 'Amend Contract' },
        { name: 'terminate', displayName: 'Terminate Contract' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
    {
      name: 'PerformanceReview',
      displayName: 'Performance Review',
      description: 'A periodic evaluation of a vendor against quality, delivery, and service metrics',
      properties: [
        { name: 'vendor', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'period', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'metrics', type: 'text' as const, required: true },
        { name: 'score', type: 'number' as const, required: false },
      ],
      linkTypes: [
        { name: 'contract', target: 'Contract', cardinality: 'one' as const },
      ],
      actions: [
        { name: 'schedule', displayName: 'Schedule Review' },
        { name: 'complete', displayName: 'Complete Review' },
        { name: 'flag-issue', displayName: 'Flag Issue' },
      ],
      status: 'published' as const,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Key Takeaways

- **Standardized application pipeline reduces procurement friction.** Every vendor goes through the same structured intake, eliminating inconsistency from ad-hoc email submissions.
- **Contract-linked applications create an audit trail.** The link between VendorApplication and Contract ensures that every supply agreement traces back to a vetted and approved application.
- **Performance scores drive data-driven renewals.** Quarterly PerformanceReviews produce numeric scores that inform contract renewal, amendment, or termination decisions.
- **Category-based vendor segmentation.** Categorizing vendors by product type enables procurement leads to assess supplier diversity and identify gaps in the vendor portfolio.
